title.en: Volume 476 Biographies 263: Exemplary Officials 1: Bai Dengming with: Tang Jiaxiang, Ren Chendan, Yu Zongyao, Song Bida with: Lu Zaixin, Zhang Mu with: Zhang Xun, Chen Ruxian, Mou Sui with: Chen Shilin, Yao Wenxie with: Huang Zhenlin, Luo Zhonglin with: Cui Zongtai, Zu Jinchao, Zhao Jishi, Zhang Jin, Jiang Gao with: Zhang Keyi, Jia Pu, Shao Siyao with: Wei Liding, Gao Yinjue, Jin Rang, Cui Hua with: Zhou Zhonghong, Liu Qi, Tao Yuanchun, Liao Jiheng, Tong Guo Long, Lu Shi with: Gong Jian

sentences.zh: 清初以武功定天下，日不暇給。

translations.literal: In the early Qing, martial prowess secured the realm under Heaven, and there was no leisure even by day.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qing the dynasty won the empire by force of arms, and the court scarcely had a moment to breathe.

sentences.zh: 世祖親政，始課吏治，詔嚴舉劾，樹之風聲。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor personally took power, he first made officials conduct a matter of assessment, issued edicts strictly requiring impeachment and commendation, and established a model of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Shunzhi Emperor assumed personal rule, he began to hold officials accountable, ordered strict impeachment and reward, and set a tone across the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 聖祖平定三籓之後，與民休息，拔擢廉吏，如于成龍、彭鵬、陳璸、郭琇、趙申喬、陳鵬年等，皆由縣令洊厯部院封疆，治理蒸蒸，於斯為盛。

translations.literal: After the Sage Ancestor pacified the Three Feudatories, he gave the people rest, promoted incorrupt officials such as Yu Chenglong, Peng Peng, Chen Bin, Guo Xiu, Zhao Shenqiao, and Chen Pengnian, all of whom rose from county magistrate through repeated appointments in ministries, courts, and frontier posts; governance flourished, and at that time it reached its height.
translations.idiomatic: After the Kangxi Emperor put down the Three Feudatories, he let the people recover and elevated honest officials—Yu Chenglong, Peng Peng, Chen Bin, Guo Xiu, Zhao Shenqiao, Chen Pengnian, and others—who had all risen from county magistracies through the ministries and provincial governments; administration thrived as never before.

sentences.zh: 世宗綜覈名實，人知奉法。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor examined names against realities comprehensively, and people knew to obey the law.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor scrutinized performance against claims, and officials learned to heed the law.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初政，循而勿失。

translations.literal: In the early reign of Qianlong, he followed this course and did not let it slip.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qianlong reign the court carried on the same path without deviation.

sentences.zh: 國家豐亨豫大之休，蓋數十年吏治修明之效也。

translations.literal: The state enjoyed the blessings of abundance and ease; this was largely the effect of decades of well-ordered officialdom.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty prosperity and security owed much to decades of sound administration.

sentences.zh: 及後權相用事，政以賄成，蠹國病民，亂萌以作。

translations.literal: Later a powerful minister held sway; government was accomplished through bribes, the state was harmed and the people afflicted, and the seeds of disorder sprouted.
translations.idiomatic: Later a dominant chief minister took power, office was bought, the treasury and populace suffered, and unrest began to stir.

sentences.zh: 仁宗矯之，冀滌瑕穢。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong corrected this, hoping to wash away stains and filth.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaqing Emperor tried to correct it, hoping to cleanse corruption.

sentences.zh: 道、咸以來，軍事興而吏治疏。

translations.literal: From the Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns onward, military affairs arose while official discipline grew lax.
translations.idiomatic: From the Daoguang and Xianfeng eras on, war multiplied while bureaucratic standards slackened.

sentences.zh: 同治中興，疆吏賢者猶能激揚清濁，以彌縫其間。

translations.literal: In the Tongzhi restoration, able frontier governors could still stir clear and turbid waters to patch the gaps between them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongzhi revival, capable provincial governors could still rouse the honest and restrain the corrupt to hold things together.

sentences.zh: 然保舉冒濫，捐例大開，猥雜不易爬梳。

translations.literal: Yet recommendations were recklessly abused, purchase offices were widely opened, and the mixed mass was not easy to sort through.
translations.idiomatic: Yet patronage was abused, sale of offices flourished, and the ranks became an intractable tangle.

sentences.zh: 末造財政紊亂，新令繁興，簿書期會，救過之不遑。

translations.literal: In the final phase finances were chaotic, new orders proliferated, ledgers and deadlines piled up, and there was no leisure to remedy past faults.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty closing years revenue was in disorder, regulations multiplied, and clerks raced deadlines with no time to fix what had already gone wrong.

sentences.zh: 又遷調不時，雖有潔己愛民者，亦不易自舉其職。

translations.literal: Transfers were also untimely; even those who kept themselves pure and loved the people found it hard to fulfill their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Frequent reshuffling meant that even upright, caring magistrates could scarcely do their jobs properly.

sentences.zh: 論者謂有清一代，治民寬而治吏嚴，其敝也奉行故事，實政不修，吏道媮而民生益蹙。

translations.literal: Commentators say that through the Qing as a whole the people were governed leniently but officials strictly; the abuse was clinging to precedent, not carrying out real policy, the way of officials grew slack and the people lives grew more strained.
translations.idiomatic: Observers hold that the Qing governed the populace lightly but officials harshly; the flaw was ritual adherence without real reform—officialdom slackened while commoners bore ever heavier burdens.

sentences.zh: 迨紀綱漸隳，康、雍澄清之治，邈焉不可見。

translations.literal: When discipline gradually collapsed, the clarifying rule of Kangxi and Yongzheng was far beyond sight.
translations.idiomatic: As standards eroded, the clear governance of the Kangxi and Yongzheng eras vanished from view.

sentences.zh: 觀此，誠得失之林也。

translations.literal: Viewing this, it is truly a forest of gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, the chapter is a thicket of lessons in success and failure.

sentences.zh: 明史所載，以官至監司為限，今從之。

translations.literal: What the History of Ming records is limited to those who reached the rank of surveillance commissioner; the present work follows this.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming History includes officials only up to the rank of surveillance commissioner; this volume does the same.

sentences.zh: 尤以親民為重，其非由守令起家者不與焉。

translations.literal: It especially values closeness to the people; those who did not rise from prefectural and county magistracies are not included.
translations.idiomatic: Proximity to the people counts most; those who did not begin as prefects or magistrates are omitted.

sentences.zh: 白登明，字林九，奉天蓋平人，隸漢軍鑲白旗。

translations.literal: Bai Dengming, style Linjiu, was a native of Gaiping in Fengtian, registered in the Han military Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Dengming, courtesy name Linjiu, came from Gaiping in Fengtian and belonged to the Han Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治二年拔貢，五年，授河南柘城知縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he was selected as a tribute student; in the fifth year he was appointed magistrate of Zhecheng in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a tribute scholar in Shunzhi 2, he was appointed magistrate of Zhecheng, Henan, in Shunzhi 5.

sentences.zh: 時大兵之後，所在萑苻嘯聚。

translations.literal: At that time, after the great armies had passed, bandits gathered and roared everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the wake of the wars, brigands were rallying throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 登明治尚嚴肅，擒諸盜魁按以法，境內晏然。

translations.literal: Dengming valued stern severity in governance; he seized the chiefs of the bandits and dealt with them according to law, and within his jurisdiction all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Dengming governed with strict discipline, arrested the bandit leaders and punished them by law, and the district grew calm.

sentences.zh: 憫遺黎荒殘，多方招撫，停止增派河夫，設條以勸耕讀。

translations.literal: He pitied the surviving people in their desolation and ruin, recruited and comforted them in many ways, stopped extra levies of river laborers, and set regulations to encourage farming and study.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying the war-ravaged populace, he worked to bring them back, halted additional corvée for river work, and issued rules to promote agriculture and schooling.

sentences.zh: 十年，考最，擢江南太倉知州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year his evaluation ranked highest and he was promoted to prefect of Taicang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten he topped the performance review and was promoted to prefect of Taicang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 釐賦稅，除耗羨，雪諸冤獄，訪察利弊，所摘發輒中。

translations.literal: He rectified tax levies, removed surcharges, cleared wrongful cases, investigated advantages and abuses, and what he exposed always hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: He reformed taxation, abolished illegal surcharges, righted wrongful convictions, and investigated local abuses—his findings invariably proved correct.

sentences.zh: 鄰境有冤抑，赴愬上官，輒原下州為理。

translations.literal: When neighboring districts had grievances of injustice, people went to appeal to superiors, who always sent the case back to his prefecture for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Wronged parties from neighboring jurisdictions appealed to higher authorities, who routinely referred their cases to him for adjudication.

sentences.zh: 海濱居民因亂盪析，登明召民開墾，復成聚落。

translations.literal: Coastal inhabitants had been scattered by turmoil; Dengming summoned the people to open land for cultivation and settlements were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal communities shattered by war were brought back as he called people to reclaim farmland and villages reformed.

sentences.zh: 是年九月，海寇犯劉河堡，登明盡力守禦，寇不得逞，遂退。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year sea bandits attacked Liuhe Fort; Dengming defended with all his strength, the raiders could not prevail, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That September pirates struck Liuhe Fort; Dengming mounted a full defense, the enemy failed to break through, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 十六年，海寇破鎮江，由江寧敗走，急攻崇明。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year sea bandits took Zhenjiang, were defeated fleeing through Jiangning, and pressed an urgent attack on Chongming.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen the pirates seized Zhenjiang, were beaten back from Jiangning, and turned to storm Chongming.

sentences.zh: 巡撫蔣國柱治兵策應，欲遣告師期，莫敢前。

translations.literal: Governor Jiang Guozhu prepared troops to respond and wished to send word of the army schedule, but no one dared go forward.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Jiang Guozhu mobilized troops and needed a messenger to report the army schedule, yet no one would go.

sentences.zh: 登明獨駕一艘夜半往，絙城入，眾知援至，守益力，寇乃遁。

translations.literal: Dengming alone took one boat at midnight, was hauled over the wall by rope, the garrison knew relief had come and defended more fiercely, and the bandits fled.
translations.idiomatic: Dengming sailed alone at midnight, was pulled over the wall by rope; once the defenders knew help had arrived they fought harder and the pirates withdrew.

sentences.zh: 劉河北支有硃涇者，宋范仲淹新塘遺跡也，久淤塞。

translations.literal: On a northern branch of the Liu River was Zhujing, a relic of Fan Zhongyan Xintang of the Song, long silted up.
translations.idiomatic: A northern tributary of the Liu River, Zhujing, was a Song-era work associated with Fan Zhongyan and had long been choked with silt.

sentences.zh: 登明請於上官，疏鑿五十里。

translations.literal: Dengming petitioned his superiors and dredged and opened fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned his superiors and had fifty li of the channel dredged open.

sentences.zh: 巡按李森先知其能，復令大開劉河六十里，於是震澤在北諸水悉導入海，旱潦有備，為一郡利。

translations.literal: Censor Li Senxian knew his ability and again ordered a major opening of the Liu River for sixty li; then the waters north of Lake Tai all led to the sea, drought and flood were provided against, and it became a benefit to the whole prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Senxian, knowing his capacity, ordered another sixty li of the Liu River cleared; waters north of Lake Tai were channeled to the sea, drought and flood were both managed, and the whole prefecture benefited.

sentences.zh: 先是寇急時，需餉無出，以雲南協餉應之，卒為大吏所劾落職。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the bandits pressed urgently, funds were needed with no source; he used Yunnan cooperative pay to meet it and in the end was impeached by a high official and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: During the crisis he had no funds for supplies and drew on Yunnan cooperative pay; he was eventually impeached by a senior official and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 州民列治狀請留，弗得，坐廢二十餘年。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture listed his record of governance and asked that he stay, but could not; he sat idle for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural residents petitioned with accounts of his good rule asking him to remain, but failed; he remained out of office for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年，會台灣用兵，福建總督姚啟聖、巡撫吳興祚素知登明，代為入貲，疏薦，起授高郵知州。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kangxi, when Taiwan was under military campaign, Fujian Governor-General Yao Qisheng and Governor Wu Xingzuo, who had long known Dengming, paid his quota for him, memorialized recommending him, and he was raised and appointed prefect of Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18, during the Taiwan campaign, Governor-General Yao Qisheng and Governor Wu Xingzuo, who knew him well, paid his required contribution and recommended him; he was recalled as prefect of Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 值歲旱蝗，繼而大水，湖漲。

translations.literal: The year saw drought and locusts, followed by great floods and the lake rising.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought drought and locusts, then severe flooding as the lake swelled.

sentences.zh: 決清水潭，築堤御之。

translations.literal: He breached Qing Shui Pond and built dikes to hold the water back.
translations.idiomatic: He opened Qing Shui Pond and built dikes to contain the flood.

sentences.zh: 嚴禁胥吏克減，役者踴躍從事。

translations.literal: He strictly forbade clerks from skimming and cutting; laborers eagerly took part in the work.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade clerks from skimming funds, and corvée laborers worked with enthusiasm.

sentences.zh: 次年復災，再請蠲賑，勸富民分食，全活無算。

translations.literal: The next year disaster struck again; he again requested remission and relief, urged wealthy households to share food, and countless lives were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster returned the following year; he again sought tax relief and famine aid, urged the wealthy to share food, and saved innumerable lives.

sentences.zh: 時三籓初平，軍檄猶繁。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Feudatories had just been pacified and military dispatches were still numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Feudatories had only just been subdued, and military requisitions were still heavy.

sentences.zh: 登明與民約，凡供億驛夫，聞吹笳而至，免奪民時。

translations.literal: Dengming made a pact with the people: for all provision of relay labor, when the horn was blown they would come, sparing seizure of the people's time.
translations.idiomatic: Dengming agreed with the people that whenever relay service was needed, they would come at the sound of the horn so farming time would not be wasted.

sentences.zh: 上官有所徵調，不輕給，然皆諒其清廉，亦無相督過者。

translations.literal: When superiors made requisitions he did not lightly comply, yet all understood his integrity and none pressed him for faults.
translations.idiomatic: He did not readily meet every demand from above, but superiors knew his honesty and did not press him.

sentences.zh: 以積勞卒官，貧無餘貲，州人醵金以殮。

translations.literal: He died in office from accumulated labor, poor without surplus funds; the people of the prefecture pooled money for his burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office from overwork, leaving no wealth; the prefectural people pooled funds for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 入祀名宦祠，鄉民多肖像立祠私祀焉。

translations.literal: He was entered in the shrine of eminent officials; many country people set up portrait halls and private shrines to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the hall of distinguished officials, and many villagers erected portrait temples to honor him privately.

sentences.zh: 時江南以良吏稱者，湯家相、任辰旦、于宗堯，皆與登明相先後云。

translations.literal: At that time in Jiangnan those famed as good officials were Tang Jiaxiang, Ren Chendan, and Yu Zongyao, all in succession with Dengming, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan at the time Tang Jiaxiang, Ren Chendan, and Yu Zongyao were also praised as model magistrates, serving in the same era as Dengming.

sentences.zh: 家相，字泰瞻，山西趙城人。

translations.literal: Jiaxiang, style Taizhan, was a native of Zhaocheng in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jiaxiang, courtesy name Taizhan, was from Zhaocheng in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Shunzhi 6.

sentences.zh: 八年，授常熟知縣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed magistrate of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he was appointed magistrate of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 潔己愛民，釐剔耗蠹，撫卹凋殘，善政具舉。

translations.literal: He kept himself pure and loved the people, rectified waste and corruption, comforted the devastated, and good policies were all carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He lived frugally and cared for the people, rooted out waste and graft, aided the war-shattered, and put every good measure into practice.

sentences.zh: 前令被劾逮問，家相左右之，力白其誣，以是忤巡按御史。

translations.literal: The previous magistrate was impeached and arrested for questioning; Jiaxiang assisted him and strongly declared his innocence, thereby offending the touring censor.
translations.idiomatic: When his predecessor was impeached and arrested, Jiaxiang supported him and vigorously proved his innocence, which offended the touring censor.

sentences.zh: 時江南逋賦數百萬，嚴旨奪各官職，家相坐免。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangnan had millions in arrears of tax; a stern edict stripped all officials of rank, and Jiaxiang was dismissed on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan owed millions in back taxes; an imperial order stripped officials of rank, and Jiaxiang was removed with the rest.

sentences.zh: 士民爭先輸納，不逾宿而額足，且以治狀訴大吏，請留，勿獲。

translations.literal: Scholars and commoners vied to pay first; within a night the quota was met, and they also appealed to high officials with his record of governance asking that he stay, but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners rushed to pay taxes; the quota was met overnight, and they petitioned senior officials with accounts of his rule asking him to remain—but in vain.

sentences.zh: 既而給事中周之桂疏上其事，十三年，起授湖北南漳縣。

translations.literal: Later Supervising Secretary Zhou Zhigui memorialized the matter; in the thirteenth year he was raised and appointed to Nanzhang County in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Later Censor Zhou Zhigui memorialized on his behalf; in year thirteen he was recalled as magistrate of Nanzhang in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 縣居萬山中，寇盜窟穴，時出肆掠，戕官，人咸危之。

translations.literal: The county lay among myriad mountains; bandits had their dens and often came out to plunder wantonly, killing officials, and all regarded it as perilous.
translations.idiomatic: The county sat deep in the mountains where bandits nested, raided at will, and had killed officials; everyone considered the post dangerous.

sentences.zh: 家相下車，即令堅壁清野。

translations.literal: As soon as Jiaxiang took office he ordered fortified walls and cleared fields.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Jiaxiang immediately ordered walls strengthened and the countryside cleared.

sentences.zh: 寇大至，家相謂同城守備曰：「寇眾我寡，當效羅士信破盧明月法，可勝。」

translations.literal: When the bandits came in force, Jiaxiang said to the garrison commander of the same city: "The bandits are many and we few; we should follow the method by which Luo Shixin defeated Lu Mingyue, and we can win."
translations.idiomatic: When a large bandit force arrived, Jiaxiang told the local garrison commander: "They outnumber us; we should use the tactic Luo Shixin used against Lu Mingyue—and we can win."

sentences.zh: 密授方略，寇果墮伏中，遂擒其魁黨馬成、孫信輩，斬首數百級。

translations.literal: He secretly gave the plan; the bandits indeed fell into the ambush, and they then seized the chiefs Ma Cheng, Sun Xin, and their ilk, beheading several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out the plan in secret; the bandits fell into the ambush, and his men captured leaders Ma Cheng, Sun Xin, and their followers, taking several hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 寇大創，遠遁。

translations.literal: The bandits were greatly wounded and fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits suffered a crushing blow and fled deep into the hills.

sentences.zh: 於是招流亡，修學校，教養兼施，墾田六百餘頃。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recruited exiles, repaired schools, applied both teaching and nurturing, and opened more than six hundred qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He then recalled exiles, restored schools, combined education with relief, and reclaimed more than six hundred qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 築永泉、八觀諸堰，民賴其力，邑以大治。

translations.literal: He built the Yongquan, Baguan, and other weirs; the people relied on his labor and the district was greatly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Yongquan, Baguan, and other irrigation works; the people benefited, and the county flourished.

sentences.zh: 疆吏交章薦之，以病乞歸。

translations.literal: Frontier officials submitted joint memorials recommending him; he requested retirement on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials repeatedly recommended him; he retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 辰旦，字千之，浙江蕭山人。

translations.literal: Chendan, style Qianzhi, was a native of Xiaoshan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Chendan, courtesy name Qianzhi, was from Xiaoshan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治十三年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the thirteenth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in Shunzhi 13.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，授上海知縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign he was appointed magistrate of Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 清苦自勵，敏於聽斷，數決疑獄，豪猾斂跡。

translations.literal: He disciplined himself in austerity, was quick in hearing cases, repeatedly decided doubtful lawsuits, and the powerful and cunning drew in their steps.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly and pushed himself hard, judged cases swiftly, resolved knotty lawsuits, and local bullies fell silent.

sentences.zh: 催科以時，不大用鞭樸，百姓感其仁，輸納恐後。

translations.literal: He collected taxes on schedule, did not greatly use the whip, the people were moved by his benevolence, and paid taxes fearing to be last.
translations.idiomatic: He collected taxes on time, rarely used the lash, and the people, grateful for his kindness, paid early for fear of being late.

sentences.zh: 瀕海防軍將撤，密請行期，故邀軍主歡飲，宣言期須少緩，次日令下，促急行。

translations.literal: Coastal defense troops were about to be withdrawn; he secretly requested the march date, then deliberately invited the commander to a feast and announced the date would be slightly delayed; the next day the order came down urging rapid departure.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal garrisons were to be withdrawn; he secretly learned the departure date, then entertained the commander and announced a slight delay—whereupon the next day orders came to march at once.

sentences.zh: 乃厚其牛酒，道上勞軍，軍無敢遷延他顧，居民帖然。

translations.literal: He then generously supplied oxen and wine, entertained the army along the road, the troops dared not linger or look elsewhere, and the residents were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He lavishly supplied provisions and entertained the troops along the route so they would not linger or plunder; the populace remained undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 黃龍浦為吳淞江入海要口，建閘屢圮。

translations.literal: Huanglong Ford was the vital mouth where the Wusong River enters the sea; sluice gates built there repeatedly collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Huanglong Ford, where the Wusong River meets the sea, was a critical point; sluices built there repeatedly failed.

sentences.zh: 故事，修閘必築壩，費不貲。

translations.literal: By precedent, repairing the sluice required building a dam, at immeasurable expense.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, repairing the sluice meant building a cofferdam, at enormous cost.

sentences.zh: 辰旦仿浙人為梁法，度基廣狹，約丈尺伐石，識其甲乙，下之水，使善泅者厝之，悉中程。

translations.literal: Chendan imitated the Zhejiang method of beam construction, measured the breadth and narrowness of the foundation, estimated feet and inches for cutting stone, marked them in sequence, lowered them into the water, and had skilled swimmers place them—all fitting the measure.
translations.idiomatic: Chendan adopted the Zhejiang beam method, measured the foundation, cut stones to size, marked each piece, lowered them into the water, and had expert swimmers set them in place—all fitting precisely.

sentences.zh: 复廣左右護堤，約水就道，十閱月而工成。

translations.literal: He also widened the protective dikes on left and right, guided the water into its channel, and in ten months the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: He widened the flanking dikes, channeled the water properly, and finished the project in ten months.

sentences.zh: 不病役，不糜帑，邑人頌之。

translations.literal: Corvée was not overburdened, the treasury was not wasted, and the people of the district praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Labor was not overtaxed, public funds were not squandered, and the county sang his praises.

sentences.zh: 縣田沒水者六千畝，賦額未除，輸者率破家。

translations.literal: Six thousand mu of county fields were submerged; the tax quota was not reduced, and those who paid generally ruined their families.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand mu of county land lay underwater, yet the tax quota stood unchanged, and families were ruined paying it.

sentences.zh: 前令屢勘虛實貿亂，至是巡撫慕天顏疏請復勘。

translations.literal: Previous magistrates had repeatedly surveyed real and false conditions in confusion; at this time Governor Mu Tianyan memorialized requesting a new survey.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier magistrates surveys had muddled fact and fiction; Governor Mu Tianyan now memorialized for a fresh inspection.

sentences.zh: 辰旦喜曰：「是吾志也。」

translations.literal: Chendan said with joy: "This is my aim."
translations.idiomatic: Chendan said gladly: "This is what I have long wished for."

sentences.zh: 日往來泥沙中，按舊冊履丈，釐其荒者，閱二月，費皆自辦，俸不足，出銀釧棉布償之。

translations.literal: Day after day he went back and forth in mud and sand, followed old registers pacing and measuring, sorted out the wasteland, and in two months all expenses were self-provided; when salary was insufficient he sold silver bracelets and cotton cloth to cover them.
translations.idiomatic: He waded daily through mud and silt, measured fields against old registers, and sorted out wasteland; within two months he paid all costs himself, selling his silver bracelets and cotton cloth when his salary fell short.

sentences.zh: 籍上，得減除額徵有差。

translations.literal: When the register was submitted, the levied quota was reduced by varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: His report led to a proportional reduction in the tax quota.

sentences.zh: 十八年，舉博學鴻儒，放還故官。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was recommended as a Broad Learning and Eminent Scholar and was released to return to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen he was nominated for the special Broad Learning examination and returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 復以良吏薦，入為給事中，論事切直，改大理寺丞。

translations.literal: Again recommended as a good official, he entered office as supervising secretary, spoke on affairs sharply and directly, and was transferred to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended again as an exemplary magistrate, he became a supervising secretary, spoke bluntly on policy, and was transferred to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He retired to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 旋以前廷推事詿誤落職，卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon after, because of an error in a prior court nomination he was dismissed and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed over a prior court nomination error and died at home.

sentences.zh: 宗堯，字二巍，漢軍正白旗人，廣西總督時曜子。

translations.literal: Zongyao, style Erwei, was a Han military Plain White Banner man, son of Guangxi Governor-General Shi Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zongyao, courtesy name Erwei, belonged to the Han Plain White Banner and was the son of Guangxi Governor-General Shi Yao.

sentences.zh: 以廕入監讀書。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he entered the Imperial Academy to study.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial Academy by hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，授常熟知縣，年甫十九。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Changshu, aged only nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 7 he was appointed magistrate of Changshu at the age of nineteen.

sentences.zh: 興利除弊，勇於為治，老於吏事者勿逮也。

translations.literal: He promoted benefit and removed abuses, was bold in governance, and veterans of official affairs could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted public good and cut abuses, governed boldly, and outshone officials with decades of experience.

sentences.zh: 時漕政積弊，糧皆民運，往往破家。

translations.literal: At that time grain transport had accumulated abuses; grain was all transported by the people, and families were often ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Grain transport was riddled with abuses; civilians bore the hauling and families were often bankrupted.

sentences.zh: 宗堯議定官收官兌之法，重困得甦。

translations.literal: Zongyao proposed fixing the method of official receipt and official exchange of grain, and heavy distress was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyao instituted official collection and government exchange of grain, easing the crushing burden.

sentences.zh: 其徵糧則戒期令各自輸，胥吏莫由上下其手，民便之。

translations.literal: In collecting grain he set deadlines ordering each to pay separately, so clerks had no means to manipulate above and below, and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: For tax collection he set deadlines for direct payment so clerks could not skim, to the people's relief.

sentences.zh: 興文教，戢豪強，救荒療疫，皆以誠懇肫摯出之，四年如一日。

translations.literal: He promoted culture and education, restrained the powerful, relieved famine and treated pestilence—all with sincere earnestness from the heart, four years like one day.
translations.idiomatic: He fostered learning, curbed local bullies, and fought famine and plague with wholehearted sincerity, unwavering through four years.

sentences.zh: 以勞致疾，卒於官，年二十有三耳。

translations.literal: From overwork he fell ill and died in office, aged only twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Overwork brought on illness; he died in office at twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 民為罷市，醵金發喪，遂葬之虞山南麓，題其阡曰「萬民留葬」。

translations.literal: The people closed the markets for him, pooled money for the funeral, and buried him at the southern foot of Mount Yu, inscribing his grave path "Buried by the Ten Thousand People Who Asked Him to Stay."
translations.idiomatic: The people shut the markets in mourning, pooled funds for his funeral, and buried him at the southern foot of Mount Yu with the epitaph "Buried Where the People Begged Him to Remain."

sentences.zh: 宋必達，字其在，湖北黃州人。

translations.literal: Song Bida, style Qizai, was a native of Huangzhou in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Song Bida, courtesy name Qizai, was from Huangzhou in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 順治八年進士，授江西寧都知縣。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the eighth year of Shunzhi and was appointed magistrate of Ningdu in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Shunzhi 8, he was appointed magistrate of Ningdu in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 土瘠民貧，清泰、懷德二鄉久罹寇，民多遷徙，地不治。

translations.literal: The soil was poor and the people impoverished; Qingtai and Huaide townships had long suffered bandits, many people had migrated, and the land was uncultivated.
translations.idiomatic: The land was barren and the people poor; Qingtai and Huaide had long been ravaged by bandits, many had fled, and fields lay fallow.

sentences.zh: 請盡蠲逋賦以徠之，二歲田盡闢。

translations.literal: He requested complete remission of arrears to draw them back; in two years all fields were opened.
translations.idiomatic: He sought full remission of back taxes to bring people home; within two years every field was under cultivation again.

sentences.zh: 縣治瀕河，夏雨暴漲，城且沒。

translations.literal: The county seat bordered the river; summer rains swelled violently and the city was about to be submerged.
translations.idiomatic: The county seat lay on the river; summer floods surged and the city was nearly swallowed.

sentences.zh: 禱於神，水落，按故道疏治之，自是無水患。

translations.literal: He prayed to the spirits; the water fell, and following the old channel he dredged and repaired it; from then on there was no flood disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He prayed to the gods; the waters receded, and he dredged the old channel—after which the county knew no more floods.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，耿精忠叛，自福建出攻掠旁近地，江西大震，群賊響應。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, Geng Jingzhong rebelled, sallying forth from Fujian to attack and plunder nearby lands; Jiangxi was greatly shaken, and bandits rose in response everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: In 1674, Geng Jingzhong rose in rebellion and marched out of Fujian to raid the surrounding country. Jiangxi was thrown into alarm, and brigands answered his call on every side.

sentences.zh: 寧都故有南、北二城，南民北兵。

translations.literal: Ningdu formerly had southern and northern cities; southerners were civilians and northerners were soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Ningdu had long been divided into a southern city and a northern city — civilians in the south, garrison troops in the north.

sentences.zh: 必達曰：「古有保甲、義勇、弓弩社，民皆可兵也。

translations.literal: Bidá said: "In antiquity there were baojia systems, voluntary militias, and crossbow societies — the people could all be soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Bidá said, "In old times there were baojia systems, volunteer militias, and crossbow clubs — every man among the people could be made a fighter.

sentences.zh: 王守仁破宸濠嘗用之矣。」

translations.literal: When Wang Shouren defeated Zhu Chenhao, he had once used this method."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren had employed just such a measure when he crushed the rebellion of Zhu Chenhao."

sentences.zh: 如其法訓練，得義勇二千。

translations.literal: Following his method he trained them, and obtained two thousand volunteer soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled the men by that method and raised two thousand volunteers.

sentences.zh: 及賊前鋒薄城下，營將邀必達議事，曰：「眾寡食乏，奈何？」

translations.literal: When the bandits' vanguard pressed close beneath the walls, the garrison commander invited Bidá to discuss affairs, saying: "Our numbers are few and food is scarce — what are we to do?"
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel vanguard reached the foot of the walls, the garrison commander summoned Bidá for counsel. "We are outnumbered and short of provisions," he said. "What now?"

sentences.zh: 必達曰：「人臣之義，有死無二。

translations.literal: Bidá said: "The duty of a subject is to die without a second thought.
translations.idiomatic: Bidá replied, "A loyal minister's duty admits only one choice: to stand and die.

sentences.zh: 賊本烏合，掩其始至，可一鼓破也。」

translations.literal: The bandits are at bottom a rabble in union; if we strike them just as they arrive, they can be broken in a single drumbeat."
translations.idiomatic: These rebels are nothing but a mob. Catch them at first arrival and one charge will scatter them."

sentences.zh: 營將遂率所部進，賊少卻，必達以義勇橫擊之，賊奔。

translations.literal: The garrison commander then led his troops forward; the bandits retreated somewhat, and Bidá struck them across with the volunteers, and the bandits fled.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander led his men out; the rebels gave ground. Bidá hit them on the flank with his volunteers, and they broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 已而復率眾來攻，巨砲隳雉堞，輒壘補其缺，隨方備禦益堅。

translations.literal: Before long they again led their masses to attack; great cannon destroyed the parapets, and he immediately piled up earth to repair the gaps, preparing defenses on every side with growing firmness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they returned in force. Heavy guns shattered the battlements; each breach he patched with earthen ramparts, and the city's defenses grew tighter with every assault.

sentences.zh: 會援至，賊解去。

translations.literal: When reinforcements arrived, the bandits lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Relief finally came, and the rebels drew off.

sentences.zh: 或言於巡撫，縣堡砦多從賊，巡撫將發兵，必達刺血上書爭之，乃止。

translations.literal: Someone spoke to the provincial governor, saying that many county forts and stockades had followed the bandits; the governor was about to dispatch troops, but Bidá wrote a memorial in his own blood to argue against it, and the plan was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached the governor that many local forts had gone over to the rebels. As troops were about to be sent against them, Bidá submitted a memorial written in his own blood, and the punitive expedition was called off.

sentences.zh: 官軍有自汀州還者，婦女在軍中悲號聲相屬，自傾橐計口贖之，詢其姓氏里居，護之歸。

translations.literal: There were government troops returning from Tingzhou; women in the army camp wailed in succession. He emptied his purse and ransomed them by head count, inquired their surnames and native places, and escorted them home.
translations.idiomatic: When government troops returned from Tingzhou with captive women whose cries filled the camp, he emptied his own purse to redeem them, learned each woman's name and home village, and saw every one safely back.

sentences.zh: 縣初食淮鹽，自明王守仁治贛，改食粵鹽，其後苦銷引之累，必達請以粵額增淮額，商民皆便。

translations.literal: The county had originally consumed Huai salt; since the Ming when Wang Shouren governed Ganzhou, it was changed to consume Yue salt; afterward it suffered the burden of unsold salt tickets. Bidá requested that Yue quotas be added to Huai quotas, and merchants and the people were all benefited.
translations.idiomatic: The county had once drawn its salt from the Huai region; under Wang Shouren's governorship of Ganzhou in the Ming it was switched to Guangdong salt, and later merchants groaned under the quotas they could not sell. Bidá petitioned to merge Guangdong allotments with the Huai quota, to the great relief of traders and townspeople alike.

sentences.zh: 卒以粵引不中額，被論罷職，寧都人哭而送之，餞貽皆不受，間道赴南昌，中途為賊所得，脅降不屈，系旬有七日。

translations.literal: In the end, because Yue salt tickets did not meet the quota, he was impeached and dismissed from office. The people of Ningdu wept as they saw him off; gifts of farewell he accepted none. He took bypaths toward Nanchang, and midway was seized by bandits; they forced him to submit but he would not yield, and he was imprisoned for ten-odd days.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually dismissed for failing to meet the Guangdong salt quota. The people of Ningdu wept at his departure; he refused every parting gift. Taking back roads toward Nanchang, he was captured by rebels and held for more than ten days; they demanded his surrender, and he would not bend.

sentences.zh: 忽夜半有數十人持兵踰垣入，曰：「宋爺安在？

translations.literal: Suddenly at midnight several dozen men bearing arms climbed the wall and entered, saying: "Where is Master Song?
translations.idiomatic: One night, dozens of armed men scaled the wall and burst in. "Where is Master Song?

sentences.zh: 吾等皆寧都民。」

translations.literal: We are all people of Ningdu."
translations.idiomatic: We are all men of Ningdu."

sentences.zh: 擁而出，乃得脫。

translations.literal: They escorted him out, and he thus obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: They hustled him out, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 既歸里，江西總督董衛國移鎮湖廣，見之，歎曰：「是死守孤城者耶？

translations.literal: After he returned home, Dong Weiguo, governor-general of Jiangxi, was transferred to garrison Huguang; meeting him, he sighed and said: "Is this the one who held a lone city to the death?
translations.idiomatic: Back home, he was met by Dong Weiguo, lately transferred from Jiangxi to Huguang, who exclaimed, "Can this be the man who defended a besieged city unto death?

sentences.zh: 吾為若諮部還故職，且以軍功敘。」

translations.literal: I will consult the ministry on your behalf to restore your former office, and moreover reward you for military merit."
translations.idiomatic: I shall petition the ministry to restore your post and see you rewarded for your service in arms."

sentences.zh: 必達遜謝之。

translations.literal: Bidá modestly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Bidá demurred with thanks.

sentences.zh: 既而語人曰：「故吏如棄婦，忍自媒乎？」

translations.literal: Afterward he said to others: "A dismissed official is like a cast-off wife — how could one bear to go seeking a match for oneself?"
translations.idiomatic: Later he told others, "A disgraced official is like a discarded wife — would anyone stoop to hawking herself anew?"

sentences.zh: 褐衣蔬食，老於田間，寧都人歲時祀之。

translations.literal: He wore coarse cloth and ate simple vegetables, growing old among the fields; the people of Ningdu worshipped him at the seasonal festivals.
translations.idiomatic: He lived out his days in coarse dress and plain fare, working the fields; the people of Ningdu honored him with offerings year after year.

sentences.zh: 越數年，滇寇韓大任由吉安竄入寧都境，後令萬蹶生踵必達鄉勇之制御之，卒保其城云。

translations.literal: After several years, the Yunnan bandit Han Daren fled from Ji'an into Ningdu territory; later the magistrate Wan Juesheng followed Bidá's method of village militias to control them, and in the end preserved the city — so it is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, the Yunnan rebel Han Daren broke from Ji'an into Ningdu. Magistrate Wan Juesheng revived Bidá's militia system and held the walls — so the account runs.

sentences.zh: 陸在新，字文蔚，江南長洲人。

translations.literal: Lu Zaixin, courtesy name Wenwei, was a native of Changzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zaixin, styled Wenwei, came from Changzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，以策論取士，在新夙講經濟，遂得舉，除松江府學教授，教諸生以質行為先，其以金贄者卻之，用不足，知府魯某分俸助之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kangxi, by policy essays officials were selected; Zaixin had long studied statecraft, and so obtained appointment, receiving the post of professor at the Songjiang prefectural school. He taught students with integrity as the first priority; those who offered gold gifts he refused. When funds were insufficient, Prefect Lu so-and-so shared his salary to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1666, Zaixin passed the examination in policy essays. Long versed in statecraft, he was appointed professor at the Songjiang prefectural academy, where he put moral seriousness before book learning, turned away every gift of gold, and, when funds ran short, was subsidized from Prefect Lu's own salary.

sentences.zh: 巡撫湯斌察其廉勤，以卓異薦。

translations.literal: The governor Tang Bin observed his integrity and diligence, and recommended him as exceptionally outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Tang Bin noted his probity and tireless service and nominated him for exceptional merit.

sentences.zh: 是歲江南七府一州諸長吏被薦者獨在新一人，時以此服斌之知人。

translations.literal: That year among all the chief officials of seven prefectures and one department in Jiangnan who were recommended, Zaixin alone was the one; at the time people admired Bin for knowing men because of this.
translations.idiomatic: That year he alone among senior officials across Jiangnan's seven prefectures and one autonomous department received such nomination — and men said Tang Bin truly knew talent.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擢江西廬陵知縣，嚴重有威，境內貼然。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to magistrate of Luling in Jiangxi; solemn and dignified with authority, within his jurisdiction all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: In 1686 he was elevated to magistrate of Luling in Jiangxi. Grave in bearing and firm in authority, he kept the district utterly quiet.

sentences.zh: 誓不以一錢自污，錢穀耗羨，革除都盡。

translations.literal: He vowed not to soil himself with a single coin; surcharges on taxes and grain he abolished entirely.
translations.idiomatic: He swore never to accept a copper coin in bribes and abolished every fee and surcharge on tax and grain payments.

sentences.zh: 傍水設五倉，便民輸納。

translations.literal: By the water he established five granaries to facilitate the people's payment of taxes.
translations.idiomatic: He set up five riverside granaries so people could pay their taxes with ease.

sentences.zh: 建問苦亭於衙西，訪求民隱。

translations.literal: He built an "Inquiry into Hardships" pavilion west of the yamen to seek out the people's hidden grievances.
translations.idiomatic: West of the yamen he built a pavilion for hearing grievances, where hidden troubles of the people could be brought to light.

sentences.zh: 時裹糧歷山谷間，勞苦百姓，軫其災患而導之於善。

translations.literal: At times he carried provisions himself and traveled through valleys and mountains, sharing in the people's toil, sympathizing with their disasters and misfortunes and guiding them toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Often he shouldered his own rations and walked the hill country, laboring alongside the common people, mourning their hardships and leading them toward better ways.

sentences.zh: 召諸生，考德論藝，如為校官時。

translations.literal: He summoned the students, examining virtue and discussing learning, as when he had been a school officer.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the scholars to sessions on virtue and letters, just as he had done when teaching at the academy.

sentences.zh: 設四門義學，刻孝經、小學頒行之。

translations.literal: He established free schools at the four city gates, engraved the Classic of Filial Piety and the Elementary Learning and distributed them for circulation.
translations.idiomatic: He opened charity schools at all four gates, had the Classic of Filial Piety and the Elementary Learning printed and distributed among the people.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，江溢，民多溺。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the river overflowed, and many among the people drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In 1687 the river burst its banks and countless people were drowned.

sentences.zh: 在新急出錢募民船往救，躬自倡率，出入洪濤中，全活無算。

translations.literal: Zaixin urgently put forth money to recruit civilian boats to go rescue them; he personally took the lead, going in and out among the raging floods, saving innumerable lives.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixin spent his own money to hire boats and led the rescue himself, plunging again and again into the flood until untold numbers were saved.

sentences.zh: 以受前官虧帑盈萬無所抵，憂卒。

translations.literal: Because he inherited from a predecessor a treasury deficit of more than ten thousand with no means to make it good, he died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited a treasury shortfall of more than ten thousand taels from his predecessor with no way to cover it, and died of despair.

sentences.zh: 初赴官時，子孔奐在京師，蹙然曰：「吾父此行，必殉是官矣。」

translations.literal: When he first went to take office, his son Kong Huan was in the capital and said with a frown: "On this journey my father will surely die for this office."
translations.idiomatic: When he first set out for his post, his son Kong Huan, in the capital, said bleakly, "My father is going to die for that magistracy."

sentences.zh: 亟從之。

translations.literal: He hurried after him.
translations.idiomatic: The son raced to join him.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，鬻書數篋以斂。

translations.literal: On the day of his death, several cases of books were sold to pay for his burial.
translations.idiomatic: At his death, a few chests of books were sold to pay for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 廬陵人為罷市三日，請祀名宦祠，長洲人亦以鄉賢祀之。

translations.literal: The people of Luling closed the markets for three days; they requested his worship in the shrine of eminent officials, and the people of Changzhou also honored him in the shrine of worthy natives.
translations.idiomatic: Luling shut its markets for three days in mourning. He was enshrined among distinguished officials, and his home county of Changzhou added him to the roll of local worthies.

sentences.zh: 張沐，字仲誠，河南上蔡人。

translations.literal: Zhang Mu, courtesy name Zhongcheng, was a native of Shangcai in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mu, styled Zhongcheng, was from Shangcai in Henan.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fifteenth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in 1658.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，授直隸內黃知縣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Neihuang in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In 1662 he was appointed magistrate of Neihuang in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 縣苦賦役不均，沐令田主自首，不丈而清。

translations.literal: The county suffered from unequal distribution of taxes and corvée; Mu ordered landholders to report themselves, and without measuring, the registers were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The county groaned under unfair levies. Mu had landowners declare their holdings openly; without a single survey, the tax rolls were set right.

sentences.zh: 嚴行十家牌法，姦宄斂跡。

translations.literal: He strictly enforced the ten-household registration system; villains and evildoers withdrew from sight.
translations.idiomatic: He rigorously enforced the ten-household mutual-responsibility system, and wrongdoers vanished from the streets.

sentences.zh: 大旱，自八月不雨至明年九月，民飢甚。

translations.literal: Great drought: from the eighth month no rain fell until the ninth month of the following year; the people starved greatly.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought ran from the eighth month through the following September without rain, and the people faced famine.

sentences.zh: 沐力籌賑，捐貲為倡，勸富民貸粟，官為書其數，俟秋穫取償，人爭應之，民免轉徙。

translations.literal: Mu exerted himself to organize relief, donating funds as the first example, urging the wealthy to lend grain; the government recorded the amounts, to be repaid after the autumn harvest; people competed to respond, and the people were spared displacement.
translations.idiomatic: Mu organized famine relief, pledging his own money and urging rich households to lend grain on the government's ledger for repayment at harvest. The response was eager, and the people were spared from wandering away in search of food.

sentences.zh: 沐為政務德化，令民各書「為善最樂」四字於門以自警。

translations.literal: Mu in governing emphasized moral transformation; he ordered each household to write the four characters "Doing good is the greatest joy" on their door as self-admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Mu governed through moral persuasion and had every household post the motto "There is no joy greater than doing good" above its door as a daily reminder.

sentences.zh: 著六諭敷言，俾人各誦習，反覆譬喻，雖婦孺聞之，莫不欣欣鄉善。

translations.literal: He composed Expositions on the Six Edicts, causing people each to recite and study them; repeating comparisons and illustrations, even women and children who heard them all joyously turned toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote commentaries on the Six Edicts for the people to memorize; his explanations were so plain that even women and children listened with delight and took pleasure in virtue.

sentences.zh: 五年，坐事免。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was dismissed because of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of his tenure he was dismissed on a charge.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以左都御史魏象樞薦，起授四川資陽縣，途出內黃，民遮道慰問，日行僅數里。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, on the recommendation of Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiangju, he was recalled and appointed to Ziyang County in Sichuan; passing through Neihuang, the people blocked the road to greet and inquire after him; each day he advanced only a few li.
translations.idiomatic: In 1679, recommended by Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiangju, he was called back to serve as magistrate of Ziyang in Sichuan. Passing through Neihuang, crowds blocked his path to welcome him, and he made only a few li per day.

sentences.zh: 既抵任，值吳三桂據瀘州，相去數百里，羽檄如織。

translations.literal: After he arrived to take office, Wu Sangui held Luzhou, several hundred li distant; urgent dispatches came thick as woven silk.
translations.idiomatic: No sooner had he taken up his post than Wu Sangui seized Luzhou, only a few hundred li away, and orders flew in without cease.

sentences.zh: 城中人戶不滿二百，沐入山招撫，量為調發，供夫驛不缺。

translations.literal: Within the city registered households numbered fewer than two hundred; Mu entered the mountains to win over and pacify people, appropriately requisitioned them, and supplies for corvée labor and courier stations never fell short.
translations.idiomatic: The town held fewer than two hundred households. Mu went into the hills to recruit and reassure the people, rationed their labor fairly, and never once failed to meet the army's demands for men and post-horses.

sentences.zh: 滇事平，以老乞休。

translations.literal: When the Yunnan affair was settled, he requested retirement on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yunnan rebellion was put down, he asked to retire on grounds of age.

sentences.zh: 沐自幼勵志為聖賢，初官內黃，講學明倫堂，請業恆數百人。

translations.literal: From youth Mu resolved to become a sage or worthy; when he first served as magistrate of Neihuang, he lectured at the Hall of Illuminating Principle, and those seeking instruction were invariably several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Mu set his heart on becoming a sage. As magistrate of Neihuang he lectured in the Hall of Illuminating Principle before audiences that routinely numbered in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 湯斌過境，與語大悅，遺書孫奇逢，稱其任道甚勇，求道甚切。

translations.literal: Tang Bin passed through the territory; speaking with him, he was greatly pleased and wrote to Sun Qifeng, praising him as very bold in bearing the Way and very earnest in seeking the Way.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Bin passed through, he spoke with Mu and was deeply impressed; he wrote Sun Qifeng calling Mu fearless in his devotion to the Way and urgent in his pursuit of it.

sentences.zh: 沐因以禮幣迎奇逢至內黃講學，俾多士有所宗仰。

translations.literal: Mu therefore with ritual gifts invited Qifeng to Neihuang to lecture, enabling many scholars to have someone to revere and follow.
translations.idiomatic: Mu accordingly invited Sun Qifeng to Neihuang with proper ceremony, giving the local scholars a master worthy of devotion.

sentences.zh: 及在資陽，供億軍興之暇，猶進諸生誨導不倦。

translations.literal: When he was at Ziyang, amid provisioning the army's mobilization, he still advanced upon the students with tireless instruction and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Even while provisioning the army in Ziyang, he never ceased teaching and guiding his students.

sentences.zh: 退休後，主講汴中，兩河之士翕然歸之，多所成就。

translations.literal: After retirement, he served as chief lecturer in Bianzhou; scholars of the two He regions all at once turned to follow him, and many were brought to accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he headed the academy at Bianliang; scholars from across the Yellow River and Huai River regions flocked to him, and he shaped many of the finest minds of his day.

sentences.zh: 年八十三，卒。

translations.literal: At age eighty-three he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 沐之自內黃罷歸也，值登封令張塤興書院，偕耿介同講學，為文紀其事，一時稱盛。

translations.literal: When Mu was dismissed from Neihuang and returned home, it happened that Magistrate Zhang Kun of Dengfeng was founding an academy; together with Geng Jie they jointly lectured, and he wrote a piece commemorating the affair — for a time it was acclaimed as a flourishing age.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu left Neihuang in disgrace, Magistrate Zhang Kun was reviving an academy at Dengfeng. Mu joined Geng Jie there in teaching and wrote an account of the gathering, which was celebrated as a high point of the age.

sentences.zh: 塤字牖如，江蘇長洲人。

translations.literal: Kun, courtesy name Youru, was a native of Changzhou in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kun, styled Youru, came from Changzhou in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 以官學教習議敘知縣。

translations.literal: Through his post as instructor at the Imperial Academy he was evaluated and granted the rank of magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His service as an instructor at the Imperial Academy earned him qualification as a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 康熙十七年，授登封縣，單騎之任。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi he was appointed to Dengfeng County and went alone on horseback to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1678 he was appointed magistrate of Dengfeng and rode to his post unaccompanied.

sentences.zh: 途中與登封吏同宿逆旅，吏不知也。

translations.literal: On the road he lodged at the same inn with a Dengfeng clerk, and the clerk did not know who he was.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he shared an inn with a clerk from Dengfeng who never guessed his identity.

sentences.zh: 至縣三日，拜岳，誓不取一錢，不枉一人。

translations.literal: Three days after reaching the county he worshipped at the sacred mountain and swore to take not one coin nor wrong one person.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after arriving he paid homage at Mount Song and swore he would take not a single coin in bribes nor wrong a single soul.

sentences.zh: 衙前樹巨石鐫曰「永除私派」。

translations.literal: Before the yamen he planted a great stone engraved with the words "Private levies abolished forever."
translations.idiomatic: Before the yamen he set up a boulder carved with the words "Unauthorized exactions abolished forever."

sentences.zh: 設櫃，民自封投，無羨折。

translations.literal: He set up a chest; the people sealed and submitted payments themselves, with no surplus deductions.
translations.idiomatic: He installed drop-boxes so people could seal and submit their payments themselves, with no surcharges or skimming.

sentences.zh: 招集流亡，督之耕種，相其土宜，課植木棉及諸果實。

translations.literal: He gathered the displaced, supervised their planting and cultivation, assessed the suitability of the soil, and assigned the planting of cotton and various fruits.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled refugees, set them to farming, matched crops to local conditions, and promoted cotton orchards and fruit trees.

sentences.zh: 大修學宮，复嵩陽書院，宋四大書院之一也，延耿介為之師。

translations.literal: He greatly repaired the Confucian temple, restored the Songyang Academy — one of the four great academies of the Song — and invited Geng Jie to serve as its teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the county school and restored the Songyang Academy, one of the Song dynasty's four great academies, appointing Geng Jie as its master.

sentences.zh: 導諸生以程、硃之學。

translations.literal: He guided the students in the learning of the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the scholars in the Neo-Confucian teachings of the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 自縣治達郊鄙，立學舍二十一所。

translations.literal: From the county seat reaching to the outer villages, he established twenty-one schoolhouses.
translations.idiomatic: From the county seat to the remotest hamlets he founded twenty-one village schools.

sentences.zh: 課童子，以時巡閱，正句讀，導之以揖讓進退之禮。

translations.literal: He instructed village boys, touring to inspect at fixed times, correcting pauses in recitation, and guiding them in the rites of bowing, yielding, advancing, and withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: He tested village boys on schedule, corrected their recitation, and drilled them in the ceremonies of bowing, yielding, advancing, and retreating.

sentences.zh: 間策蹇驢歷諸郊問所苦，有小爭訟，輒於阡陌間決之。

translations.literal: At times he drove a lame donkey through the various suburbs inquiring after hardships; for small disputes and lawsuits he immediately decided them among the fields and paths.
translations.idiomatic: Now and then he rode a donkey through the countryside asking after the people's troubles, settling petty disputes right there among the fields.

sentences.zh: 西境有呂店者，俗好訟。

translations.literal: In the western borderlands there was a place called Lüdian whose custom was fondness for litigation.
translations.idiomatic: In the west of the district lay Lüdian, a place notorious for quarrelsome litigation.

sentences.zh: 塤察里長張文約賢，舉為鄉約，俾行化導，澆風一變。

translations.literal: Kun observed that the village head Zhang Wenyue was worthy and promoted him as village covenant leader, enabling him to carry out moral transformation and guidance; the decadent custom was transformed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing the village head Zhang Wenyue as a man of worth, Kun appointed him covenant elder to lead moral reform — and the district's corrosive habits changed overnight.

sentences.zh: 里長申爾瑞負課且受杖，路拾人輸稅金，返之，寧受責，不利人財，塤義之，旌其門。

translations.literal: The village head Shen Errui owed taxes and had been beaten with the stick; on the road he picked up someone's tax payment in gold, returned it, and would rather accept punishment than profit from another's money; Kun praised his righteousness and honored his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Village head Shen Errui, beaten for tax arrears, found a lost payment on the road and returned it though he would rather face punishment than keep another's money. Kun honored him with a commendation at his gate.

sentences.zh: 鄉民高鵬舉死，妻孟年少，舅欲強嫁之，孟哭夫墓將自縊，塤適微行，問其故，給以銀米勸還家而免其徭，歲時存問，俾終其節。

translations.literal: A villager named Gao Pengju died; his wife Meng was young in years; her husband's elder brother wished to force her to remarry. Meng wept at her husband's grave and was about to hang herself. Kun happened to be traveling incognito, asked the reason, gave her silver and grain and urged her to return home while exempting her from corvée, visiting her at the seasons to inquire after her welfare, enabling her to maintain her chastity to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When villager Gao Pengju died, his young widow Meng was pressed by her brother-in-law to remarry. She wept at her husband's grave and was about to hang herself when Kun, passing incognito, learned her story, gave her silver and grain, sent her home exempt from labor, and visited her each season so she might keep her widowhood to the end.

sentences.zh: 縣故多胥役，時獄訟日尟，姦偽無所容，諸胥多自引去。

translations.literal: The county formerly had many clerk-runners; now lawsuits daily grew fewer, and fraud and deceit had nowhere to lodge; many of the clerks withdrew of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: The county had swarmed with grasping clerks and runners, but as lawsuits dwindled and fraud had no room to hide, most of them quit of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 其更番執事者，退則操耒耜為農，以在官無所得錢也。

translations.literal: Those who took turns in office, when off duty would wield hoes and plows as farmers, because in office they obtained no money.
translations.idiomatic: Those who still served rotated in and out of duty and went back to the fields afterward, for office brought them no illicit gain.

sentences.zh: 開萼嶺二百里，復古轘轅路。

translations.literal: He opened Eling for two hundred li and restored the ancient Xuanyuan Road.
translations.idiomatic: He cut a two-hundred-li road through E Ridge and reopened the ancient Xuanyuan Pass route.

sentences.zh: 建古賢令祠，修鄢公墓，崇禎末為令守城抗賊死者也。

translations.literal: He built a shrine to ancient worthy magistrates and repaired the tomb of Prefect Yan, who in the late Chongzhen reign had died as magistrate defending the city against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He built a shrine to worthy magistrates of old and restored the tomb of Magistrate Yan, who had died defending the walls against rebels in the last days of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 在官五年，民知向方，生聚日盛，大書「官清民樂」於門。

translations.literal: In office for five years, the people knew which way to turn; population and prosperity grew daily; they wrote in large characters "Officials clean, people joyful" on the gate.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in office the people knew virtue from vice, prosperity and population flourished, and someone inscribed "Clean Officials, Happy People" above the city gate in great characters.

sentences.zh: 耿介嘗歎曰：「年來嵩、洛間，別一世界矣！」

translations.literal: Geng Jie once sighed and said: "In recent years, between Mount Song and the Luo River, it is a separate world!"
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jie once exclaimed, "These past years, between Song and Luo — it is another world entirely!"

sentences.zh: 二十二年，以卓異薦，擢廣西南寧通判。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, on recommendation as exceptionally outstanding, he was promoted to assistant prefect of Nanning in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1683 he was nominated for exceptional merit and promoted to assistant prefect of Nanning in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 去之日，民遮道哭，立祠於四鄉，肖像祀焉，榜曰「天下清官第一」。

translations.literal: On the day of his departure the people blocked the road weeping; they established shrines in the four townships and worshipped his portrait, with a placard reading "The Number One Clean Official under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: When he left, people blocked the roads in tears, erected shrines in four townships with his portrait for worship, and posted the title "The Foremost Honest Official Under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 至南寧，未幾，乞歸。

translations.literal: After reaching Nanning, before long he requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Nanning but soon asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 母喪，服除，赴京師，卒。

translations.literal: His mother died; when mourning was completed he went to the capital and died.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he journeyed to the capital and died there.

sentences.zh: 陳汝咸，字華學，浙江鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Chen Ruxian, courtesy name Huaxue, was a native of Yin County in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ruxian, styled Huaxue, was from Yin County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少隨父錫嘏講學證人社，黃宗羲曰：「此程門之楊迪，硃門之蔡沈也。」

translations.literal: In youth he followed his father Xichang in lecturing at the Society for Proving the Way; Huang Zongxi said: "This is Yang Di of Cheng's gate, Cai Shen of Zhu's gate."
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied with his father Xichang at the Society for Proving the Way. Huang Zongxi said of him, "He is to the Cheng school what Yang Di was — to Zhu's school what Cai Shen was."

sentences.zh: 康熙三十年，會試第一，成進士，選庶吉士，散館授福建漳浦知縣。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Kangxi he placed first in the metropolitan examination, became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor, and upon leaving the Hanlin Academy was appointed magistrate of Zhangpu in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1691 he came first in the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy, and upon completion of his training was sent as magistrate of Zhangpu in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 民好訟，嚴懲訟師，無敢欺者。

translations.literal: The people were fond of litigation; he severely punished litigation masters, and none dared to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: The people were litigious; he cracked down harshly on professional lawsuit brokers, and none dared ply that trade under his watch.

sentences.zh: 縣中賦役故責戶長主辦，版籍混淆，吏緣為奸。

translations.literal: In the county taxes and corvée had traditionally been charged to household heads to manage; registers were confused, and clerks exploited this for fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Tax and corvée had long been dumped on household heads; confused registers gave clerks endless openings for graft.

sentences.zh: 汝咸躬自編審人丁，各歸現籍。

translations.literal: Ruxian personally compiled and reviewed the population register, each person returning to their current registration.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxian personally revised the household registers and assigned every man to his current domicile.

sentences.zh: 糧戶自封投納，用滾單法輪催，以三百戶為一保，第其人口多寡供役。

translations.literal: Grain households sealed and submitted payments themselves; he used the rotating demand-slip method for collection in turn; with three hundred households as one bao, he ranked corvée service according to population size.
translations.idiomatic: Taxpayers sealed their own payments; he rotated collection duties via the "rolling roster" method; every three hundred households formed a bao, and labor assignments were scaled to population.

sentences.zh: 五年一編丁，而役法平。

translations.literal: Every five years the register of males was revised, and the corvée law was equitable.
translations.idiomatic: A census of adult males every five years left the corvée system fair and balanced.

sentences.zh: 吏胥以不便撓之，大吏搖惑，汝咸毅然不回，奸人無所施技。

translations.literal: Clerk-runners obstructed on grounds of inconvenience; high officials wavered in doubt; Ruxian resolutely did not turn back, and evil men had nowhere to deploy their tricks.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks raised objections on grounds of inconvenience and even senior officials wavered, but Ruxian held firm, and the schemers had no lever left to pull.

sentences.zh: 民樂輸將，賦無逋負。

translations.literal: The people gladly paid taxes and tribute; levies had no arrears.
translations.idiomatic: The people paid willingly, and not a farthing of tax went unpaid.

sentences.zh: 俗輕生，多因細故服斷腸草死，挾以圖財，力懲其弊，令當刑者掘草根贖罪。

translations.literal: The custom held life cheap; many for trivial causes took gut-severing grass to die, using it to extort wealth. He strictly punished this abuse, ordering those facing punishment to dig up the grass roots to redeem their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom treated life lightly: over petty quarrels people swallowed gut-severing grass to feign suicide and shake down their opponents for money. Ruxian cracked down hard on the racket and ordered offenders sentenced to corporal punishment to dig up the plant by the roots as part of their penance.

sentences.zh: 禁舁神療病，曉示方證，自製藥以濟貧者。

translations.literal: He banned carrying gods about to heal illness, explained prescriptions and indications, and made medicines himself to aid the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He outlawed the practice of parading spirit-images through the streets to cure sickness, taught people proper prescriptions instead, and compounded medicines with his own hands for the poor.

sentences.zh: 毀學宮伽藍祠，葺故儒陳真晟、周瑛、高登諸人所著書表章之。

translations.literal: He demolished the Buddhist shrine in the academy precinct, restored and publicly honored books by former Confucians Chen Zhensheng, Zhou Ying, Gao Deng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He tore down the Buddhist chapel within the county school, restored the works of earlier local scholars such as Chen Zhensheng, Zhou Ying, and Gao Deng, and had them publicly celebrated.

sentences.zh: 歸誠書院，乃黃道周講學地，為僧據，逐而新之。

translations.literal: Guicheng Academy was where Huang Daozhou had lectured; monks had seized it, and he expelled them and renovated it.
translations.idiomatic: Guicheng Academy, where Huang Daozhou had once taught, had been taken over by monks; Ruxian drove them out and rebuilt the hall.

sentences.zh: 無為教者，男女群聚茹蔬禮佛，籍其居為育嬰堂。

translations.literal: Followers of the Wuwei sect gathered men and women to eat vegetables and worship Buddha; he converted their meeting place into an infant asylum.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuwei sect drew men and women together for vegetarian worship; he seized their meeting house and turned it into a foundling asylum.

sentences.zh: 西洋天主教要大吏將於漳浦開堂，卻止之。

translations.literal: Western Catholicism sought permission from high officials to open a church in Zhangpu; he blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: Western Catholics had petitioned provincial authorities to establish a church in Zhangpu, and he put a stop to it.

sentences.zh: 修文廟，造祭器，時會邑中士紳於明倫堂講經史性理諸書。

translations.literal: He repaired the Confucian temple, made sacrificial vessels, and regularly gathered local gentry and scholars at the Minglun Hall to lecture on the classics, histories, and Neo-Confucian texts.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Confucian temple, commissioned ritual vessels, and regularly assembled the county gentry in the Minglun Hall for readings in the classics, histories, and moral philosophy.

sentences.zh: 設義學，延諸生有學行者為之師。

translations.literal: He established a charity school and invited licentiates of learning and conduct to serve as teachers.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a charity school and engaged licentiates of proven scholarship and character to teach there.

sentences.zh: 修硃子祠。

translations.literal: He restored the shrine to Master Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the shrine to Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 教養兼施，風俗為之一變。

translations.literal: Instruction and nurture were applied together, and local customs were wholly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Education and relief went hand in hand, and the county's customs were transformed.

sentences.zh: 會大水驟漲，幾及城堞，輿錢登城，多為木筏，渡一人與錢三十，人皆以錢助拯，活者數千。

translations.literal: When a flood suddenly rose and nearly reached the battlements, he carried silver up onto the walls, had many rafts built, paying thirty cash per person rescued; everyone contributed their reward money to the rescue effort, saving thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When a sudden flood nearly topped the city walls, he brought silver up onto the ramparts, had rafts built in large numbers, and paid thirty cash for every person ferried to safety; people poured their rewards back into the rescue, and thousands were saved.

sentences.zh: 多方撫卹，雖災不害。

translations.literal: He comforted and relieved the victims on many fronts, so that despite the calamity there was little harm.
translations.idiomatic: Relief came from every direction he could muster, so that even amid disaster the harm was contained.

sentences.zh: 土寇伏七里洞，將入海，發兵擊之，走山中。

translations.literal: Bandits lurked at Qili Cave, about to take to the sea; he sent troops to strike them, and they fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Local bandits lay hidden at Qili Cave, poised to slip out to sea; he sent troops against them and drove them into the hills.

sentences.zh: 密招賊黨，誘擒其渠曾睦等，餘黨悉散。

translations.literal: Secretly he summoned bandit associates, lured and captured their ringleader Zeng Mu and others, and the rest scattered entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Through secret contacts among the bandits he lured out their chief, Zeng Mu, and others; the remaining gangs broke up completely.

sentences.zh: 又擒海盜徐容，盡得賊中委曲，赦其罪，責以招撫。

translations.literal: He also captured the pirate Xu Rong, learned every detail of the bandit network, pardoned his crime, and charged him with winning others over by leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He next captured the pirate Xu Rong, learned the whole inner workings of the gangs, pardoned him, and set him to win the rest over by persuasion.

sentences.zh: 諸盜歸誠，海氛遂清。

translations.literal: All the bandits submitted in good faith, and piracy on the seas was cleared away.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates surrendered in earnest, and the coast was cleared at last.

sentences.zh: 汝咸任漳浦凡十有八年，大吏因南靖多盜，調使治之，縣民請留不得，扌冓生祠曰月湖書院，歲時祀之。

translations.literal: Ruxian served Zhangpu for eighteen years in all; higher officials, because Nanjing had many bandits, transferred him to govern there; county people petitioned to keep him but could not; they built a living shrine called Yuehu Academy and sacrificed to him at the proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxian had governed Zhangpu for eighteen years when higher officials, troubled by banditry in Nanjing County, transferred him there. The people petitioned in vain to keep him and instead built a living shrine, Yuehu Academy, where they worshipped him at the proper seasons.

sentences.zh: 汝咸至南靖，諸盜自首就撫，開示威信，頌聲大作。

translations.literal: When Ruxian reached Nanjing, all the bandits surrendered themselves for lenient settlement; he showed authority and trust, and praise for him resounded widely.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ruxian arrived in Nanjing, bandits came forward of their own accord to accept amnesty. He combined firmness with good faith, and praise for his rule spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，內遷刑部主事，擢御史。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, he was transferred inward to main clerk in the Ministry of Justice and promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year of Kangxi he was recalled to the capital as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice and then promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「商船出海，掛號無​​益，徒以滋累。」

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "When merchant vessels put out to sea, registration is useless and only increases burdens.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he argued that registering merchant ships before they sailed served no purpose and only piled on red tape.

sentences.zh: 又言：「海賊入內地，必返其家。

translations.literal: He also said: "When sea bandits enter the interior, they invariably return to their homes.
translations.idiomatic: He added that sea pirates who slipped inland always returned home afterward.

sentences.zh: 下海劫掠，責之巡哨官；

translations.literal: For raids at sea, hold the patrol officers responsible;
translations.idiomatic: Raids at sea should be laid at the door of the coastal patrol officers;

sentences.zh: 未下海之踪跡，責之本籍縣令；

translations.literal: for traces before they went to sea, hold the magistrate of their native county responsible;
translations.idiomatic: their movements on land before they took to the water should be the responsibility of the magistrate in their home county;

sentences.zh: 當力行各澳保甲。」

translations.literal: each harbor's baojia system should be vigorously enforced.
translations.idiomatic: and the baojia household registers at every harbor ought to be enforced with real vigor.

sentences.zh: 會海盜陳尚義乞降，汝咸自請往撫。

translations.literal: Just then the pirate Chen Shangyi begged to surrender, and Ruxian volunteered to go and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the pirate Chen Shangyi offered to surrender, and Ruxian asked to go and accept his submission in person.

sentences.zh: 聖祖命郎中雅奇偕汝咸所薦阮蔡生往，尚義率其黨百餘人果就撫，擢通政使參議。

translations.literal: The Sagely Ancestor ordered Director Ya Qi to go with Ruan Caisheng, whom Ruxian had recommended; Shangyi led more than a hundred followers and did indeed submit; Ruxian was promoted to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Director Ya Qi to accompany Ruan Caisheng, whom Ruxian had recommended. Shangyi brought more than a hundred followers and submitted as promised, and Ruxian was promoted to vice commissioner in the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，奉使祭炎帝神農、帝舜陵，並頒賚駐防兵。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year, he was sent on mission to sacrifice at the tombs of the Flame Emperor Shennong and Emperor Shun, and also to distribute imperial gifts to garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year he was dispatched to offer sacrifice at the tombs of the Flame Emperor Shennong and Emperor Shun, and to distribute imperial rewards to frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 遍歷苗疆，審度形勢撫馭之策。

translations.literal: He traveled throughout the Miao frontier, assessing terrain and devising policies of pacification and control.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled the Miao frontier from end to end, studying the terrain and shaping policies for pacification and control.

sentences.zh: 歷鴻臚寺少卿、大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: He served successively as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，命赴甘肅賑荒，徒步窮鄉，感疫，卒於固原。
