translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, he was ordered to Gansu for famine relief, traveled on foot through remote villages, caught epidemic disease, and died at Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year he was sent to Gansu to relieve famine, tramped on foot through the poorest villages, contracted an epidemic illness, and died at Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 漳浦士民聞之，奔哭於月湖書院，醵金置田，歲祀不絕。

translations.literal: When Zhangpu gentry and commoners heard, they ran weeping to Yuehu Academy, pooled money to endow fields, and sacrifices continued year after year without lapse.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Zhangpu heard the news, they rushed weeping to Yuehu Academy, pooled funds to endow sacrificial fields, and kept his rites alive year after year.

sentences.zh: 著有兼山堂遺稿、漳浦政略​​諸書。

translations.literal: His writings include Posthumous Drafts of the Jianshan Hall, Administrative Outline of Zhangpu, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: He left writings including Posthumous Drafts from the Jianshan Hall and An Administrative Account of Zhangpu, among others.

sentences.zh: 繆燧，字雯曜，江蘇江陰人。

translations.literal: Miao Sui, courtesy name Wenyao, was a native of Jiangyin, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Sui, styled Wenyao, came from Jiangyin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 貢生，入貲為知縣。

translations.literal: A tribute student; he purchased office and became a magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: A tribute student, he bought his way into office and was appointed a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 康熙十七年，授山東沂水縣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, he was appointed to Yishui County, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi he was assigned to Yishui County in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 時山左飢，朝使發賑，將購米濟南。

translations.literal: At that time Shandong was in famine; the court sent relief commissioners who planned to purchase grain in Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong was then in famine, and the court dispatched relief officials who planned to buy grain in Jinan for distribution.

sentences.zh: 燧以路遠往返需日，且運費多，不便。

translations.literal: Sui said the road was long, round trips required days, and transport costs were heavy—inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Sui argued that the distance made each round trip consume days and that transport costs would be ruinous—the scheme was impractical.

sentences.zh: 請以銀給民自買，當事以違旨勿聽。

translations.literal: He requested giving silver to the people to buy for themselves; the authorities refused as contrary to the directive.
translations.idiomatic: He asked instead that silver be given directly to the people to buy grain locally, but the commissioners rejected the idea as contrary to orders.

sentences.zh: 燧力爭以因地制宜之義，代草疏奏請，得允。

translations.literal: Sui argued forcefully on grounds of adapting to local conditions, drafted a memorial on their behalf, and obtained approval.
translations.idiomatic: Sui pressed the case on grounds of adapting policy to local conditions, drafted a memorial for them, and won approval.

sentences.zh: 既而帑金不足，傾囊以濟之。

translations.literal: Before long the treasury silver was insufficient; he emptied his own purse to make up the shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: When the allotted funds soon ran short, he emptied his own purse to cover the gap.

sentences.zh: 洊飢之後，民多流亡，出私錢為償逋欠，購牛種，招徠復業。

translations.literal: After repeated famine many people had fled; he paid out private money to clear debts, bought oxen and seed, and recruited them back to their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: After successive famines many people had fled; he spent his own money to settle their debts, bought oxen and seed, and coaxed them home to farm again.

sentences.zh: 因捕劇盜已獲复逸，被議歸。

translations.literal: Because a notorious bandit who had been captured escaped again, he was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When a notorious bandit he had captured broke jail, he was impeached and sent home.

sentences.zh: 尋复官。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，授浙江定海縣，故舟山也，設治未久，百度草創。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, he was appointed to Dinghai County, Zhejiang—the former Zhoushan; administration had recently been established and every institution was still being founded.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he was posted to Dinghai County in Zhejiang—the old Zhoushan—where civil administration was newly established and every institution still had to be built from scratch.

sentences.zh: 海水不宜穀，築塘岸以御咸蓄淡，修復塘碶百餘所，田日增闢。

translations.literal: Seawater was unsuitable for grain; he built dyke walls to hold back salt and store fresh water, restored more than a hundred sluice-gates and seawalls, and farmland expanded daily.
translations.idiomatic: Seawater made grain-growing difficult, so he built dykes to keep out salt and hold fresh water, restored more than a hundred sluices and seawalls, and opened new fields day by day.

sentences.zh: 繕城濬濠，葺學宮，建祠廟，役繁而不擾。

translations.literal: He repaired walls and dredged moats, restored the academy, built shrines and temples—the workload was heavy yet the people were not harassed.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the city walls and dredged the moat, restored the county school, and built shrines and temples—heavy work, yet the people were not unduly burdened.

sentences.zh: 地瘠民貧，完賦不能以時，逾限者先為墊解，秋後輸還。

translations.literal: The land was poor and the people impoverished; they could not pay taxes on time—those past deadline he advanced payment for from his own funds, to be repaid after the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was thin and the people poor; they could not meet tax deadlines, so he advanced payment for those who fell behind and let them repay after the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 舊有塗稅，出自漁戶網捕之地，後漁塗被佔，苦賠累，為請罷之。

translations.literal: There had been a mudflat tax levied on fishing grounds; later the fishing flats were seized and fishermen suffered compensatory liability—he petitioned to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: An old tax on tidal flats had been tied to fishing grounds, but once those grounds were seized the fishermen were still forced to pay; he petitioned successfully to abolish the levy.

sentences.zh: 地故產鹽，無灶戶，鹽運使屢檄設廠砌盤，官為收賣。

translations.literal: The area naturally produced salt but had no saltern households; the salt transport commissioner repeatedly ordered setting up offices and evaporating pans for official purchase and sale.
translations.idiomatic: The county naturally yielded salt but had no registered saltern households, and the salt commissioner repeatedly ordered official pans and government purchase and resale.

sentences.zh: 燧持不可，請仿江南崇明縣計丁銷引，歲完鹽稅銀四十二兩有奇，著為例。

translations.literal: Sui held this was unworkable and requested following Chongming County in Jiangnan: assess by household and cancel salt certificates, completing annual salt tax of a little over forty-two taels of silver—this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Sui objected that this would not work and proposed following the Jiangnan model of Chongming County: assess households and cancel salt certificates, paying a fixed annual salt tax of just over forty-two taels of silver. The arrangement became permanent law.

sentences.zh: 學額多為外籍竄冒，援宣平縣例，半為土著，半令他縣人認墾入籍以充賦。

translations.literal: Many examination quotas were stolen by outsiders falsely claiming native status; citing Xuanping County precedent, half for natives, half permitting outsiders from other counties who claimed reclaimed land and entered the register to meet tax obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Examination quotas were often seized by outsiders falsely claiming local status; citing the precedent of Xuanping County, he reserved half the places for natives and half for settlers from other counties who reclaimed land, entered the register, and fulfilled tax obligations.

sentences.zh: 又以土著不能副額，擴建義學，增廩額以鼓舞之，文教興焉。

translations.literal: Also because natives could not fill the quota, he expanded the charity school and increased stipend quotas to encourage them—literary culture flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Because local candidates still could not fill the quota, he enlarged the charity school and added stipends to encourage study, and learning flourished.

sentences.zh: 民間日用所需，多航海市諸郡城，關胥苛索，請永禁，立石海關。

translations.literal: Daily necessities came mostly by sea from prefectural cities; customs clerks extorted harshly—he requested permanent prohibition and erected a stone at the maritime customs.
translations.idiomatic: Daily goods came mostly by sea from mainland ports, where customs runners extorted bribes; he petitioned for a permanent ban and had the prohibition carved in stone at the harbor customs house.

sentences.zh: 海嶼為盜藪，隨監司歷勘，凡羊巷、下八、盡山、花腦、玉環、半邊、牛韭諸島，權度要害措置之，盜風頓戢。

translations.literal: Sea islands were bandit dens; he accompanied the surveillance commissioner on inspection tours; for Yangxiang, Xiaba, Jinshan, Huanao, Yuhuan, Banbian, Niujiu, and other islands he weighed key points and disposed forces—piracy subsided sharply.
translations.idiomatic: The outlying islands were pirate haunts; he toured them with the surveillance commissioner and, at Yangxiang, Xiaba, Jinshan, Huanao, Yuhuan, Banbian, Niujiu, and other isles, placed guards at every strategic point. Piracy collapsed almost overnight.

sentences.zh: 同歸域者，海上死事諸人瘞骨處，捐貲修葺，建成仁祠，以勸忠義。

translations.literal: Tonggui Yu was where the bones of those who died at sea were buried; he donated funds to restore it and built the Chengreng Shrine to encourage loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggui Yu, the burial ground for those lost at sea, he restored at his own expense and built the Chengreng Shrine there to honor loyalty and public service.

sentences.zh: 歷權慈谿、鎮海、鄞縣及寧波府事，皆有惠政。

translations.literal: He held acting posts in Cixi, Zhenhai, Yin County, and Ningbo prefecture affairs—everywhere benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: He also served in acting posts at Cixi, Zhenhai, Yin County, and the Ningbo prefectural seat, leaving benevolent rule wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 擢杭州府同知，未任。

translations.literal: Promoted to vice prefect of Hangzhou but never took up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice prefect of Hangzhou but never left Dinghai to take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，卒於定海。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, he died at Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year he died at Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 士民援唐王漁、宋趙師旦故事，留葬衣冠，奉祀於義學，名之曰蓉浦書院，蓉浦，燧自號也。

translations.literal: Gentry and people, citing Tang Wangyu and Song Zhao Shidan, kept his garment and cap for burial and worshipped him at the charity school, naming it Rongpu Academy—Rongpu was Sui's sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: Following the examples of Tang Wangyu and Song Zhao Shidan, the gentry and common people kept his hat and robes for burial and worshipped him at the charity school, renaming it Rongpu Academy—Rongpu being Sui's own style.

sentences.zh: 遺愛久而不湮，光緒中復請祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: His cherished memory endured long without fading; in the Guangxu era they again petitioned for sacrifice in the shrine of celebrated officials.
translations.idiomatic: Memory of his kindness endured; in the Guangxu reign his admirers petitioned again to enshrine him among celebrated officials.

sentences.zh: 燧任定海前後二十二年，賜四品頂戴，賜御書。

translations.literal: Sui served Dinghai for twenty-two years before and after, was granted fourth-rank hat ornament and imperial calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Sui governed Dinghai for twenty-two years in all and was granted a fourth-rank hat ornament and an imperial inscription in the Emperor's own hand.

sentences.zh: 後雖擢官，迄未離任。

translations.literal: Though later promoted, he never left his post.
translations.idiomatic: Though promoted later on, he never actually left the county.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷重守令，循良多久於其職。

translations.literal: At the time the court valued magistrates; upright officials often remained long in office.
translations.idiomatic: In those days the court prized local magistrates, and upright officials were often kept in post for many years.

sentences.zh: 陳汝咸治漳浦十有八年，陳時臨治汝陽亦二十年。

translations.literal: Chen Ruxian governed Zhangpu for eighteen years; Chen Shilin governed Ruyang also for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ruxian ruled Zhangpu for eighteen years, and Chen Shilin ruled Ruyang for twenty.

sentences.zh: 一邑利病，無所不知，視如家事，故吏治蒸蒸日上云。

translations.literal: The strengths and ills of a single county they knew completely, treating them as household affairs—thus administrative governance rose steadily.
translations.idiomatic: They knew every strength and sore point of their counties as if they were family matters, and for that reason local governance kept improving.

sentences.zh: 時臨，字二咸，浙江鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Shilin, courtesy name Erxian, was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shilin, styled Erxian, came from Yin County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少從陳錫嘏學，得聞證人書院之教。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Chen Xigu and received the teaching of the Zhengren Academy.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under Chen Xigu and absorbed the teachings of the Zhengren Academy.

sentences.zh: 家貧，遊京師。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he traveled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, so he went to the capital to seek his fortune.

sentences.zh: 三籓之變，從軍敘功，授湖南城步知縣。

translations.literal: During the Three Feudatories rebellion he joined the army, received merit appointment as magistrate of Chengbu, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Rebellion of the Three Feudatories he joined the army, earned merit, and was appointed magistrate of Chengbu in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸，廬墓三年。

translations.literal: When his father died he returned home, dwelling by the grave for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he returned home and mourned at the grave for three years.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十年，起授河南汝陽縣，兵亂之後，風俗大壞，民不知喪禮。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Kangxi, he was recalled and appointed to Ruyang County, Henan; after military chaos customs were greatly corrupted and the people did not know mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Kangxi he was recalled to serve as magistrate of Ruyang in Henan, where war had shattered custom and people no longer knew proper mourning.

sentences.zh: 時臨為斟酌古今所可通行者，衰絰聚飲之風以息。

translations.literal: Shilin adapted what was passable from ancient and modern practice—the custom of gathering in mourning garb to drink subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Shilin weighed ancient and modern practice and settled on what could actually be enforced, and the custom of carousing in mourning dress died away.

sentences.zh: 楊埠有支河，久淤，濬復其舊，民獲灌溉之利。

translations.literal: Yangbu had a branch river long silted up; he dredged and restored it, and the people gained irrigation benefit.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangbu a branch channel had long been choked with silt; he dredged it back to its old course and the farmers gained irrigation.

sentences.zh: 河南諸縣多食蘆鹽，獨汝寧一郡食淮鹽，蘆商欲並之，時臨謂：「蘆鹽計口而授，不問其所需之多寡，以成額給之，是厲民也。

translations.literal: Henan counties mostly ate reed salt; only Runing prefecture ate Huai salt; reed salt merchants wished to merge it. Shilin said: "Reed salt is allocated by mouth count regardless of need, fixed quota given—this harms the people.
translations.idiomatic: Most counties in Henan consumed reed salt, but Runing alone used Huai salt, and reed-salt merchants wanted to absorb the market. Shilin said, "Reed salt is rationed by head count without regard to actual need—a fixed quota for everyone. That only oppresses the people.

sentences.zh: 吾不能為河南盡革其害，反徇商人意以害境內乎？」

translations.literal: Can I not eliminate all the harm for Henan yet instead follow merchants' wishes to harm my jurisdiction?
translations.idiomatic: Am I to fail to remove every harm I can for Henan, and instead do the merchants' bidding to the injury of my own county?

sentences.zh: 力爭得止。

translations.literal: He argued forcefully and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the proposal hard and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 巡撫徐潮亟稱之，於是前後諸大吏皆以為循吏當令久任，數報最，數留之。

translations.literal: Governor Xu Chao praised him highly; thereafter successive great officials all regarded him as an upright official who should serve long—repeatedly reported top performance, repeatedly retained him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Xu Chao praised him warmly, and thereafter one superior after another treated him as the sort of upright magistrate who should be kept in place: his record was repeatedly rated highest, and he was repeatedly retained.

sentences.zh: 時臨亦與民相安於無事。

translations.literal: Shilin also lived with the people in untroubled peace.
translations.idiomatic: Shilin, for his part, lived with the people in quiet harmony.

sentences.zh: 後擢兵部主事，宦橐蕭寥，臨行，百姓扶老載弱相送數十里。

translations.literal: Later promoted to main clerk in the Ministry of War; his official purse was empty; on departure old and weak were supported and carried, seeing him off for dozens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted to a principal clerkship in the Ministry of War. His official purse was nearly empty; when he left, the people—old men supported on canes, children carried on backs—escorted him for miles.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以病乞歸，卒。

translations.literal: After a year, he begged retirement due to illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he petitioned to retire on grounds of illness and died.

sentences.zh: 姚文燮，字經三，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: Yao Wenxie, courtesy name Jingsan, was a native of Tongcheng, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Wenxie, styled Jingsan, came from Tongcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年進士，授福建建寧府推官。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the sixteenth year of Shunzhi; appointed reviewing officer of Jianning prefecture, Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the sixteenth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed reviewing officer for Jianning Prefecture in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 建寧俗號獷悍，以睚眥仇殺者案山積，文燮片言立剖，未數月囹圄為空。

translations.literal: Jianning customs were fierce; cases of killing over trifles piled mountain-high; Wenxie settled with a few words; within months the prisons were empty.
translations.idiomatic: Jianning had a reputation for violent tempers, and murder cases born of petty grudges piled up like hills. Wenxie cut through them with a few words, and within months the jails stood empty.

sentences.zh: 有方秘者，殺方飛熊，前令已讞定大辟。

translations.literal: There was Fang Mi who killed Fang Feixiong; the previous magistrate had already sentenced to capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: One Fang Mi had killed Fang Feixiong, and the previous magistrate had already fixed the sentence at death.

sentences.zh: 文燮鞫得飛熊初為盜，嘗殺秘一家，既就撫，秘乃乘間復仇，不可與殺平人等，秘得活。

translations.literal: Wenxie on trial learned Feixiong had first been a bandit, had killed Mi's whole family; after submission Mi took opportunity for revenge—not same as killing an equal—Mi lived.
translations.idiomatic: At trial Wenxie learned that Feixiong had once been a bandit who slaughtered Mi's entire family; after Feixiong accepted amnesty, Mi seized his chance for revenge—a case unlike ordinary murder—and Mi was spared.

sentences.zh: 大吏謂文燮明允，凡疑獄輒委決之。

translations.literal: Higher officials said Wenxie was bright and fair; all doubtful cases were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Superior officials judged Wenxie clear-minded and fair, and every doubtful case was sent to him for decision.

sentences.zh: 有武弁被殺，株連眾，文燮僅坐數人罪。

translations.literal: A military officer was killed, many implicated; Wenxie only punished several persons.
translations.idiomatic: When a military officer was murdered and a wide net of suspects was cast, Wenxie convicted only a handful.

sentences.zh: 大吏駭曰：「此叛案，何遽輕率？」

translations.literal: A higher official alarmed said: "This is a rebellion case—why so rashly light?
translations.idiomatic: A superior official was alarmed: "This is a case of rebellion—why treat it so lightly?

sentences.zh: 文燮曰：「某所據初報文及盜供也。」

translations.literal: Wenxie said: "What I relied on was the initial report and bandit confession.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxie replied, "I relied on the first report and the bandits' own confession.

sentences.zh: 蓋鄉民逐盜，弁適遇之，從騎未至，為盜所殺而盜逸，營中執為民叛殺弁。

translations.literal: In fact villagers were chasing bandits; the officer happened upon them, escort had not arrived, bandits killed him and escaped; camp detained it as villagers rebelling and killing officer.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers had been chasing bandits when the officer happened upon the scene; his escort had not yet arrived, the bandits killed him and fled, and the garrison treated it as a peasant revolt against an officer.

sentences.zh: 文燮檢得初報文，而盜亦獲，自供殺弁，故得其情。

translations.literal: Wenxie found the initial report; bandit also captured, confessed killing officer—thus he grasped the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxie recovered the first report, the bandits were captured and confessed to killing the officer, and the truth came out.

sentences.zh: 時耿氏建籓，其下多怙勢虐民，貸民錢而奪其妻女。

translations.literal: At the time the Geng princely establishment was founded; their men often relied on power to abuse people, lent money and seized wives and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: While the Geng princely house held its fief, its retainers often abused their power, lending money to commoners and seizing their wives and daughters when debts fell due.

sentences.zh: 文燮悉使訐發，為捐募代償，贖歸百數。

translations.literal: Wenxie had all exposed, raised donations to repay debts, ransomed back over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxie had every case brought forward, raised funds to pay off the debts, and ransomed back more than a hundred women.

sentences.zh: 奉檄主丈田事，建寧環郡皆山，民依山鑿田，每陡峻不能施弓繩，文燮授吏勾股法，計田廣狹，增減為畝，區畫悉當。

translations.literal: Ordered to oversee land surveying; Jianning ringed by mountains, people carved fields on slopes—too steep for bow-and-rope measurement; Wenxie taught clerks gougu method to calculate field width and adjust to acres—zoning all correct.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned to supervise land surveys, he found Jianning hemmed in by mountains where farmers terraced steep slopes too sheer for the standard bow-and-rope method. He taught his clerks the gougu right-triangle method to calculate each plot's width and convert it to acres, and every boundary was drawn correctly.

sentences.zh: 值邊海修戰船，或擬按戶口出錢，文燮上陳疾苦，籌款以代，民乃安。

translations.literal: When border-sea war ships were repaired, some proposed levying by household; Wenxie memorialized hardships and found funds as substitute—people then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When coastal war junks were due for repair and some proposed a head tax on every household, Wenxie memorialized the hardship and found other funds to cover the cost, and the people were spared.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，報最。

translations.literal: Term completed, reported top performance.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, his record was rated highest.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，詔裁各府推官，去職。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi, an edict abolished reviewing officers in all prefectures—he left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kangxi an edict abolished prefectural reviewing officers, and he left his post.

sentences.zh: 八年，改直隸雄縣知縣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, transferred to magistrate of Xiong County, Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to serve as magistrate of Xiong County in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 渾河泛溢，浸城，文燮修城築堤，造橋利涉者。

translations.literal: Hun River overflowed, flooding the city; Wenxie repaired walls, built dykes, and made bridges for easy crossing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hun River burst its banks and flooded the city, Wenxie repaired the walls, raised dykes, and built bridges to ease passage.

sentences.zh: 邑貢狐皮為民累，條上其弊，獲免。

translations.literal: County tribute of fox pelts was a burden on the people; he memorialized the abuse and obtained exemption.
translations.idiomatic: The county's tribute quota of fox pelts had become a crushing burden; he memorialized the abuse and won an exemption.

sentences.zh: 地近京畿，膏腴多圈佔為旗產，文燮為民爭之。

translations.literal: The land was close to the capital region; much fertile land had been enclosed and seized as banner estates, and Wenxie contended on behalf of the people.
translations.idiomatic: The district lay near the capital, and much of its best land had been fenced off and claimed as banner estates. Wenxie fought to reclaim it for the people.

sentences.zh: 旗人請於戶部，遣司官至，牽繩量地，繩所及，民不得有。

translations.literal: Bannermen petitioned the Board of Revenue; a department official was sent; they pulled ropes to measure land—wherever the rope reached, the people could not retain possession.
translations.idiomatic: Bannermen petitioned the Board of Revenue, which dispatched an official who measured land with ropes; whatever ground the rope covered was declared off limits to common holders.

sentences.zh: 文燮拔刀斷繩，司官見其剛直，詞稍遜。

translations.literal: Wenxie drew his sword and cut the measuring rope; the department official saw his firm integrity and his words became somewhat more deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxie drew his sword and severed the measuring rope. Seeing his unyielding integrity, the official moderated his tone.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有旨退地還民。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict ordered the land returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, an imperial edict ordered the land returned to the people.

sentences.zh: 團練屯丁，以資守望，盜賊屏跡。

translations.literal: He organized militia and garrison laborers to provide watch and guard; bandits vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: He organized militia and garrison laborers for patrol and watch, and bandits disappeared from the area.

sentences.zh: 報墾地，蠲耗羨，減鹽引，卹驛政，拊循瘡痏，民慶更生。

translations.literal: He reported reclaimed land, remitted surplus surcharges, reduced salt quotas, redressed courier-station administration, comforted wounds and sores, and the people rejoiced at rebirth.
translations.idiomatic: He registered reclaimed fields, remitted surplus levies, cut salt quotas, reformed the courier stations, and nursed the people's wounds until they celebrated a new lease on life.

sentences.zh: 擢雲南開化府同知，攝曲靖府阿迷州事。

translations.literal: Promoted to vice-prefect of Kaifu in Yunnan; acted in charge of Ami subprefecture in Qujing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice-prefect of Kaifu in Yunnan and placed in charge of Ami subprefecture under Qujing.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂叛，文燮陷賊中。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui rebelled; Wenxie was trapped among the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Wenxie was caught behind rebel lines.

sentences.zh: 密與建義將軍林興珠有約，為賊所覺，被系，乘隙遁，謁安親王岳樂軍中。

translations.literal: He secretly had an agreement with the Jianyi General Lin Xingzhu; the rebels detected it, he was imprisoned, escaped at an opening, and paid respects at Prince An Yuele's camp.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly made contact with the Jianyi General Lin Xingzhu, but the rebels discovered the plot, seized and imprisoned him; he slipped away at the first chance and made his way to Prince An Yuele's camp.

sentences.zh: 王以聞，召至京，賜對，詢軍事甚悉。

translations.literal: The prince reported it upward; Wenxie was summoned to the capital, granted an audience, and military affairs were inquired into in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: The prince reported the matter to the throne; Wenxie was summoned to the capital for an audience and questioned exhaustively on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 滇寇平，乃乞養歸。

translations.literal: When the Yunnan rebels were pacified, he requested retirement to care for his parents and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yunnan rebellion was put down, he asked leave to retire home and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 黃貞麟，字振侯，山東即墨人。

translations.literal: Huang Zhenlin, styled Zhenhou, a native of Jimo in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhenlin, styled Zhenhou, was a native of Jimo in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twelfth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Shunzhi (1655).

sentences.zh: 十八年，授安徽鳳陽推官，嚴懲訟師，閤郡懍然。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, appointed reviewing officer of Fengyang in Anhui; he severely punished litigation masters, and the entire prefecture was awed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Shunzhi (1661), he was appointed reviewing officer in Fengyang, Anhui. He cracked down hard on professional litigators, and the whole prefecture fell into awe-struck order.

sentences.zh: 大旱，禱雨未應，貞麟曰：「得無有沈冤未雪，上乾天和乎？」

translations.literal: Great drought; prayers for rain went unanswered. Zhenlin said: "Could it be that deep wrongs have not been cleared, offending Heaven's harmony?"
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought, prayers for rain went unanswered. Zhenlin said, "Could it be that some grave injustice remains unredressed, disturbing Heaven's harmony?

sentences.zh: 於禱雨壇下，立判諸大獄，三日果雨。

translations.literal: At the rain-prayer altar he immediately judged major cases; rain indeed fell within three days.
translations.idiomatic: At the rain-prayer altar he promptly adjudicated the most serious pending cases, and within three days rain fell.

sentences.zh: 江南逋賦案興，蒙城、懷遠、天長、盱眙各逮紳民百餘人繫獄候勘。

translations.literal: A Jiangnan case of arrear taxes arose; Mengcheng, Huaiyuan, Tianchang, and Xuyi each detained over a hundred gentry and commoners imprisoned awaiting investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When a case over tax arrears in Jiangnan flared up, Mengcheng, Huaiyuan, Tianchang, and Xuyi each held more than a hundred gentry and commoners in prison awaiting investigation.

sentences.zh: 獄不能容，人皆立，貞麟曰：「彼逋賦皆未驗實，忍令僵死於獄乎？」

translations.literal: The prisons could not hold them; all stood packed in. Zhenlin said: "Those tax arrears have none been verified—can we bear to let them stiffen and die in prison?"
translations.idiomatic: The prisons could not hold them all and inmates stood shoulder to shoulder. Zhenlin said, "None of those tax debts has been verified. How can we allow people to die standing in jail?

sentences.zh: 悉還其家。

translations.literal: All were sent back to their homes.
translations.idiomatic: He sent them all home.

sentences.zh: 及訊，則或舞文吏妄為註名，或誤報，或續完，悉原而釋之，保全者五百家。

translations.literal: When interrogated, some proved to be clerks fiddling with documents and falsely adding names, some mistaken reports, some who had since paid in full—all were pardoned and released; five hundred households were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Upon investigation some cases proved to be false names inserted by scheming clerks, mistaken reports, or debts already paid off. He pardoned and released them all, saving five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 河南優人硃虎山，遊食太和，髮長數寸，土猾範之諫與昝姓有隙，誣以藏匿故明宗室謀不軌。

translations.literal: Zhu Hushan, an actor from Henan, wandered for a living in Taihe; his hair was several inches long. A local rogue Fan Zhijian bore a grudge against the Zan clan and falsely accused them of harboring a Ming imperial clansman plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hushan, an actor from Henan who wandered Taihe for his living with hair cropped to a few inches, became entangled when a local rogue named Fan Zhijian, who bore a grudge against the Zan clan, falsely accused them of sheltering a Ming imperial clansman and plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 事發，江寧推官不敢問，以委貞麟，貞麟力白其誣。

translations.literal: When the matter broke, the Jiangning reviewing officer dared not investigate and entrusted it to Zhenlin; Zhenlin vigorously cleared the false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: When the case broke, the reviewing officer in Jiangning dared not touch it and handed it to Zhenlin, who vigorously proved the accusation false.

sentences.zh: 逮至京師复勘，刑鞫無異，乃釋昝姓而治之諫罪。

translations.literal: Brought to the capital and reinvestigated; under judicial interrogation nothing differed—then the Zan clan was released and Zhijian was punished for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: The case was sent to the capital for a second investigation; judicial interrogation yielded the same conclusion, and the Zans were released while Zhijian was punished.

sentences.zh: 潁州民吳月以邪教惑眾，株連千餘人，貞麟勘多愚民無知，止坐月及為首者。

translations.literal: Wu Yue of Yingzhou misled the masses with heterodox teaching; over a thousand were implicated. Zhenlin investigated and found most were ignorant commoners; only Yue and the ringleaders were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yue of Yingzhou led people astray with heterodox teachings, implicating more than a thousand. Zhenlin found most were ignorant commoners and punished only Yue and the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 捕人索財於水姓，不得，指為月黨，追至新蔡殺之。

translations.literal: Constables demanded money from the Shui clan and did not get it; they denounced them as Yue's party, pursued them to Xincai, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Constables tried to extort the Shui clan, failed, declared them members of Yue's sect, chased them to Xincai, and killed them.

sentences.zh: 鄉人來救，並誣為月黨。

translations.literal: Villagers came to the rescue and were also denounced as Yue's party.
translations.idiomatic: When villagers came to their aid, they too were branded as Yue's followers.

sentences.zh: 撫鎮發兵圍之，係其眾至鳳陽。

translations.literal: The provincial governor and garrison commander sent troops to surround them and brought the crowd bound to Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial governor and garrison commander sent troops to surround them and marched the prisoners in bonds to Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 貞麟廉得實，懲捕而盡釋新蔡鄉人。

translations.literal: Zhenlin investigated and got the truth; he punished the constables and released all the Xincai villagers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenlin investigated and learned the truth, punished the constables, and released every villager from Xincai.

sentences.zh: 其理枉活人類如此。

translations.literal: His manner of righting wrongs and saving lives was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: This was typical of how he righted injustice and saved lives.

sentences.zh: 旋以他事解官，得白。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed on another matter, but was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed over another matter but was ultimately exonerated.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，改授直隸鹽山知縣，地瘠而多盜，立法牌甲互相救護。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi, reassigned as magistrate of Yanshan in Zhili; the land was barren and bandits many; he enacted regulations for paijia mutual rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kangxi (1670), he was reassigned as magistrate of Yanshan in Zhili. The district was poor and plagued by bandits, so he instituted a paijia system for mutual protection.

sentences.zh: 有警，一村中半守半援，盜日以息。

translations.literal: When alarm arose, half a village would stand guard and half would reinforce; bandits daily diminished.
translations.idiomatic: When alarm sounded, half a village would stand guard while the other half came to help, and banditry steadily declined.

sentences.zh: 清裡役，逃亡者悉與豁除，不期年，流民復業數百家。

translations.literal: He cleared corvée levies; all fugitives were exempted; within less than a year, several hundred refugee households returned to their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: He cleaned up corvée rolls, exempted all who had fled, and within a year several hundred refugee households returned to work.

sentences.zh: 十二年，旱，謂父老曰：「大吏使勘災者至，供給惟官是責，不費民一錢。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, drought; he told the elders: "When the superior's disaster-inspection envoy arrives, provisioning is solely the magistrate's responsibility—not one coin from the people."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1673), during a drought, he told the village elders, "When the superior's disaster-inspection envoy arrives, I alone am responsible for their provisioning—not one coin shall come from you.

sentences.zh: 及秋徵，吏仍以舊額進。

translations.literal: When autumn collection came, clerks still submitted the old quota.
translations.idiomatic: When autumn tax collection arrived, the clerks still reported the full old quota.

sentences.zh: 貞麟曰：「下輸上易，上反下難。

translations.literal: Zhenlin said: "Delivering payment upward is easy; returning payment downward is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenlin said, "Collecting from the people and paying upward is easy; returning funds downward is hard.

sentences.zh: 待準蠲而還之，反覆間民必受損。」

translations.literal: If one waits for approved remission before returning it, in the back-and-forth the people will surely suffer loss."
translations.idiomatic: If we wait for official approval of a remission before refunding them, the delays will only hurt the people.

sentences.zh: 立令除之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered the reduction.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the reduction at once.

sentences.zh: 又永革雜派陋例，民皆感惠。

translations.literal: He also permanently abolished miscellaneous levies and shabby precedents; the people all felt his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He also abolished for good the miscellaneous surcharges and abusive local fees, and the people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 內擢戶部山西司主事，山西聞喜丁徭重，力請減之。

translations.literal: Promoted internally to secretary in the Shanxi Bureau of the Board of Revenue; Wenxi in Shanxi had heavy corvée—he vigorously petitioned to reduce it.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretary in the Shanxi Bureau of the Board of Revenue and vigorously petitioned to reduce the heavy corvée burden in Wenxi, Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 監督京左、右翼倉，因失察侵盜罷職，卒於家。

translations.literal: He supervised the left and right wing granaries of the capital; for failure to detect embezzlement he was dismissed from office, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising the capital's left and right wing granaries he was dismissed for failing to detect embezzlement, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 駱鍾麟，字挺生，浙江臨安人。

translations.literal: Luo Zhonglin, styled Tingsheng, a native of Lin'an in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zhonglin, styled Tingsheng, was a native of Lin'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治四年進士副榜，授安吉學正。

translations.literal: A supplemental jinshi of the fourth year of Shunzhi; appointed district instructor of Anji.
translations.idiomatic: He placed on the supplemental jinshi list in the fourth year of Shunzhi (1647) and was appointed district instructor of Anji.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷陝西盩厔知縣。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, transferred to magistrate of Zhouzhi in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi (1659), he was transferred to magistrate of Zhouzhi in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 為政先教化，春秋大會明倫堂，進諸生迪以仁義忠信之道。

translations.literal: In governance he put moral instruction first; in spring and autumn he held great assemblies in the Minglun Hall, advancing students and instructing them in the Way of benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and faith.
translations.idiomatic: He put moral instruction first in government. Each spring and autumn he gathered students in the Minglun Hall to teach them benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and good faith.

sentences.zh: 增刪呂氏士約，頒學舍。

translations.literal: He revised and abridged Master Lu's Scholars' Covenant and distributed it in the schoolhouses.
translations.idiomatic: He edited Master Lu's Scholars' Covenant and distributed it in the schoolhouses.

sentences.zh: 朔望詣里社講演，訪耆年有德、孝弟著聞者，見與鈞禮，歲時勞以粟肉。

translations.literal: On the new and full moons he went to village altars to lecture; he sought out venerable men of virtue famed for filial piety and brotherliness, received them with equal courtesy, and at year's end rewarded them with grain and meat.
translations.idiomatic: On the first and fifteenth of each month he lectured at village altars, sought out elders famed for virtue and filial piety, treated them as equals, and rewarded them with grain and meat at year's end.

sentences.zh: 立學社，擇民間子弟授以小學、孝經。

translations.literal: He founded study societies and selected boys from among the people to teach them the Elementary Learning and the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: He founded study societies and selected village boys to instruct in the Elementary Learning and the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 飭保伍，修社倉。

translations.literal: He tightened the baowu system and repaired community granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened the mutual-responsibility system and repaired community granaries.

sentences.zh: 蒞獄明決，所案治即勢豪居間莫能奪，人畏而愛之。

translations.literal: Presiding over cases he was clear and decisive; cases he tried could not be swayed even when powerful families intervened; people both feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over cases with clarity and firmness; not even powerful families could sway his judgments, and the people feared and loved him in equal measure.

sentences.zh: 縣城去渭不十里，鍾麟行河畔，知水勢將南浸，議自覽家寨迤東開復故道，眾難之。

translations.literal: The county seat was less than ten li from the Wei River; Zhonglin walked the riverbank, knew the water would soon encroach south, and proposed opening the old channel from east of Lanjiatun—but the crowd opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: The county seat lay less than ten li from the Wei River. Walking the bank, Zhonglin saw that the water would soon flood southward and proposed reopening the old channel east of Lanjiatun, but the people objected.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年夏，大雨，渭南溢，且及城，齋沐臨禱，自跪水中，幸雨止，水頓減，徙而北流者數里。

translations.literal: Summer of the first year of Kangxi, great rain; south of the Wei flooded, reaching nearly the city walls; he bathed and prayed, knelt in the water himself; fortunately rain ceased; water suddenly diminished and shifted to flow north for several li.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Kangxi 1 (1662), heavy rains made the Wei overflow southward almost to the city walls. He bathed, prayed, and knelt in the floodwaters. Rain stopped, the waters fell sharply, and the current shifted north for several li.

sentences.zh: 兼攝興平、鄠兩縣，興平豪右分為部黨，前令不能治，廉得其狀，收案以法。

translations.literal: He concurrently held Xingping and Hu counties; Xingping's powerful families had split into factions; previous magistrates could not control them; he investigated and got the facts, seized cases and handled by law.
translations.idiomatic: While also acting for Xingping and Hu counties, he found Xingping's gentry split into rival factions that previous magistrates had failed to break up. He investigated thoroughly and prosecuted them by law.

sentences.zh: 奏最，內遷北城兵馬司指揮，復出為西安府同知。

translations.literal: Reported top performance; promoted internally to commander of the North City Horse-and-Firearms Office; later went out again as vice-prefect of Xi'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a top evaluation he was promoted to commander of the North City Horse-and-Firearms Office, then returned to the field as vice-prefect of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢江南常州知府。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, promoted to prefect of Changzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kangxi (1669), he was promoted to prefect of Changzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 常州、縣賦重，科條繁多，吏緣為奸。

translations.literal: Changzhou's prefectural and county taxes were heavy, regulations numerous; clerks used them as pretext for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou and its counties bore heavy taxes under a tangle of regulations that clerks exploited for profit.

sentences.zh: 鍾麟立法鉤稽清逋，吏受成事而已。

translations.literal: Zhonglin enacted laws for audit and clearing arrears; clerks had only to receive completed work.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglin created audit rules to clear tax arrears, leaving clerks with nothing to manipulate.

sentences.zh: 屬邑歲例餽漕羨三千金，鍾麟曰：「利若金，如吾民何？」

translations.literal: Subordinate counties yearly customarily presented three thousand taels of grain-transport surplus; Zhonglin said: "If profit is measured in gold, what of our people?"
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate counties annually offered three thousand taels in grain-transport surplus. Zhonglin said, "If we treat profit as gold, what becomes of my people?

sentences.zh: 峻卻之。

translations.literal: He sternly refused.
translations.idiomatic: He refused them flatly.

sentences.zh: 諸漕卒咸斂手奉法。

translations.literal: All grain-boat soldiers folded their hands and obeyed the law.
translations.idiomatic: The grain-transport workers all kept their hands clean and obeyed the law.

sentences.zh: 初，鍾麟在盩厔以師禮數造李顒廬，至是創延陵書院，迎顒講學，率僚屬及薦紳學士北面聽。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhonglin was in Zhouzhi, he repeatedly visited Li Yong's hut as to a teacher; now he founded Yanling Academy, welcomed Yong to lecture, and led subordinates and gentry scholars to listen facing north.
translations.idiomatic: While magistrate of Zhouzhi he had often visited Li Yong's cottage as a disciple. Now he founded Yanling Academy, invited Yong to lecture, and led his staff and local scholars to sit as pupils facing north.

sentences.zh: 問為學之要，顒曰：「天下之治亂在人心，人心之邪正在學術。

translations.literal: Asked the essentials of learning, Yong said: "The order and disorder of all under Heaven lie in the human heart; the right and wrong of the human heart lie in scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: When asked the heart of learning, Yong said, "The rise and fall of the realm depends on the human heart, and whether the heart turns good or evil depends on learning.

sentences.zh: ​​人心正，風俗移，治道畢矣。」

translations.literal: When hearts are upright, customs change, and the way of governance is complete."
translations.idiomatic: When hearts are set right, customs follow, and good government is achieved.

sentences.zh: 鍾麟書其言，終身誦之。

translations.literal: Zhonglin wrote down his words and recited them all his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglin copied down these words and recited them for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 已而江陰、靖江、無錫諸有司爭禮致顒，顒為發明性善之旨，格物致知之說，士林蒸蒸向風，吏治亦和。

translations.literal: Before long officials of Jiangyin, Jingjiang, Wuxi and elsewhere competed to honor and invite Yong; Yong expounded the intent of innate goodness and the doctrine of investigating things to extend knowledge; the scholarly world steamed toward the trend, and official governance also harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Soon officials in Jiangyin, Jingjiang, Wuxi, and elsewhere vied to host Yong. He expounded the doctrine of innate moral goodness and investigation of things to extend knowledge. Scholars flocked to his teaching and local governance grew more harmonious.

sentences.zh: 九年，大水，發倉廩，勸富人出粟賑，民無荒亡。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, great flood; opened granaries, urged the wealthy to give grain for relief—the people had none who perished of famine.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1670), after great floods he opened the granaries, urged the wealthy to contribute grain, and no one died of famine.

sentences.zh: 十年夏，大旱，葛衣草履，步禱不應，責躬籥天，言知府不德累民，涕泣並下。

translations.literal: Tenth year summer, great drought; in hemp robe and straw sandals he walked praying without response; blaming himself he locked the city gates and appealed to Heaven, saying the prefect's lack of virtue harmed the people—tears streaming down.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth summer (1671), during severe drought he prayed in hemp and straw sandals. When rain did not come he fastened the city gates, blamed himself before Heaven for failing the people as prefect, and wept openly.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，士民乞留，不可。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his mother; gentry and people begged him to stay—it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning for his mother; gentry and commoners begged him to stay, but he could not.

sentences.zh: 既歸，連遭父喪，以毀卒。

translations.literal: After returning home, he suffered his father's death in succession and died from grief-exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he suffered his father's death in quick succession and died from overwhelming grief.

sentences.zh: 郡人論賢有司知治體必首推鍾麟。

translations.literal: When people of the prefecture discuss worthy officials who understand governance, Zhonglin is always placed first.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of the prefecture speak of worthy officials who truly grasp governance, Zhonglin is always named first.

sentences.zh: 先鍾麟守常州者，祖重光、崔宗泰，皆有名。

translations.literal: Before Zhonglin governed Changzhou, Zu Chongguang and Cui Zongtai had each been renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhonglin governed Changzhou, Zu Chongguang and Cui Zongtai had each earned renown there.

sentences.zh: 其後有祖進朝，政聲尤著。

translations.literal: Afterward there was Zu Jinchao, whose reputation for governance was especially outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Zu Jinchao, whose reputation for governance was especially outstanding.

sentences.zh: 重光官至天津巡撫。

translations.literal: Chongguang's highest office was governor of Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Chongguang rose to governor of Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 宗泰，奉天人。

translations.literal: Zongtai was a native of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtai was a native of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 順治初，授松江府同知，以敏幹稱。

translations.literal: In early Shunzhi, appointed vice-prefect of Songjiang Prefecture; known for alert efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shunzhi he was appointed vice-prefect of Songjiang and was known for his sharp efficiency.

sentences.zh: 擢常州知府，政尚嚴厲，善鉤距，吏民驚為神明。

translations.literal: Promoted to prefect of Changzhou; governance emphasized severity; skilled at detection; officials and people marveled at him as divine.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to prefect of Changzhou, he governed with stern discipline, excelled at investigative methods, and officials and people alike regarded him with awe.

sentences.zh: 十三年，大兵徵閩，過郡久駐，人情恇擾，宗泰先期儲偫，纖悉備具。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the great army marched to conquer Fujian and lingered long in the prefecture; public sentiment was alarmed; Zongtai stored provisions in advance down to the finest detail.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi (1656), as the army marched on Fujian and lingered in the prefecture, Zongtai foresaw the panic and stored provisions in meticulous advance.

sentences.zh: 有遊騎入村落，逐婦女溺水死，宗泰夜叩營門，白將軍縛置之法。

translations.literal: Straggling cavalry entered a village, chased a woman who drowned; Zongtai knocked on the camp gate at night, reported to the general, who bound the man and punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: When straggling cavalry entered a village, chased a woman into the river, and drowned her, Zongtai went to the camp gate at night, reported to the general, and had the man bound and executed.

sentences.zh: 時時單騎巡行，遇小有剽奪，隸傳呼「崔太守來」，皆引避去，民得安堵。

translations.literal: From time to time he patrolled alone on horseback; when small robberies occurred, runners shouted "Prefect Cui comes!"—all withdrew and fled; the people could live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: He often patrolled alone on horseback; at the slightest robbery his runners would shout "Prefect Cui is coming!" and the culprits would scatter, so the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 令甲，府漕以推官監兌，推官懦而衛弁橫。

translations.literal: By regulation, prefectural grain transport was supervised by the reviewing officer, but the reviewing officer was timid while military ensigns were overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation the reviewing officer supervised grain transport for the prefecture, but the officer was timid while military ensigns threw their weight around.

sentences.zh: 宗泰自請於漕督，檄之監兌，盛騶從，帶刀鞬建臨倉，弁卒悚懼，竟事無譁。

translations.literal: Zongtai volunteered to the grain-transport superintendent, who commissioned him to supervise exchange; with grand escort, sword and bow at belt he arrived at the granary; officers and soldiers were fearful; the affair ended without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtai volunteered to the grain-transport superintendent to take over supervision himself. He arrived at the granary with a large escort, sword and bow at his belt; the soldiers were terrified and the exchange passed without incident.

sentences.zh: 尋以事左遷福建延平府同知。

translations.literal: Soon on account of an affair he was demoted and transferred to vice-prefect of Yanping in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon demoted to vice-prefect of Yanping in Fujian over another matter.

sentences.zh: 後乞免歸。

translations.literal: Later he requested dismissal and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked to be relieved and returned home.

sentences.zh: 進朝，亦奉天人。

translations.literal: Jinchao was also a native of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Jinchao was also a native of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 以廕監起家。

translations.literal: He began his career through hereditary yin privilege as a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through hereditary yin privilege as an Imperial Academy student.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十三年，由部郎擢授常州知府，有惠政，以失察鐫級去，士民呼籥於巡撫湯斌，請留進朝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kangxi, from department secretary promoted and appointed prefect of Changzhou; had benevolent policies; for failure to detect, reduced in rank and removed; gentry and people clamored before Governor Tang Bin, asking to retain Jinchao.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 23 (1684) he was promoted from a ministry post to prefect of Changzhou, where he won the people's trust. Reduced in rank for a supervisory failure, gentry and commoners clamored before Governor Tang Bin to keep him.

sentences.zh: 斌上疏言：「進朝履任未一載，操守廉、治事勤，臣私心重之。

translations.literal: Bin memorialized: "Jinchao has held office less than a year; integrity in conduct, diligence in affairs—I personally hold him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Bin memorialized: "Jinchao has served less than a year. His conduct is upright and his work diligent, and I hold him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 頃緣失察法寶事降調，常州五縣士民輒號泣罷市，赴臣請留，日不下數千人。

translations.literal: Recently for failure to detect the Fabao affair he was demoted; the five counties of Changzhou—gentry and people at once wept and closed markets, came to me pleading retention, no fewer than several thousand per day.
translations.idiomatic: He was recently demoted for failing to detect the Fabao affair. Gentry and commoners in all five Changzhou counties wept, shut their shops, and came to me by the thousands each day to beg that he stay.

sentences.zh: 臣諭以保留例已久停，士民謂常州四十年未有愛民如進朝者，其減繇輕耗，興學正俗，戢姦除暴，息訟安民，窮鄉僻壤，盡沾惠澤。

translations.literal: I explained that the retention precedent had long been suspended; gentry and people said in forty years Changzhou had never had one who loved the people like Jinchao—reducing corvée, lightening surcharges, promoting schools and correcting customs, restraining villains and removing violence, settling lawsuits and pacifying people—even remote hamlets were fully bathed in grace.
translations.idiomatic: I told them the precedent for retaining an official had long been suspended. They replied that in forty years Changzhou had never seen an official who loved the people as Jinchao did—cutting corvée, easing surcharges, promoting schools, correcting customs, suppressing criminals, settling lawsuits, bringing peace to the people—and that even the remotest villages had felt his kindness.

sentences.zh: 朝廷軫念東南，如江寧府知府於成龍，特恩超擢，吏治丕變。

translations.literal: The court showed concern for the southeast—as with Yu Chenglong, prefect of Jiangning, specially favored with exceptional promotion—official governance greatly changed.
translations.idiomatic: The court has shown special concern for the southeast, as when Yu Chenglong, prefect of Jiangning, was exceptionally promoted and local governance was transformed.

sentences.zh: 進朝操守才幹可與成龍頡頏，而獨以一眚被謫，士民攀留，言之泣下，臣不知進朝何以感人之深如此。

translations.literal: Jinchao's integrity and talent can match Chenglong's, yet for a single fault he was demoted; gentry and people cling to retain him, speaking through tears—I do not know how Jinchao moves people so deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Jinchao's integrity and ability can stand beside Chenglong's, yet for one fault he was demoted. The people plead to keep him with tears streaming down. I cannot fathom how he has touched them so deeply.

sentences.zh: 臣受事四日始獲法寶，是受事之日，已為失察之日，且當候處分，何敢代人凟奏？

translations.literal: I received office only four days before capturing Fabao—thus the day I assumed office was already the day of failure to detect; moreover I await disposition—how dare I memorialize on another's behalf?
translations.idiomatic: I had held office only four days when Fabao was captured, so my very first day in office was already a day of failure to detect. I await my own disposition—how dare I plead another's case?

sentences.zh: 惟臣蒙恩簡畀封疆大任，屬吏之敗檢者得糾劾之，廉能者不能為之一言，非公也。

translations.literal: Yet I have received grace and been appointed to a great frontier charge—subordinates who breach conduct may be impeached; if the upright and able cannot be spoken for in one word, that is not public-minded.
translations.idiomatic: Yet having been entrusted with a great provincial charge, if I can impeach officials who breach conduct but cannot speak one word for the upright and able, I would not be serving the public good.

sentences.zh: 民情皇皇如是，而不為之解慰安輯，非仁也。

translations.literal: The people's sentiment is so anxious—if I do not soothe and settle them, that is not benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The people are so anxious; if I do not soothe and reassure them, I would fail in benevolence.

sentences.zh: 畏罪緘默而使輿情不上聞，非忠也。

translations.literal: Fearing guilt and keeping silent so public sentiment does not reach the throne—that is not loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: If I stay silent for fear of punishment and keep public sentiment from reaching the throne, I would fail in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 敢據情陳奏。」

translations.literal: I dare report according to the facts."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore dare report the facts as I have found them.

sentences.zh: 章下部議，格不行。

translations.literal: The memorial went to the ministry for deliberation; it was blocked and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministry for deliberation and was blocked.

sentences.zh: 聖祖諭曰：「設官原以養民，湯斌保奏祖進朝清廉，百姓同聲懇留，可從所請，以勸廉吏。」

translations.literal: The Sage Ancestor decreed: "Offices are originally established to nourish the people; Tang Bin recommends Zu Jinchao as incorrupt; the common people unite in earnest pleas to retain him—his request may be granted, to encourage upright officials."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor decreed: "Offices exist to nourish the people. Tang Bin vouches for Zu Jinchao's integrity, and the people united in pleading to keep him. Grant their request to encourage upright officials.

sentences.zh: 進朝復任。

translations.literal: Jinchao resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: Jinchao resumed his post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以老疾乞免，民恆思之不置云。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of age and illness he requested release; the people constantly thought of him without end.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked to retire on account of age and illness; the people never ceased to miss him.

sentences.zh: 趙吉士，字天羽，安徽休寧人，寄籍杭州。

translations.literal: Zhao Jishi, courtesy name Tianyu, was a native of Xiuning, Anhui; his registered residence was Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jishi, styled Tianyu, came from Xiuning in Anhui but was registered as a resident of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 順治八年舉人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shunzhi he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the eighth year of the Shunzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，授山西交城知縣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi, he was appointed magistrate of Jiaocheng, Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Jiaocheng in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 縣居萬山中，地產馬，饒灌木，時禁民間牧馬，停南堡村木廠，民困，往往去為盜。

translations.literal: The county lay amid myriad mountains; the land produced horses and abounded in scrub; at the time common folk herding horses was forbidden and the timber mill at Nanbao Village was shut down; the people were distressed and often turned to banditry.
translations.idiomatic: The county sat deep in the mountains, where horses were raised and scrubland was plentiful. The government had banned common grazing and closed the timber mill at Nanbao Village; driven to hardship, many people turned to banditry.

sentences.zh: 武弁路時運貪而擾民，民殺時運作亂，與大同叛將薑瓖合，連破諸邑。

translations.literal: The military officer Lu Shiyun was greedy and harassed the people; the people killed Shiyun and rose in revolt, joining with the Datong rebel general Jiang Rang, and in succession overran various districts.
translations.idiomatic: The army officer Lu Shiyun was greedy and oppressive; the people killed him and rose in rebellion, joining forces with the Datong rebel general Jiang Rang to overrun one district after another.

sentences.zh: 及瓖誅，餘盜匿山中。

translations.literal: When Rang was executed, the remaining bandits hid in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiang Rang was put to death, the surviving bandits took refuge in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 吉士到官，定先撫後剿之策，有投撫者，給示令招其黨。

translations.literal: When Jishi took office, he fixed on a strategy of pacifying first and then suppressing; those who surrendered to pacification were given proclamations ordering them to summon their comrades.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office, Jishi adopted a policy of offering amnesty before resorting to force. Those who surrendered received written orders to bring in their fellow bandits.

sentences.zh: 诇知群盜陰事，選鄉兵，得技優者百人。

translations.literal: Having spied out the bandits' secret affairs, he selected local militia and obtained a hundred of the most skilled.
translations.idiomatic: Through reconnaissance he learned the bandits' secret movements, then recruited a hundred of the most capable local militiamen.

sentences.zh: 令紳戶家出一丁，與民均役。

translations.literal: He ordered each gentry household to contribute one male, sharing corvée labor equally with the common people.
translations.idiomatic: He required every gentry household to supply one man, so that the elite shared corvée duties with the common people.

sentences.zh: 分夕巡城，行保甲法，匿賊者連坐，鄰盜相戒不入境。

translations.literal: He divided night patrols of the city, implemented the baojia system, punished concealment of bandits by collective liability, and neighboring bandits warned one another not to enter the county.
translations.idiomatic: He organized night patrols around the city, enforced the baojia system of mutual accountability, and made those who hid bandits liable together with them; neighboring bandits warned one another to stay out of the county.

sentences.zh: 時交城多抗賦，河北都者賦倍他都。

translations.literal: At the time Jiaocheng had many who resisted tax payment; the Hebei district's levy doubled that of other districts.
translations.idiomatic: Many in Jiaocheng resisted paying taxes at the time, and the Hebei district's assessment was twice that of every other district.

sentences.zh: 吉士往諭朝廷德意，勗以力耕勿為盜，眾悚息。

translations.literal: Jishi went to expound the court's benevolent intent, urging them to labor at farming and not become bandits; the crowd trembled into silence.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi went in person to explain the court's benevolent intentions and urged the people to farm diligently rather than turn to banditry; they were awed into submission.

sentences.zh: 日暮寢陶穴中聽訟，左右多賊黨，吉士陽若勿知，詰朝深入，察其形勢。

translations.literal: At dusk he lodged in a pottery cave to hear lawsuits; many about him were bandit partisans—Jishi feigned ignorance; the next morning he penetrated deeply and examined the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he took lodgings in a pottery cave to hear lawsuits, surrounded by many bandit sympathizers; Jishi pretended not to notice. The next morning he pressed deep into the hills and studied the terrain.

sentences.zh: 最險者曰三坐崖，東西兩葫蘆川繞其下。

translations.literal: The most perilous spot was called Sansuoya; the eastern and western Hulugou streams wound below it.
translations.idiomatic: The most formidable position was Sansuoya Cliff, with the eastern and western Hulugou valleys winding beneath it.

sentences.zh: 塞葫蘆口，則官軍不得登。

translations.literal: If the mouths of the Hulugou were blocked, government troops could not ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Block the mouths of the Hulugou valleys and government troops could not climb up at all.

sentences.zh: 吉士默識之而還。

translations.literal: Jishi silently memorized this and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi filed the layout away in memory and returned.

sentences.zh: 交山賊楊芳林、芳清等時出肆掠，九年春，吉士入山勸農，撫姜瓖舊卒惠崇德，詢得二楊所在，命二卒立擒至，杖系之。

translations.literal: Bandits of Jiaoshan, Yang Fanglin, Fangqing, and others often sallied forth to plunder; in the spring of the ninth year, Jishi entered the mountains to encourage farming, pacified Jiang Rang's former soldier Hui Chongde, inquired where the two Yangs were, ordered the two soldiers immediately to seize them and bring them in, and had them flogged and bound.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaoshan bandits Yang Fanglin, Yang Fangqing, and others frequently raided the countryside. In the spring of the ninth year Jishi entered the hills to promote farming, won over Hui Chongde, a former soldier of Jiang Rang, learned where the two Yangs were hiding, and had the two men seize them at once, flog them, and bind them.

sentences.zh: 賊渠任國鉉、鍾斗等糾眾尾之不敢發。

translations.literal: Bandit chiefs Ren Guoxuan, Zhong Dou, and others gathered a crowd and followed behind but did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit leaders Ren Guoxuan, Zhong Dou, and their followers trailed behind but did not dare strike.

sentences.zh: 會有陝西叛弁黃某入葫蘆川與國鉉合，吉士謀間之，遣山民持書付國鉉等，偽誤投黃所，黃得書疑國鉉等，率眾去。

translations.literal: It happened that a Shaanxi rebel officer surnamed Huang entered Hulugou and joined with Guoxuan; Jishi plotted to drive them apart, sent a hill dweller bearing a letter intended for Guoxuan and the rest, feigned mistaken delivery to Huang's camp; Huang received the letter and suspected Guoxuan and the rest, and led his crowd away.
translations.idiomatic: A Shaanxi rebel officer surnamed Huang had meanwhile entered Hulugou and joined Ren Guoxuan. Jishi set out to divide them: he sent a hill villager with a letter meant for Ren Guoxuan and his men, but had it deliberately misdelivered to Huang. Huang read the letter, grew suspicious of Ren's group, and marched away with his followers.

sentences.zh: 國鉉等既失黃弁，無所恃，有投誠意。

translations.literal: Guoxuan and the rest, having lost the officer Huang, had nothing to rely on and showed willingness to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Deprived of Officer Huang's support, Ren Guoxuan and his men had no one to rely on and began to show a willingness to surrender.

sentences.zh: 靜樂盜李宗盛踞周洪山，遣其黨趙應龍劫清源，吉士遣惠崇德入山說國鉉等，令獻趙應龍可免罪。

translations.literal: The Jingyue bandit Li Zongsheng held Zhouhongshan and sent his partisan Zhao Yinglong to raid Qingyuan; Jishi sent Hui Chongde into the mountains to persuade Guoxuan and the rest, offering that if they delivered Zhao Yinglong their crimes could be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingyue bandit Li Zongsheng held Zhouhong Mountain and sent his henchman Zhao Yinglong to raid Qingyuan. Jishi dispatched Hui Chongde into the hills to persuade Ren Guoxuan and his men that surrendering Zhao Yinglong would win them pardon.

sentences.zh: 國鉉與宗盛紿應龍縛付崇德，應龍恨為所賣，盡發諸盜陰謀。

translations.literal: Guoxuan and Zongsheng deceived Yinglong, bound him, and handed him to Chongde; Yinglong, resenting being sold out, fully disclosed the bandits' secret plots.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Guoxuan and Li Zongsheng tricked Zhao Yinglong, bound him, and turned him over to Chongde. Enraged at being betrayed, Zhao Yinglong revealed every secret plot of the bandits.

sentences.zh: 吉士會兵剿宗盛，復遣崇德往說國鉉等使無動，遂擒宗盛，賊黨益渙。

translations.literal: Jishi gathered troops to suppress Zongsheng, again sent Chongde to persuade Guoxuan and the rest to keep still, thereby seized Zongsheng, and the bandit partisans grew ever more scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi assembled troops to hunt down Li Zongsheng, sent Chongde again to hold Ren Guoxuan's group in check, and captured Zongsheng; the bandit factions grew ever more fragmented.

sentences.zh: 十年，廷旨下總督治群盜，期盡剿絕。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, a court edict descended on the governor-general to deal with the bandit gangs, fixing a deadline to wipe them out entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the court ordered the governor-general to suppress the bandit gangs and wipe them out completely by a set deadline.

sentences.zh: 吉士曰：「交山劇賊不過十餘人，其它率烏合，一聞盡剿，恐山中向化之民畏罪自疑，反為賊用。

translations.literal: Jishi said: "The ringleaders of Jiaoshan number no more than ten-odd men; the rest are mostly a rabble assembled in a mob. Once they hear of total extermination, I fear the mountain people who have turned toward civilization will fear guilt and grow suspicious of themselves, and be turned instead to serve the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi said: "The hard-core bandits of Jiaoshan number barely a dozen; the rest are mere rabble. If word spreads of a policy of total extermination, the hill people who have begun to settle down may fear punishment, lose heart, and end up serving the bandits instead.

sentences.zh: 今靖安堡初复，請協兵三百以駐防為名，剋期入山，可一戰擒也。」

translations.literal: Now that Jing'an Fort has just been restored, I request three hundred auxiliary troops under the pretext of garrison duty; then on the fixed day enter the mountains and they can be captured in one battle."
translations.idiomatic: Jing'an Fort has only just been rebuilt. Request three hundred auxiliary troops under the pretext of garrison duty, and on the appointed day we can enter the hills and take them in a single strike.

sentences.zh: 靖安堡者，近葫蘆口三十里，昔以屯兵，吉士就廢壘新築之。

translations.literal: Jing'an Fort lay thirty li from Hulukou; formerly used to station troops, Jishi newly built it upon the ruined ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'an Fort stood thirty li from Hulukou. Once a military garrison, it had been rebuilt by Jishi on its ruined foundations.

sentences.zh: 守備姚順率兵至縣，吉士約期進屯。

translations.literal: The garrison commandant Yao Shun led troops to the county; Jishi fixed a date to advance and encamp.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commandant Yao Shun marched his troops to the county, and Jishi set a date for them to move in and encamp.

sentences.zh: 先期七日置酒大享客，夜半，席未散，吉士上馬會師，疾驅四十里至水泉灘。

translations.literal: Seven days before the appointed day he set out wine and lavishly entertained guests; at midnight, before the feast had broken up, Jishi mounted and joined forces, galloping forty li to Shuiquan Beach.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days before the scheduled date he threw a grand banquet for his guests. At midnight, while the feast was still in full swing, Jishi mounted his horse, joined his forces, and raced forty li to Shuiquan Beach.

sentences.zh: 分三隊，一襲東葫蘆，一襲西葫蘆，自偕姚順進駐東坡底，為兩葫蘆要道。

translations.literal: He divided into three columns—one to strike eastern Hulugou, one western Hulugou—and himself with Yao Shun advanced to occupy Dongpodi, the key pass between the two Hulugou.
translations.idiomatic: He split his force into three columns: one to strike the eastern Hulugou, one the western, while he and Yao Shun took up position at Dongpodi, the choke point between the two valleys.

sentences.zh: 東西賊援並絕，國鉉等為內應，呼曰：「官兵入山矣！」

translations.literal: Bandit reinforcements east and west were both cut off; Guoxuan and the rest served as inner collaborators, shouting: "Government troops have entered the mountains!"
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements from east and west were cut off. Ren Guoxuan and his men acted as insiders, shouting: "The government troops are in the mountains!

sentences.zh: 兩葫蘆賊皆走上三坐崖。

translations.literal: The bandits of both Hulugou all fled up to Sansuoya.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits in both Hulugou valleys fled up toward Sansuoya Cliff.

sentences.zh: 吉士遣人至崖下語之曰：「汝等良民，毋為賊脅，官且按戶稽丁，不在即以賊論。」

translations.literal: Jishi sent men to the cliff base to tell them: "You are good common people—do not let bandits coerce you. The government will soon check households and register males; those absent will be treated as bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Jishi sent men to the foot of the cliff to call out: "You are honest folk—do not let the bandits drag you down. The magistrate will soon check each household and register every able-bodied man; anyone absent will be counted a bandit.

sentences.zh: 眾乃稍稍去，僅存二百餘人。

translations.literal: The crowd then gradually dispersed; only slightly over two hundred remained.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd thinned out until barely two hundred people remained.

sentences.zh: 分兵要賊去路，賊四竄，被獲頗眾。

translations.literal: He divided troops to block the bandits' escape routes; the bandits fled in all directions and many were captured.
translations.idiomatic: He posted troops to cut off the bandits' escape routes; they scattered in every direction, and a great many were captured.

sentences.zh: 分搜巢穴，縱降賊，質其妻子，俾捕他賊以自贖。

translations.literal: He divided forces to search lairs, released surrendering bandits, held their wives and children hostage, and made them capture other bandits to redeem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He sent detachments to scour the hideouts, released surrendered bandits, held their families hostage, and made them hunt down other bandits to earn their freedom.

sentences.zh: 入山旬有六日，盜悉平。

translations.literal: Sixteen days after entering the mountains, banditry was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen days after entering the mountains, banditry was completely suppressed.

sentences.zh: 乃召山中民始終不附賊者三十七家，賚以羊酒，立為約正；

translations.literal: He then summoned thirty-seven hill households that from first to last had never joined the bandits, rewarded them with sheep and wine, and established them as pact heads;
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned thirty-seven mountain families that had never sided with the bandits, rewarded them with sheep and wine, and appointed them as local pact leaders;

sentences.zh: 其素不與徭役者千四百三十家，編其籍入都圖。

translations.literal: as for the fourteen hundred thirty households that had never shared corvée duties, he registered them on the rolls into district and ward maps.
translations.idiomatic: and registered the fourteen hundred and thirty households that had long evaded corvée duties on the district rolls.

sentences.zh: 自後交山無賊患。

translations.literal: From then on Jiaoshan had no bandit trouble.
translations.idiomatic: After that Jiaoshan knew no further bandit trouble.

sentences.zh: 吉士初患山路險阻，命每都具一圖，鱗比為大圖，召父老詢徑途曲折注之，以次及永寧、靜樂鄰縣諸山。

translations.literal: Jishi had initially worried about perilous mountain roads; he ordered each district to prepare a map, arranged them scale-like into a large map, summoned elders to inquire about winding paths and annotate them, extending in sequence to the mountains of neighboring Yongning and Jingyue counties.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi had worried from the start about the treacherous mountain roads. He ordered each district to produce a map, assembled them into one large chart, and summoned village elders to trace every winding path onto it, eventually extending the survey to the hills of the neighboring counties of Yongning and Jingyue.

sentences.zh: 每獲賊，善遇之，因得諸賊踪跡。

translations.literal: Whenever he captured bandits he treated them well and thereby learned the traces of the various bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he captured a bandit he treated him well, and so learned the whereabouts of the rest.

sentences.zh: 上官知其能，不拘以文法，用卒成功。

translations.literal: Superiors knew his ability and did not bind him with regulations; he succeeded at last.
translations.idiomatic: His superiors recognized his ability and did not hamper him with bureaucratic rules, allowing him to succeed in the end.

sentences.zh: 治交城五年，百廢俱舉，內遷戶部主事，監揚州鈔關，擢戶科給事中。

translations.literal: Governing Jiaocheng for five years, he revived a hundred neglected projects; transferred inward as a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, supervised the Yangzhou customs office, and was promoted to supervising censor in the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: After five years governing Jiaocheng, during which he restored every neglected project, he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue as a secretary, put in charge of the Yangzhou customs station, and promoted to supervising censor in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 忌者劾其父子異籍被黜，尋補國子監學正。

translations.literal: Envious parties impeached him for father and son holding different registrations and he was dismissed; soon after he was appointed an instructor at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Rivals impeached him for having a different registered residence from his father, and he was dismissed; he was soon appointed an instructor at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，卒，祀交城名宦祠。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he died and was sacrificed to in Jiaocheng's shrine of celebrated officials.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-fifth year and was enshrined in Jiaocheng's hall of celebrated officials.

sentences.zh: 張瑾，字去瑕，江南江都人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jin, courtesy name Quxia, was a native of Jiangdu, Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin, styled Quxia, came from Jiangdu in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年舉人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the second year of the Kangxi reign.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授雲南昆明知縣。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed magistrate of Kunming, Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was appointed magistrate of Kunming in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 時吳三桂初平，故軍衛田隸籓府者，徵租量豐歉收之，事平沿為額，民不能供。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Sangui had just been pacified; former military-guard fields subordinate to the princely establishment collected rent according to good or bad harvests; after pacification this became fixed quota, and the people could not meet it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui had only recently been suppressed. Farmland that had belonged to military garrisons under the princely establishment had been taxed according to the harvest, but after the rebellion this provisional rate was fixed as a permanent quota the people could not meet.

sentences.zh: 又軍興後官司府署器用皆裡下供應，而取給於縣，故昆明之徭，尤重於賦。

translations.literal: Moreover after the military campaigns, utensils for government offices and residences were all supplied by the lixia—the lowest administrative units—and these were requisitioned from the county; thus Kunming's corvée was even heavier than its land tax.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaigns, moreover, every utensil needed by government offices was supplied by local communities and charged to the county; corvée in Kunming weighed even more heavily on the people than the land tax.

sentences.zh: 瑾請於大吏，奏減其賦，不可；

translations.literal: Jin petitioned the grand officials to memorialize reducing the tax—it could not be done;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin petitioned the provincial authorities to memorialize for a tax reduction, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 乃疆畫荒地，招流亡，給牛種，薄其徵以濟軍衛之賦。

translations.literal: He then demarcated wasteland, recruited displaced persons, supplied oxen and seed, and lightened the levy to meet the military-guard tax.
