translations.idiomatic: He then surveyed wasteland, summoned back refugees, supplied oxen and seed, and set a lighter levy to help the people pay the military-guard tax.

sentences.zh: 一年墾田千三百餘畝，三年得萬餘畝。

translations.literal: In one year over thirteen hundred mu were opened; in three years he obtained over ten thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: In one year more than thirteen hundred mu were brought under cultivation; within three years the total exceeded ten thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 又均其徭，裡蠹無科派，奸民無包收，諸侵漁弊皆絕。

translations.literal: He also equalized corvée; li parasites had no assessed levies, wicked people had no wrap-collection, and all abuses of embezzlement were ended.
translations.idiomatic: He also equalized corvée obligations; village parasites could no longer levy unauthorized charges, corrupt middlemen could no longer collect fees, and every form of extortion was stamped out.

sentences.zh: 民舊供縣公費日十金，瑾曰：「吾食祿於君，不食傭於民。」

translations.literal: The people had formerly supplied the county public expense of ten taels per day; Jin said: "I eat salary from the sovereign—I do not eat wages from the people."
translations.idiomatic: The people had long paid ten taels of silver a day for county operating expenses. Zhang Jin said: "I draw my salary from the throne—I will not live off the people's labor.

sentences.zh: 革之。

translations.literal: He abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 總督曰：「陳仲子之廉，能理劇乎？」

translations.literal: The governor-general said: "The integrity of Chen Zhongzi—can he handle difficult affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general remarked: "A man as upright as Chen Zhongzi—can he manage so demanding a post?

sentences.zh: 又問：「今家幾何人？」

translations.literal: He again asked: "How many people are in your household now?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked: "How many people do you have at home now?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「子一，客與僕各二。」

translations.literal: He answered: "One son; two guests and two servants."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin replied: "One son, two boarders, and two servants.

sentences.zh: 瞷之，信，皆驚異。

translations.literal: He secretly observed—believed it—and all were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: The governor sent someone to look in on the household, found the account true, and was astonished along with everyone else.

sentences.zh: 自公費除而上之取給者亦減。

translations.literal: From the abolition of the public expense, those above who drew supplies were also reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Once the daily public expense was abolished, the demands on the people from higher offices also fell.

sentences.zh: 昆明池受四山之水，夏秋暴漲，怒流入閘河。

translations.literal: Kunming Lake received the waters of four mountains; in summer and autumn it swelled violently, rushing furiously into the Zhahe River.
translations.idiomatic: Kunming Lake collected the runoff from four surrounding mountains; in summer and autumn it swelled violently and sent floodwater rushing into the Zhahe River.

sentences.zh: 沙石壅塞，水乃溢。

translations.literal: Sand and stones obstructed it and the water then overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Sand and gravel clogged the channel until the water spilled over.

sentences.zh: 浸瀕池田，歲勞民力濬之。

translations.literal: It inundated fields bordering the lake; every year the people's labor was exhausted dredging it.
translations.idiomatic: It flooded the lakeside fields, and every year the people were worn out dredging the channel.

sentences.zh: 晉寧州境毗於昆明，受東南諸箐之水，舊蹟有河道入江，上官議鑿之以通閘河。

translations.literal: Jinning Prefecture's territory bordered Kunming, receiving waters from southeastern gullies; old traces showed a river course entering the Yangzi; superiors discussed digging it to connect with the Zhahe.
translations.idiomatic: Jinning Prefecture adjoined Kunming and collected water from the southeastern ravines. Ancient traces showed a river channel that once reached the Yangzi, and the provincial authorities proposed digging it anew to link it with the Zhahe.

sentences.zh: 瑾按地勢為圖白之曰：「閘河獨受昆明之水，已不能吐納，沙石旁溢為害，豈可更受晉寧水乎？

translations.literal: Jin surveyed the terrain, made a map, and reported: "The Zhahe alone receives Kunming's water and already cannot discharge and absorb; sand and stones spill sideways as harm—how can it receive Jinning's water as well?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin surveyed the terrain, drew a map, and submitted his report: "The Zhahe already receives Kunming Lake's water and can barely handle the flow; sand and gravel spill over the banks. How can it take on Jinning's water as well?

sentences.zh: 且其地高若建瓴，沙石犖確尤甚，殆不可治。」

translations.literal: Moreover its land is high as if water poured from a eave; rocky sand and stones are especially severe—likely untreatable."
translations.idiomatic: And the ground there slopes steeply like water tipping from a rooftop; the rock and gravel are especially hard—likely impossible to dredge.

sentences.zh: 台司持之堅，則指圖爭曰：「高下在目，何忍陷民於死！」

translations.literal: The provincial commissioner held firm; then pointing to the map he contested: "High and low are before the eyes—how can one bear to trap the people in death!"
translations.idiomatic: The provincial commissioner held firm, so Zhang Jin pointed to his map and protested: "The elevations are plain to see—how can you condemn the people to die!

sentences.zh: 總督范承勳曰：「令言是也。」

translations.literal: Governor-General Fan Chengxun said: "The magistrate's words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Fan Chengxun said: "The magistrate is right.

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The proposal thus lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 縣有止善、春登、利城諸裡田，坳垤錯出，不旱則潦。

translations.literal: The county had farmlands in the li of Zhishan, Chundeng, and Licheng—depressions and mounds alternating; if not drought then flooding.
translations.idiomatic: In the li of Zhishan, Chundeng, Licheng, and elsewhere the fields lay in a patchwork of hollows and rises, suffering flood whenever there was no drought.

sentences.zh: 瑾廉得旁近有白沙、馬裊、清水三河，可資蓄洩，年久湮塞，率民濬治。

translations.literal: Jin through investigation learned that nearby were the three rivers Baisha, Maniao, and Qingshui that could serve for storage and discharge; long years of silt had blocked them; he led the people to dredge and repair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin discovered that the Baisha, Maniao, and Qingshui rivers nearby could be used for irrigation and drainage but had silted up over the years; he led the people in dredging them.

sentences.zh: 三月河复，田以常稔。

translations.literal: Within three months the rivers were restored; fields thereby enjoyed regular harvests.
translations.idiomatic: Within three months the rivers flowed again, and the fields yielded steady harvests.

sentences.zh: 大小東門外舊皆市，兵後為墟，盜賊窟其中。

translations.literal: Outside the great and small east gates had formerly all been markets; after the military campaigns they became ruins where bandits made lairs.
translations.idiomatic: The areas outside the Great and Small East Gates had once been market districts; after the wars they lay in ruins and became bandits' hideouts.

sentences.zh: 為創造室廬，以居流亡，移城中騾、馬、羊諸市實之。

translations.literal: He built dwellings to house displaced persons, moved the markets for mules, horses, and sheep within the city to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: He built new houses for refugees and moved the city's mule, horse, and sheep markets into them to fill the streets with life.

sentences.zh: 貨廛牧場相比，盜遂絕跡。

translations.literal: Shop-stalls and pasture grounds stood side by side; bandits then vanished entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Shops and livestock pens stood side by side, and the bandits disappeared altogether.

sentences.zh: 安阜園者，故籓囿也，請耕之以食孤貧廢疾而無告者。

translations.literal: Anfu Garden was the former princely enclosure; he requested to cultivate it to feed the orphaned, poor, disabled, and those with no one to appeal to.
translations.idiomatic: Anfu Garden had been the prince's hunting park; he petitioned to farm it to feed the orphaned, the impoverished, the disabled, and others with no one to turn to.

sentences.zh: 是時上官多賢者，每倚信瑾。

translations.literal: At this time many superiors were worthy men; each relied on and trusted Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his superiors at the time were capable men, and all came to rely on Zhang Jin.

sentences.zh: 兵備道欲以流民所墾田牧馬，求之期年，不與，久亦稱其直。

translations.literal: The military preparedness intendant wished to use refugee-reclaimed land for horse grazing; he sought it for a full year—Jin would not grant it; after long he also praised his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The military preparedness intendant wanted to graze horses on land reclaimed by refugees and pressed for a full year; Zhang Jin refused, and in time even he praised his uprightness.

sentences.zh: 將軍僕殺人，按察使置酒為請，陽諾之，退而正其罪。

translations.literal: A general's servant killed a man; the provincial surveillance commissioner set out wine to intercede; Jin outwardly promised, then retired and judged his crime.
translations.idiomatic: When a general's servant murdered someone, the provincial surveillance commissioner held a banquet to plead on his behalf; Zhang Jin agreed in public, then returned and passed sentence according to the law.

sentences.zh: 巡撫僕子謀奪士人聘妻，即縣庭令士人行合卺禮，判曰：「法不得娶有夫之婦，婦乘我輿，壻乘我馬，役送之歸，有奪者治其罪。」

translations.literal: The governor's servant son plotted to seize a scholar's betrothed; at the county hall Jin had the scholar perform the wedding rites and judged: "By law one may not marry a woman who already has a husband; the woman shall ride my carriage, the son-in-law my horse; servants shall escort her home; whoever seizes her shall be punished."
translations.idiomatic: When the governor's servant tried to seize a scholar's betrothed bride, Zhang Jin had the scholar perform the wedding ceremony right in the county hall and ruled: "The law forbids marrying a woman already betrothed. The bride shall ride in my carriage, the groom on my horse; my servants will escort her home, and anyone who interferes will be punished.

sentences.zh: 時人作歌詩以傳之。

translations.literal: People of the time composed songs and poems to spread the story.
translations.idiomatic: People of the day wrote songs and poems to spread word of the deed.

sentences.zh: 初至，滯獄以百數，斷訖皆當。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, stalled cases numbered in the hundreds; when judged, all were apt.
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived, hundreds of cases lay pending; every judgment he handed down was fair.

sentences.zh: 後一省疑獄輒付瑾治，屢有平反。

translations.literal: Later the entire province's doubtful cases were entrusted to Jin; repeatedly there were reversals of wrongful verdicts.
translations.idiomatic: Later the whole province sent its hardest cases to Zhang Jin, and he repeatedly overturned wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 居三年，病卒。

translations.literal: After three years in office he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 士民圖其像藏之，請祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: Gentry and common people painted his portrait and kept it, petitioning for sacrifice in the shrine of celebrated officials.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and common people painted his portrait for safekeeping and petitioned to enshrine him in the hall of celebrated officials.

sentences.zh: 江皋，字在湄，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: Jiang Gao, courtesy name Zaimai, was a native of Tongcheng, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gao, styled Zaimai, came from Tongcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 順治十八年進士，觀政刑部。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the eighteenth year of Shunzhi; he observed administration in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighteenth year of Shunzhi and was assigned to observe proceedings at the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 父病，乞養歸。

translations.literal: His father fell ill; he requested leave to return and care for him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill, he petitioned to return home to care for him.

sentences.zh: 喪除，授江西瑞昌知縣。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, he was appointed magistrate of Ruichang, Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he was appointed magistrate of Ruichang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 故事，歲一巡鄉堡、校戶籍，斂輿馬費，皋罷之。

translations.literal: By precedent, once a year there was an inspection tour of village forts and household register verification, collecting carriage and horse expenses—Gao abolished this.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the magistrate made an annual tour of village forts to verify household registers and collected carriage and horse fees for the journey; Gao abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 縣城近河，壖岸善崩，屢決改道，環城無隍，民病汲。

translations.literal: The county seat was near the river; the riverbank easily collapsed; repeated breaches changed the course; around the city there was no moat; the people suffered in drawing water.
translations.idiomatic: The county seat stood beside a river whose banks were prone to collapse; repeated breaches had shifted the channel, leaving the city without a moat and the people struggling to draw water.

sentences.zh: 皋出俸金，率先效力，築堅堤，濬壅塞。

translations.literal: Gao contributed his salary, taking the lead in labor, building firm dikes and dredging blockages.
translations.idiomatic: Gao paid out of his own salary, took the lead in the work, built sturdy dikes, and dredged the clogged channels.

sentences.zh: 水復其故，形勢益壯，民居遂蕃。

translations.literal: The water returned to its old course; the terrain grew ever stronger; dwellings thereupon flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The river returned to its old course, the city's defenses grew stronger, and the population began to thrive.

sentences.zh: 三籓叛，縣界連湖南，土寇乘間起。

translations.literal: When the Three Feudatories rebelled, the county border connected with Hunan; local bandits rose taking advantage of the interval.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Feudatories rebelled, the county bordered Hunan, and local bandits seized the opportunity to rise.

sentences.zh: 皋曰：「吾民緣飢寒出此，迫之則走藉寇」。

translations.literal: Gao said: "Our people do this from hunger and cold; if pressed they will flee and attach themselves to bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Gao said: "Our people turn to this from hunger and cold; drive them too hard and they will flee to the bandits for refuge."

sentences.zh: 飭鄉、保長開諭撫安，而密督丁壯巡查，屢擒其魁，盜遂息。

translations.literal: He ordered village and baojia heads to open explanations and pacify; meanwhile secretly supervised able-bodied men in patrol, repeatedly captured ringleaders, and banditry then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered village and baojia heads to counsel and reassure the people, while secretly directing able-bodied men on patrol; they captured several ringleaders, and banditry subsided.

sentences.zh: 居七歲，考最，遷九江府同知，尋擢甘肅鞏昌知府。

translations.literal: After seven years in office, rated highest in evaluation, he was transferred to vice prefect of Jiujiang Prefecture, and soon promoted to prefect of Gongchang, Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years he received the highest evaluation, was promoted to vice prefect of Jiujiang Prefecture, and soon after to prefect of Gongchang in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 大軍入蜀，治辦軍需。

translations.literal: When the great army entered Shu, he managed and prepared military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army marched into Sichuan, he organized its provisions and materiel.

sentences.zh: 值歲除，檄徵騾馬千匹，茭芻器具，取具倉猝。

translations.literal: It happened to be New Year's Eve; an urgent order requisitioned a thousand mules and horses, fodder, and equipment—the supplies had to be gathered in haste.
translations.idiomatic: It was New Year's Eve when an urgent requisition arrived for a thousand mules and horses, along with fodder and equipment, all to be assembled at once.

sentences.zh: 皋策畫便宜，供應無缺。

translations.literal: Gao devised expedient measures, and the supplies were without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Gao devised workable expedients, and nothing fell short.

sentences.zh: 士卒驕悍，所過漁奪百姓，皋遇，輒縛送軍主，斬以徇，繇是肅然。

translations.literal: The soldiers were arrogant and fierce; wherever they passed they plundered the common people. When Gao encountered them, he would bind them and send them to the army commander to be executed as a warning; from this the troops became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were arrogant and violent, plundering civilians wherever they marched. Whenever Gao caught them, he had them bound and sent to their commander for execution as a public warning, and from then on discipline held.

sentences.zh: 越四歲，調廣西柳州。

translations.literal: After four years, he was transferred to Liuzhou in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he was transferred to Liuzhou in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 時新收嶺西，兵猶留鎮。

translations.literal: At the time the region west of the mountains had only recently been recovered, and troops still remained garrisoned there.
translations.idiomatic: The region west of the Ling Mountains had only just been brought under control, and troops were still stationed there.

sentences.zh: 軍中多掠婦女，皋白大吏，檄營帥，籍所掠送郡資遣，凡數百人。

translations.literal: Many women had been seized in the army. Gao reported this to senior officials, issued orders to the camp commanders, registered those who had been abducted, and sent them to the prefecture to be provided funds for their return—several hundred in all.
translations.idiomatic: Many women had been seized within the army. Gao reported the matter to his superiors and ordered the camp commanders to register every abducted woman and send her to the prefectural seat with funds for the journey home—several hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 軍餉不繼，士譁噪將變，皋馳諭緩期，趣台司發餉，應期至，軍乃戢。

translations.literal: Military rations were not forthcoming; the soldiers clamored and were on the verge of mutiny. Gao rushed to announce an extension of the deadline and urged the provincial offices to dispatch rations. They arrived on schedule, and the army then settled down.
translations.idiomatic: When army rations ran out, the soldiers grew restive and were near mutiny. Gao rode out to announce a reprieve and pressed the provincial offices to release the pay. The funds arrived on time, and the troops quieted down.

sentences.zh: 郡民王纘緒，故官家子，經亂，產為四奴所據，隻身寄食僧舍。

translations.literal: A county resident named Wang Xuanxu, formerly from an official family, had lost everything in the turmoil; his property was seized by four slaves, and he alone took refuge in a monastery for food.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Wang Xuanxu came from an official family. After years of disorder, four slaves had seized his estate, and he was left alone, living on charity at a Buddhist monastery.

sentences.zh: 皋詰得之，悉逮捕諸奴。

translations.literal: Gao interrogated the matter and got to the bottom of it, then arrested all the slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Gao investigated the case, uncovered the truth, and had all four slaves arrested.

sentences.zh: 奴懼，納二千金乞免，佯受之。

translations.literal: The slaves were afraid and offered two thousand in gold to beg release; Gao feigned acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the slaves offered two thousand taels of silver to buy their freedom. Gao pretended to accept.

sentences.zh: 訊伏罪，乃出金授纘緒，命奴從歸，盡還其產，柳人歌誦之。

translations.literal: After interrogation they confessed their crimes. He then produced the gold and gave it to Xuanxu, ordered the slaves to follow him home, and fully restored his property. The people of Liuzhou sang and recounted the story.
translations.idiomatic: Once they confessed under questioning, he turned the silver over to Wang Xuanxu, sent the slaves home with him, and restored the entire estate. The people of Liuzhou sang songs to spread word of the deed.

sentences.zh: 太和殿大工興，使者採木，民大恐。

translations.literal: When major construction began at the Hall of Supreme Harmony, envoys came to gather timber, and the people were greatly frightened.
translations.idiomatic: When work began on the Hall of Supreme Harmony, timber commissioners arrived, and the people were terrified.

sentences.zh: 長老言故明採木於此，僵僕谿谷，橫藉不可數。

translations.literal: The elders said that under the former Ming timber had been gathered here, and corpses collapsed in streams and valleys, lying strewn beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The elders said that when the Ming had gathered timber here, men had dropped dead in the ravines until the slopes were strewn with bodies beyond number.

sentences.zh: 皋曰：「上命也，何敢匿諱！」

translations.literal: Gao said: "It is the emperor's command—how dare I conceal or suppress it!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao said: "This is an imperial order—how could I dare to hide it!"

sentences.zh: 使者至，令民前導，自控騎偕使者往視。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, he had the people lead the way, took the reins himself, and rode with the envoy to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived, he had local men guide the way, mounted his own horse, and rode out with the commissioner to inspect the timber.

sentences.zh: 巨木森挺絕巘，下臨深谷。

translations.literal: Towering trees stood thick on sheer peaks, overlooking deep valleys below.
translations.idiomatic: Immense trees rose in dense stands on sheer cliff tops, with deep gorges yawning below.

sentences.zh: 下騎，掖使者攀援以登，崖益峻，無側足所。

translations.literal: He dismounted and, supporting the envoy, climbed up by handholds; the cliff grew ever steeper, with nowhere to set a foot sideways.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted and helped the envoy climb hand over hand. The cliff grew steeper still until there was scarcely room to stand.

sentences.zh: 使者咋舌曰：「是不可取。」

translations.literal: The envoy clicked his tongue and said: "This cannot be taken."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy clicked his tongue and said: "Timber like this cannot be taken."

sentences.zh: 還奏免役。

translations.literal: He returned and memorialized that the corvée be exempted.
translations.idiomatic: He went back and reported that the levy should be canceled.

sentences.zh: 民讙呼，戴上恩德。

translations.literal: The people shouted for joy and attributed it to the emperor's grace and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people erupted in cheers and credited the emperor's benevolence.

sentences.zh: 尋被薦提學四川，以母喪解官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was recommended as educational commissioner for Sichuan, but resigned when his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recommended to serve as educational commissioner of Sichuan, but resigned when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補陝西平慶道副使，遷福建興泉道參政。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed vice commissioner of the Pingqing Circuit in Shaanxi, then transferred to administrative commissioner of the Xingquan Circuit in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period he was appointed vice commissioner of the Pingqing Circuit in Shaanxi, then promoted to administrative commissioner of the Xingquan Circuit in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 以事左遷，旋以恩復職，卒於家。

translations.literal: He was demoted for an incident, but soon restored by imperial grace; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted over an incident, then restored by imperial favor, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 皋於廣西聲績最著。

translations.literal: Gao's reputation and achievements were most prominent in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's reputation and record of achievement were greatest in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 其後稱張克嶷、賈樸。

translations.literal: After him came Zhang Keyi and Jia Pu.
translations.idiomatic: After him the chapter turns to Zhang Keyi and Jia Pu.

sentences.zh: 克嶷，字偉公，山西聞喜人。

translations.literal: Keyi, courtesy name Weigong, was a native of Wenxi in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Keyi, styled Weigong, came from Wenxi in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年進士，選庶吉士，改刑部主事，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the eighteenth year of Kangxi, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, transferred to the Ministry of Justice as a clerk, and rose through successive promotions to department director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighteenth year of Kangxi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was transferred to the Ministry of Justice as a clerk, and rose through the ranks to department director.

sentences.zh: 有獄連執政族人，諸司莫敢任，克嶷請獨任之。

translations.literal: There was a case involving a senior official's clansman; no department dared take it on, but Keyi requested to handle it alone.
translations.idiomatic: When a case implicated a senior official's kinsman, no department dared touch it. Keyi volunteered to take sole responsibility.

sentences.zh: 內務府以其人出使為辭，克嶷鉤提益急。

translations.literal: The Imperial Household Department pleaded that the man was away on a diplomatic mission; Keyi pursued his summons with growing urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household Department claimed the man was abroad on a diplomatic mission, but Keyi pressed his summons all the harder.

sentences.zh: 牒問奉使何地、歸何期，力請部長入告。

translations.literal: He sent a dispatch asking where the mission was bound and when it would return, and urgently asked the department head to report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He issued a formal inquiry asking where the envoy had gone and when he would return, and pressed the department head to report the matter to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 事雖格，聞者肅然。

translations.literal: Although the matter was blocked in the end, those who heard of it were awed.
translations.idiomatic: The case was ultimately blocked, but everyone who heard of it was impressed.

sentences.zh: 出為廣西平樂知府，瑤、僮雜居，盜不可詰。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Pingle in Guangxi, where Yao and Zhuang lived intermixed and banditry was impossible to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Pingle in Guangxi, where Yao and Zhuang peoples lived side by side and banditry was beyond control.

sentences.zh: 克嶷至浹月，以信義服苗酋。

translations.literal: Within a month of Keyi's arrival, he won over the Miao chiefs through trust and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month of his arrival, Keyi had won the Miao chiefs over through integrity and fair dealing.

sentences.zh: 獲巨盜二人，斃其一，宥其一，責以偵緝，終其任盜不敢窺。

translations.literal: He captured two major bandits, killed one, pardoned the other, and charged him with reconnaissance and pursuit; throughout his tenure bandits dared not show themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He captured two notorious bandits, executed one, spared the other, and put him to work tracking down his fellows. For the rest of Keyi's term, bandits did not dare show their faces.

sentences.zh: 調廣東潮州，屬縣賊蜂起，或稱明裔，聚眾千餘人。

translations.literal: Transferred to Chaozhou in Guangdong, bandits rose in swarms in the subordinate counties; some claimed descent from the Ming and gathered more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Chaozhou in Guangdong, he found bandits rising across the subordinate counties. Some claimed to be descendants of the Ming and had assembled more than a thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 克嶷疾馳至其地，命吏士速據白葉祁山，設疑兵，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: Keyi raced to the scene, ordered officials and soldiers to quickly occupy Baiye and Qishan, set up decoy troops, and the bandits dared not press close.
translations.idiomatic: Keyi galloped to the scene and ordered his officers and soldiers to seize Baiye and Qishan at once. He deployed decoy forces, and the bandits dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 會夜半，大風起，簡健卒二百斫其營，呼曰：「大兵至矣！」

translations.literal: At midnight a great wind rose; he selected two hundred stalwart soldiers to raid their camp and shouted: "The great army has arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: At midnight a fierce wind sprang up. He picked two hundred picked troops to strike the bandit camp and shouted: "The main army is here!"

sentences.zh: 城中鼓譟出兵以助之，賊奔祁山，要擊之，斬其渠魁三人，眾散乞降。

translations.literal: Drums clamored in the city and troops sallied to assist; the bandits fled toward Qishan, were ambushed and struck, three ringleaders were beheaded, and the rest scattered and begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Drums thundered in the city and troops rushed out to join the attack. The bandits fled toward Qishan, where they were intercepted; three ringleaders were beheaded, and the rest scattered and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 巡撫將上其功，克嶷曰：「此盜耳，而稱明裔，興大獄，株連多，恐轉生變。」

translations.literal: The governor was about to report his merit, but Keyi said: "These are mere bandits. If we call them Ming descendants and open a great case, many will be implicated—we fear this will stir further trouble."
translations.idiomatic: The governor was about to memorialize his victory, but Keyi said: "These are nothing but bandits. If we treat them as Ming loyalists and open a treason case, the net will drag in too many people and may provoke fresh unrest."

sentences.zh: 乃以盜案結。

translations.literal: He therefore closed the matter as an ordinary bandit case.
translations.idiomatic: He closed the matter as an ordinary bandit case.

sentences.zh: 郡有大豪戕親迎者於路而奪其妻，克嶷微行跡而得之。

translations.literal: In the prefecture a powerful bully killed the bridegroom on the wedding procession road and seized his wife; Keyi traced the crime through secret investigation.
translations.idiomatic: A local magnate had murdered a bridegroom on the wedding procession road and seized his bride. Keyi tracked him down through undercover investigation.

sentences.zh: 獄成，當大辟。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, the sentence was death.
translations.idiomatic: Once the case was tried, the sentence was death.

sentences.zh: 監司以督撫命為之請，曰：「稍遼緩之，當有以報。」

translations.literal: The circuit intendant, on the governor-general's orders, pleaded on the man's behalf, saying: "Delay the sentence a little—there will be something with which to repay you."
translations.idiomatic: On orders from the governor-general, the circuit intendant interceded for the man, saying: "Hold off a while—we will find a way to repay the favor."

sentences.zh: 克嶷曰：「吾官可罷，獄不可鬻也。」

translations.literal: Keyi said: "My office may be dismissed, but a case cannot be sold."
translations.idiomatic: Keyi replied: "You may strip me of my post, but you cannot buy off a case."

sentences.zh: 卒寘諸法。

translations.literal: In the end he applied the law.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he carried out the sentence.

sentences.zh: 或假親王命以開礦，縛執之。

translations.literal: Someone forged a prince's order to open mines; Keyi bound and arrested him.
translations.idiomatic: When someone forged a prince's order to open a mine, Keyi had him seized and bound.

sentences.zh: 其人出龍牌，克嶷命系之獄，以牌申大府。

translations.literal: The man produced an imperial dragon tablet; Keyi ordered him imprisoned and reported the tablet to the provincial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: The man produced an imperial dragon tablet. Keyi had him thrown in prison and forwarded the tablet to the provincial authorities.

sentences.zh: 情既得，立杖殺之。

translations.literal: Once the facts were established, he immediately had the man beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Once the facts were confirmed, he had the man beaten to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂歸，遂不出。

translations.literal: When his father's mourning ended he returned home and never served again.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for his father's mourning and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 年七十六，卒。

translations.literal: At the age of seventy-six, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 樸，字素庵，直隸故城人。

translations.literal: Pu, courtesy name Su'an, was a native of Gucheng in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Pu, styled Su'an, came from Gucheng in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 貢生。

translations.literal: He was a tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: He entered through the tribute-student route.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十三年，授廣西柳州同知，有政聲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kangxi he was appointed vice prefect of Liuzhou in Guangxi and gained a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Kangxi he was appointed vice prefect of Liuzhou in Guangxi, where he quickly earned a name for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 思明土屬負固抗官，大吏知其能，調任思明治之。

translations.literal: The native chiefs of Siming stubbornly resisted the officials; senior officials, knowing his ability, transferred him to govern Siming.
translations.idiomatic: The native chiefs of Siming were entrenched and defied the authorities. Knowing his ability, his superiors transferred him to govern the district.

sentences.zh: 夜遣健卒潛入山，焚賊寨，遂出降。

translations.literal: At night he sent stalwart soldiers secretly into the mountains, burned the bandit strongholds, and they then came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: By night he sent picked troops into the hills, burned the bandit camps, and the rebels came down to surrender.

sentences.zh: 署思明知府，土田州岑氏母子相爭，土目陸師等構之以為利，殺人千餘。

translations.literal: Acting as prefect of Siming, he found the native Tianzhou chiefs of the Cen clan—mother and son—locked in dispute; the native officer Lu Shi and others incited them for profit, and more than a thousand were killed.
translations.idiomatic: As acting prefect of Siming, he found the Cen clan of Tianzhou torn by a feud between mother and son. Native officers such as Lu Shi had fanned the conflict for profit, and more than a thousand people had died.

sentences.zh: 樸至切諭，母子俱感泣。

translations.literal: When Pu arrived he earnestly counseled them, and mother and son both wept in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu arrived he spoke to them earnestly, and mother and son both wept and submitted.

sentences.zh: 師等聚眾謀不軌，先懾以兵，單騎往，曉以禍福，乃聽命。

translations.literal: Shi and his followers gathered a crowd and plotted sedition; Pu first awed them with troops, then went alone on horseback, explained fortune and disaster, and they then obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Shi and his followers gathered a mob and plotted rebellion, Pu first overawed them with troops, then rode alone into their camp and explained what fortune and ruin would bring. They submitted.

sentences.zh: 建明倫堂，設義學，代完寒士逋糧。

translations.literal: He built the Hall of Bright Morality, established a charity school, and paid off the grain-tax arrears of impoverished scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Hall of Bright Morality, founded a charity school, and paid off the grain-tax arrears of poor scholars.

sentences.zh: 民立生祠奉之。

translations.literal: The people erected a living shrine to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: The people built a living shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 擢貴州平越知府，罣誤去官。

translations.literal: Promoted to prefect of Pingyue in Guizhou, he was dismissed because of a mishap.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to prefect of Pingyue in Guizhou, he was later dismissed over a mishap.

sentences.zh: 樸在廣西，嘗條上邊事，巡撫彭鵬奇其才。

translations.literal: While Pu was in Guangxi, he once submitted a detailed memorial on border affairs; Governor Peng Peng marveled at his talent.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Guangxi, Pu once submitted a detailed memorial on frontier affairs, and Governor Peng Peng was struck by his ability.

sentences.zh: 四十年，詔舉廉吏，鵬特疏薦，授江南蘇州知府。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year an edict called for recommendations of incorrupt officials; Peng specially memorialized recommending him, and he was appointed prefect of Suzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year the throne ordered the nomination of honest officials. Peng submitted a special recommendation, and Pu was appointed prefect of Suzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 與吏民相見以誠，屏絕請託，政聲大起。

translations.literal: He met officials and people with sincerity, shut out all solicitations, and his governmental reputation rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He dealt with officials and commoners alike in good faith, refused every favor-seeker, and his reputation soared.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，聖祖南巡，幸蘇州，嘉其清廉為吳中最，擢江常鎮道，吳民數千人遮道請留賢守，御書「宜民」匾額賜之。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year the Kangxi Emperor toured south and visited Suzhou, praising his integrity as the finest in Wu; he was promoted to the Jiang-Chang-Zhen Circuit. Thousands of Wu people blocked the road pleading to keep their worthy magistrate, and the emperor wrote the plaque "Benefit the People" and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year the Kangxi Emperor toured the south and visited Suzhou, praising Pu as the most incorruptible official in the Wu region and promoting him to the Jiang-Chang-Zhen Circuit. Thousands of local people blocked the road, begging that their worthy magistrate be kept. The emperor wrote the plaque "Benefit the People" and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 調蘇松常鎮太糧儲道、布政使參政，仍兼管蘇州府事，從民原也。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Su-Song-Chang-Zhen grain storage circuit and to administrative commissioner, while still concurrently managing Suzhou Prefecture affairs—acceding to the people's wish.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Su-Song-Chang-Zhen grain-storage circuit and made administrative commissioner, while still overseeing Suzhou Prefecture in deference to popular demand.

sentences.zh: 革四府徵糧例規，積弊一清。

translations.literal: He abolished the customary surcharges on grain collection in the four prefectures, and accumulated abuses were cleared at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the customary surcharges on grain collection across four prefectures and swept away years of accumulated abuse.

sentences.zh: 忤總督噶禮，摭事劾之，四十九年，去官。

translations.literal: He offended Governor-General Gali, who seized on incidents to impeach him; in the forty-ninth year he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed Governor-General Gali, who seized on pretexts to impeach him. In the forty-ninth year he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 留吳門三年，歸里卒。

translations.literal: He remained at the Wu gate for three years, then returned home and died.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed in Suzhou for three years, then returned home and died.

sentences.zh: 邵嗣堯，字子昆，山西猗氏人。

translations.literal: Shao Siyao, courtesy name Zikun, was a native of Yishi in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Siyao, styled Zikun, came from Yishi in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年進士，授山東臨淄知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the ninth year of Kangxi, he was appointed magistrate of Linzi in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the ninth year of Kangxi and was appointed magistrate of Linzi in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 有惠政，以憂去。

translations.literal: He had benevolent policies, but left office due to mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with kindness, then left office to mourn a parent.

sentences.zh: 十九年，服闋，補直隸柏鄉。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, when mourning ended, he was appointed to Baixiang in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, when his mourning ended, he was appointed magistrate of Baixiang in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 興水利，減火耗，禁差擾，民安之。

translations.literal: He promoted waterworks, reduced melt-loss surcharges, forbade runner harassment, and the people lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: He improved irrigation, cut melt-loss surcharges, and forbade runner harassment, and the people lived at ease.

sentences.zh: 縣人大學士魏裔介為嗣堯會試座主，家人犯法，嚴治之，不少貸。

translations.literal: The county's Grand Secretary Wei Yijie had been Siyao's chief examiner at the metropolitan examination; when members of Wei's household violated the law, Siyao punished them severely without leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wei Yijie of the county had been Siyao's chief examiner at the metropolitan examination. When Wei's household broke the law, Siyao punished them without mercy.

sentences.zh: 又有旗丁毒毆子錢家，入縣庭，勢洶洶。

translations.literal: There was also a bannerman who violently beat a moneylender's family, then entered the county hall in a menacing manner.
translations.idiomatic: A banner soldier also savagely beat a moneylender's family, then stormed into the county hall in a threatening rage.

sentences.zh: 嗣堯不稍屈，系之獄，移文都統訊主者，主者不敢承，具論如法。

translations.literal: Siyao did not yield in the slightest; he imprisoned the man and sent a dispatch to the banner commander to investigate the master. The master dared not acknowledge responsibility, and Siyao adjudicated the case fully according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Siyao did not budge. He had the man imprisoned and wrote to the banner commander demanding that the soldier's master be questioned. The master disavowed him, and Siyao tried the case to the full letter of the law.

sentences.zh: 值歲饑，或言勒積粟家出粟，嗣堯曰：「人惟不積粟，故歲饑則束手，吾方蘄令積粟家獲厚利，何勒為？」

translations.literal: During a famine year, some said grain hoarders should be forced to release grain. Siyao said: "Only because people do not hoard grain do they find themselves helpless in famine. I am trying to ensure hoarders can profit greatly—why force them?"
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year, some urged him to compel grain hoarders to sell their stores. Siyao said: "People hoard grain precisely because they fear famine. If we force them to release it, they will stop storing it altogether, and then when famine comes everyone will be helpless. I want hoarders to profit—why coerce them?"

sentences.zh: 已而蠲粟者眾，歲不為災。

translations.literal: Before long many released grain, and the year did not become a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Before long many hoarders released their grain voluntarily, and the year passed without catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 有言開滏陽河通舟楫者，巡撫於成龍使嗣堯往相度，嗣堯力持不可，謂：「此河旱潦不常，未可通舟楫。

translations.literal: Some proposed opening the Fuyang River for navigation; Governor Yu Chenglong had Siyao go to survey it. Siyao strongly held that it could not be done, saying: "This river's floods and droughts are irregular—it cannot be made navigable.
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed dredging the Fuyang River for shipping, Governor Yu Chenglong sent Siyao to survey the project. Siyao firmly opposed it, saying: "This river's flow is erratic in flood and drought—it is not fit for navigation.

sentences.zh: 即或能通，恐舟楫之利歸商賈，挑濬之害歸窮民矣。」

translations.literal: Even if it could be opened, I fear the profit of navigation would go to merchants while the harm of dredging would fall on the poor."
translations.idiomatic: Even if it could be opened, the profits of shipping would go to merchants while the cost of dredging would fall on the poor."

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 盜殺人於縣界，立捕至，置之法。

translations.literal: A bandit killed someone at the county border; Siyao immediately had him captured and executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When a bandit murdered someone on the county border, Siyao had him captured at once and executed.

sentences.zh: 或毀於上官，以酷刑奪職。

translations.literal: Some slandered him to his superiors, and he lost his office on a charge of cruel punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies slandered him to his superiors, and he was dismissed on a charge of excessive punishment.

sentences.zh: 尚書魏象樞奉命巡視畿輔，民為申訴，事得白。

translations.literal: Minister Wei Xiangshu was ordered to inspect the capital region; the people petitioned on Siyao's behalf, and the matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wei Xiangshu was sent to inspect the capital region. The people petitioned on Siyao's behalf, and the truth came out.

sentences.zh: 於成龍复薦之，補清苑。

translations.literal: Yu Chenglong again recommended him, and he was appointed to Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chenglong recommended him again, and he was appointed magistrate of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 嗣堯益感奮自勵，屢斷疑獄，人以包孝肅比之。

translations.literal: Siyao was all the more inspired and disciplined himself; he repeatedly resolved doubtful cases, and people compared him to Bao Xiaosu.
translations.idiomatic: Siyao redoubled his efforts, repeatedly untangled difficult cases, and people compared him to Judge Bao.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，尚書王騭薦嗣堯清廉慈惠，行取，擢御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Minister Wang Zhi recommended Siyao as incorruptible and benevolent; he was selected for capital service and promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Minister Wang Zhi recommended Siyao as incorruptible and compassionate. He was selected for service at court and promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 三十年，出為直隸守道，持躬清介，苞苴杜絕。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he went out as defense commissioner of Zhili; personally upright and austere, he cut off bribes entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was appointed defense commissioner of Zhili. Personally upright and austere, he refused every bribe.

sentences.zh: 遇事霆發機激，勢要憚之。

translations.literal: When handling affairs he was swift and decisive as lightning; powerful figures feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He acted with lightning speed and fierce resolve, and the powerful feared him.

sentences.zh: 所屬州縣，肅然奉法。

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties under his jurisdiction were orderly in observing the law.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures and counties under his jurisdiction enforced the law with new discipline.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，江南學政缺，聖祖諭曰：「學政關係人材，朕觀陸隴其、邵嗣堯操守學問俱優，若以補授，必能秉公校士，革除積弊。」

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year the Jiangnan education commissioner's post was vacant. The Kangxi Emperor instructed: "The education commissioner bears on the quality of talent. I observe that Lu Longqi and Shao Siyao both excel in integrity and learning; if appointed, they will surely examine scholars impartially and reform accumulated abuses."
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year the post of Jiangnan education commissioner fell vacant. The Kangxi Emperor said: "The education commissioner shapes the quality of talent. I consider Lu Longqi and Shao Siyao outstanding in both integrity and scholarship. Either would examine candidates fairly and root out long-standing abuses."

sentences.zh: 時隴其已卒，遂命嗣堯以參議督學江南。

translations.literal: At that time Longqi had already died, so Siyao was ordered to supervise studies in Jiangnan as administrative commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: By then Longqi had already died, so the emperor appointed Siyao administrative commissioner to supervise education in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 既蒞事，虛衷衡校，論文宗尚簡質，著四書講義，傳示學者。

translations.literal: Once he assumed his duties, he evaluated with an open mind; in essays he valued simplicity and substance, wrote a commentary on the Four Books, and distributed it to scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he graded examinations with an open mind, favored plain and substantial writing, composed a commentary on the Four Books, and circulated it among students.

sentences.zh: 甫試三郡，以積勞遘疾卒。

translations.literal: He had examined only three prefectures when he fell ill from accumulated exhaustion and died.
translations.idiomatic: He had examined candidates in only three prefectures when overwork brought on illness and he died.

sentences.zh: 身無長物，同官斂貲致賻乃得歸葬。

translations.literal: He left no possessions; his colleagues collected funds for his funeral before he could be buried at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died leaving nothing behind. His colleagues pooled money for his funeral before his body could be sent home for burial.

sentences.zh: 士民思之，為立祠肖像以祀焉。

translations.literal: Gentry and common people missed him and erected a shrine with his portrait for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and common people missed him and built a shrine with his portrait so he could be honored.

sentences.zh: 聖祖澄清吏治，拔擢廉明，近畿尤多賢吏，如彭鵬、陸隴其及嗣堯，當時皆循名上達，聞於天下。

translations.literal: The Kangxi Emperor clarified official governance and promoted the honest and capable; especially around the capital there were many worthy officials, such as Peng Peng, Lu Longqi, and Siyao—all at the time rose on reputation and were known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor cleaned up the bureaucracy and elevated men of integrity. Around the capital in particular there were many worthy officials—Peng Peng, Lu Longqi, and Shao Siyao among them—all of whom rose on merit and were known throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 鵬及隴其自有傳。

translations.literal: Peng and Longqi have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Peng and Lu Longqi have biographies of their own.

sentences.zh: 又有衛立鼎、高廕爵、靳讓，治績亦足媲美。

translations.literal: There were also Wei Liding, Gao Yinjue, and Jin Rang, whose administrative achievements were also sufficient to compare.
translations.idiomatic: Also worth mention are Wei Liding, Gao Yinjue, and Jin Rang, whose records of governance stand comparison.

sentences.zh: 立鼎，字慎之，山西陽城人。

translations.literal: Liding, styled Shenzhi, was a native of Yangcheng in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liding, styled Shenzhi, was from Yangcheng in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年舉人，授直隸盧龍知縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi he passed the provincial examination, and was appointed magistrate of Lulong in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the second year of Kangxi and was appointed magistrate of Lulong in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 地當兩京孔道，驛使旁午，供張糗崿，悉自營辦，不以擾民。

translations.literal: The district lay on the main road between the two capitals; courier riders came and went incessantly, and provisions and rations for their reception he arranged entirely on his own without troubling the people.
translations.idiomatic: The county lay on the main road between the two capitals, where courier riders passed in an unending stream. He supplied their lodging and rations entirely from his own resources and never burdened the populace.

sentences.zh: 先是縣中徵糧，勺杪以下，皆用升合量。

translations.literal: Previously, when the county collected grain tax, amounts below the scoop level were all measured with sheng and ge.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the county had collected grain tax in sheng and ge for every fraction below a full scoop.

sentences.zh: 納草以銀代，仍抑價買諸民間。

translations.literal: Payment of fodder grass was replaced with silver, yet the price was still suppressed when buying from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Fodder dues were commuted to silver, but officials still forced purchases from the people at depressed prices.

sentences.zh: 立鼎令輸戶含納奇零，統歸斛斗，徵草則以本色輸，民甚便之。

translations.literal: Liding ordered each paying household to include odd fractional amounts in its payment and consolidate them into hu and dou; for fodder collection he required payment in kind, and the people found this very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Liding had each tax household roll odd fractions into whole hu and dou measures, and required fodder to be paid in kind. The people found this a great relief.

sentences.zh: 興行教化，獎拔士類，丕變其俗，尤以清廉著稱。

translations.literal: He promoted moral instruction, encouraged and elevated scholars, greatly transformed local custom, and was especially renowned for incorruptibility.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted moral instruction, encouraged scholars, and greatly changed local custom. He was especially famed for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 尚書魏象樞及侍郎科爾坤奉命巡畿內，至盧龍，已治具，不肯食，僅啜一甌。

translations.literal: Minister Wei Xiangshu and Vice Minister Ke'erkun were ordered to inspect the capital region; when they reached Lulong a feast had been prepared, but Liding would not eat and took only a single bowl of soup.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wei Xiangshu and Vice Minister Ke'erkun were sent to inspect the capital region. When they reached Lulong, a feast had been prepared, but Liding refused to eat and took only a single bowl of broth.

sentences.zh: 曰：「令飲盧龍一杯水耳，吾亦飲令一杯水。」

translations.literal: He said: "The magistrate drinks only a cup of Lulong water; I too will drink the magistrate a cup of water."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The magistrate lives on nothing but a cup of Lulong water. I shall drink only a cup of water with him."

sentences.zh: 諸大獄悉以諮之，立鼎引經準律，象樞大稱善。

translations.literal: All major cases were referred to him for consultation; Liding cited the classics and applied the law, and Xiangshu greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: All major cases were referred to him for advice. Liding cited the classics and applied the law, and Xiangshu praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 於成龍之巡撫直隸也，嘗迎駕於霸州，奏舉循吏，以立鼎、陸隴其並稱。

translations.literal: When Yu Chenglong was governor-general of Zhili, he once received the imperial procession at Bazhou and memorialized recommending exemplary officials, naming Liding and Lu Longqi together.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Chenglong was governor-general of Zhili, he once received the emperor at Bazhou and recommended exemplary officials, naming Liding and Lu Longqi together.

sentences.zh: 嗣巡撫格爾古德以事至盧龍，謂立鼎曰：「令之苦，無異秀才時。

translations.literal: Later Governor Ge'ergude came to Lulong on business and said to Liding: "Your hardship is no different from when you were a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Later Governor Ge'ergude came to Lulong on business and told Liding, "Your hardship is no different from when you were a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 秀才徒自苦，今令苦而百姓樂，非苦中之樂乎？」

translations.literal: A licentiate suffers only for himself; now the magistrate suffers while the people are content—is this not joy within hardship?"
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate suffers only for himself. Now you suffer while the people prosper—is that not joy found within hardship?"

sentences.zh: 疏薦立鼎治行第一，靈壽令陸隴其次之。

translations.literal: In a memorial he recommended Liding first in administrative conduct, with Lu Longqi of Lingshou second.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he ranked Liding first in administrative merit, with Lu Longqi of Lingshou second.

sentences.zh: 內遷戶部郎中，秩滿授福建福州知府，以年老致仕歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred within the capital to director in the Ministry of Revenue; when his term ended he was appointed prefect of Fuzhou in Fujian, and later retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue as a director. When his term ended he was appointed prefect of Fuzhou in Fujian, then retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 教授鄉里，以倡論道學為事。

translations.literal: He taught in his home district and made it his business to advocate Neo-Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he taught locally and devoted himself to promoting Neo-Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 年七十有六，卒。

translations.literal: At the age of seventy-six he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 廕爵，字子和，奉天鐵嶺人，隸漢軍。

translations.literal: Yinjue, styled Zihe, was a native of Tieling in Fengtian and belonged to the Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yinjue, styled Zihe, was from Tieling in Fengtian and belonged to the Han Banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，謁選，授直隸蠡縣知縣。

translations.literal: In the early Kangxi reign he presented himself for appointment and was made magistrate of Li County in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kangxi reign he presented himself for appointment and was made magistrate of Li County in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 縣多旗屯，居民田之半，佃者倚勳貴為奸利，持吏長短。

translations.literal: The county had many banner land colonies, and banner holdings made up half the residents' fields; tenants relied on meritorious nobles for illicit profit and held leverage over officials.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the county was banner land, and banner holdings accounted for half the farmland. Tenants leaned on noble patrons for illicit gain and used that leverage to intimidate officials.

sentences.zh: 河數決孟嘗村，歲比不登，民大饑。

translations.literal: The river repeatedly burst its banks at Mengchang Village; year after year the harvest failed, and the people suffered great famine.
translations.idiomatic: The river repeatedly burst its banks at Mengchang Village. Harvests failed year after year, and the people were in famine.

sentences.zh: 廕爵至，曰：「吾未暇理他政，且活民。」

translations.literal: When Yinjue arrived he said: "I have no leisure yet to manage other affairs; first I must keep the people alive."
translations.idiomatic: When Yinjue arrived he said, "I have no time yet for other business. First I must keep the people alive."

sentences.zh: 倉有粟二萬石，請發以賑。

translations.literal: The granary held twenty thousand shi of grain; he requested its release for relief.
translations.idiomatic: The granary held twenty thousand shi of grain, and he petitioned to release it for relief.

sentences.zh: 牘再上，不許；

translations.literal: He submitted the memorial twice more, but permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the petition twice more, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 請解官，乃許之五千石。

translations.literal: He asked to be relieved of office, and only then was he allowed five thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: He offered to resign, and only then was he granted five thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 廕爵曰：「若今歲又惡，民不能償​​，二萬石、五千石等死耳，吾且活吾民。」

translations.literal: Yinjue said: "If this year is bad again and the people cannot repay, twenty thousand shi and five thousand shi are equally dead to them; I will keep my people alive."
translations.idiomatic: Yinjue said, "If this year fails again the people cannot repay the grain. Whether it is twenty thousand shi or five thousand shi makes no difference to the starving. I will save my people."

sentences.zh: 乃盡發之。

translations.literal: He then released it all.
translations.idiomatic: He released the entire store.

sentences.zh: 更出帑五百金貸民種麥。

translations.literal: He further disbursed five hundred taels from the treasury to lend the people seed for wheat.
translations.idiomatic: He also lent the people five hundred taels from the treasury for wheat seed.

sentences.zh: 夏旱，蝗起，捕蝗盡。

translations.literal: In summer there was drought; locusts appeared, and he had them all captured.
translations.idiomatic: Summer brought drought and a locust plague, which he had exterminated.

sentences.zh: 秋又大霖雨，河暴溢，率吏民冒風雨捍禦，堤完而歲大熟，民乃安。

translations.literal: In autumn there were again torrential rains and the river surged; leading officials and people, he braved wind and rain to defend the dikes. The dikes held, the year brought a great harvest, and the people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn brought torrential rains and a river surge. He led officials and commoners through wind and rain to hold the dikes. The dikes held, the harvest was abundant, and the people were secure.

sentences.zh: 某甲以財雄諸佃，多為不法，誣諸生為奴，而籍其田。

translations.literal: A certain man used his wealth to dominate the tenants and committed many unlawful acts; he falsely accused a licentiate of being a bondservant and seized his land.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy tenant lord dominated the others and broke the law repeatedly. He falsely declared a licentiate a bondservant and seized his land.

sentences.zh: 按治得實，置之法。

translations.literal: An investigation established the facts, and he was punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: An investigation proved the case, and Yinjue punished him by law.

sentences.zh: 豪猾忄習服，莫敢犯令。

translations.literal: The bold and cunning learned to submit, and none dared violate the magistrate's orders.
translations.idiomatic: The bold and cunning submitted to his rule, and none dared defy his orders.

sentences.zh: 於是設義倉，置鄉學，尊禮賢士，民大和悅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established a charity granary, set up village schools, honored worthy men, and the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He then established a charity granary and village schools, honored worthy men, and the people were deeply content.

sentences.zh: 調三河，一以簡易為治。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Sanhe and governed entirely by simplicity and ease.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Sanhe, he governed with simplicity throughout.

sentences.zh: 或問之，曰：「前令已治矣，何紛更為？」

translations.literal: When someone asked him about this, he said: "The previous magistrate had already governed well—why make needless changes?"
translations.idiomatic: When asked about this he said, "The previous magistrate had already governed well. Why make needless changes?"

sentences.zh: 前令，彭鵬也。

translations.literal: The previous magistrate was Peng Peng.
translations.idiomatic: The previous magistrate was Peng Peng.

sentences.zh: 聖祖校獵至三河，問父老：「高令與彭令孰賢？」

translations.literal: The Kangxi Emperor came hunting to Sanhe and asked the elders: "Which is the worthier magistrate, Magistrate Gao or Magistrate Peng?"
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor came to Sanhe on a hunting tour and asked the elders, "Which magistrate is worthier, Gao or Peng?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「彭廉而毅，高廉而和。」

translations.literal: They replied: "Peng is incorruptible and resolute; Gao is incorruptible and conciliatory."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Peng is honest and firm; Gao is honest and gentle."

sentences.zh: 上稱善，擢順天府南路同知。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and promoted him to sub-prefect of the southern route in Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and promoted him to sub-prefect of the southern route in Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 於成龍問以捕盜方略​​，條上三事，略言：「盜以旗屯為逋逃藪，請嚴保甲首實之令，使無所匿，而平日能使之衣食粗足，則可不至為盜。」

translations.literal: Yu Chenglong asked him about strategy for capturing bandits; he submitted three points in order, saying in summary: "Bandits take banner colonies as refuges for fugitives. I ask that the order requiring baojia heads to report truthfully be strictly enforced so there is nowhere to hide; and if in ordinary times people can have food and clothing roughly sufficient, they need not become bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chenglong asked him about suppressing banditry. He submitted three proposals, saying in essence, "Bandits use banner colonies as hideouts. Enforce the baojia reporting system so fugitives have nowhere to hide, and in ordinary times see that people have enough food and clothing, and they will not turn to banditry."

sentences.zh: 成龍韙之。

translations.literal: Chenglong approved them.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 會丁父艱歸。

translations.literal: He happened to enter mourning for his father and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered mourning for his father and returned home.

sentences.zh: 成龍總督南河，築界首堤，以屬廕爵。

translations.literal: Chenglong was appointed governor-general of the Southern Rivers and built the Jieshou dike, placing Yinjue in charge of it.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong became governor-general of the Southern Rivers and built the Jieshou dike, putting Yinjue in charge.

sentences.zh: 堤成，上南巡閱工，召見，賜克食。

translations.literal: When the dike was completed the emperor came south on inspection to review the work, summoned him for audience, and granted him a meal.
translations.idiomatic: When the dike was finished the emperor came south to inspect it, received him in audience, and granted him an imperial meal.

sentences.zh: 起復補湖北德安府同知，累擢四川松茂道、直隸口北道，皆有惠政，卒於官。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning, he was appointed sub-prefect of De'an Prefecture in Hubei; he was repeatedly promoted to intendant of Songmao in Sichuan and of Koubei in Zhili, and in each post carried out benevolent policies before dying in office.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he was appointed sub-prefect of De'an in Hubei. He rose through the intendant posts of Songmao in Sichuan and Koubei in Zhili, governing well in each, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子其倬，官至大學士，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Qizhuo rose to Grand Secretary and has a biography of his own.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qizhuo rose to Grand Secretary and has a biography of his own.

sentences.zh: 讓，字益庵，河南尉氏人。

translations.literal: Rang, styled Yi'an, was a native of Weishi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Rang, styled Yi'an, was from Weishi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年進士，授浙江宣平知縣。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kangxi he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed magistrate of Xuanping in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighteenth year of Kangxi and was appointed magistrate of Xuanping in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 旱災，請蠲甚力，巡撫張鵬翮以為賢。

translations.literal: During drought disaster he petitioned vigorously for tax remission, and Governor Zhang Penghe considered him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought he petitioned forcefully for tax relief, and Governor Zhang Penghe judged him an able official.

sentences.zh: 父憂去，服闋，授山西汾西。

translations.literal: He left office on his father's death; when mourning ended he was appointed to Fenxi in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father. When mourning ended he was appointed magistrate of Fenxi in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 會親征漠北，供張杜絕擾累，民力不足，請以正賦辦治。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally campaigned in the northern desert, he cut off all provisioning burdens and harassment; the people's strength was insufficient, so he requested that regular tax revenue be used to manage the arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched north in person, he kept provisioning from burdening the people. Local resources were insufficient, so he asked to cover the costs from regular tax revenue.

sentences.zh: 行取，擢御史，數上疏言察吏安民，實行教養。

translations.literal: Selected for capital service, he was promoted to censor and repeatedly submitted memorials on inspecting officials, securing the people, and carrying out instruction and nurture in earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for service at court, he was promoted to censor and repeatedly memorialized on inspecting officials, securing the people, and earnestly carrying out moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 聖祖諭曰：「朕御極四十年，惟冀天下黎庶盡獲安全，邊疆無事。

translations.literal: The Kangxi Emperor instructed: "I have reigned forty years and only hope that all the common people under Heaven may be fully secure and the frontiers remain untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor said, "I have reigned forty years and only hope that the people may live in security and the frontiers remain at peace.

sentences.zh: 如靳讓所言，必令家給人足，無一人凍餒，此非朕所可必者，恐其不過徒為大言。

translations.literal: As Jin Rang says, one must make every household provided for and every person fed, with not one person cold or hungry—this is not something I can guarantee, and I fear it is nothing but empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: What Jin Rang proposes would require every household to be provided for and no one to go cold or hungry. That is not something I can guarantee, and I fear it is only grand talk.

sentences.zh: 曩者錢鎯、衛既齊亦曾為此言，及後用為大吏，皆不能自踐其語。

translations.literal: In the past Qian Miao and Wei Jiji also spoke in this way, yet after they were later employed as high officials none could live up to their own words.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Miao and Wei Jiji once spoke the same way, yet when they were later appointed to high office none of them lived up to their words.

sentences.zh: 靳讓曾為縣令，其所為能如是乎？

translations.literal: Jin Rang was once a county magistrate—can what he did measure up to this?
translations.idiomatic: Jin Rang was once a county magistrate. Can his record match such claims?

sentences.zh: 通州驛馬事繁，著調為通州知州，果能如所言，朕即超用。」

translations.literal: Tongzhou's relay horses involve heavy business; he is ordered transferred to be prefect of Tongzhou. If he can truly act as he says, I will immediately promote him beyond ordinary measure."
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou's relay horses make for heavy duties. Transfer him there as prefect. If he truly performs as he claims, I will promote him at once."

sentences.zh: 上意欲試之也，許其便宜啟奏。

translations.literal: The emperor's intent was to test him, and he permitted him to report as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to test him and allowed him to report directly as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 讓布衣羸馬之官，皇莊、旗莊恣肆病民，繩以法，不少貸。

translations.literal: Rang went to his post in plain clothes on a lean horse; imperial estates and banner estates ran wild and harmed the people, and he bound them with the law without leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Rang took office in plain clothes on a lean horse. Imperial and banner estates had run wild at the people's expense, and he restrained them by law without mercy.

sentences.zh: 私錢、私鑄悉禁止。

translations.literal: Private coin and private casting were entirely forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Private coinage was banned entirely.

sentences.zh: 時禁河捕魚，誣累平民，讓分別治之。

translations.literal: At the time fishing in the forbidden river led to false charges against common people; Rang distinguished cases and handled them accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Fishing in the forbidden river had led to false charges against commoners. Rang sorted the cases and judged them fairly.

sentences.zh: 奸商藉權貴勢，謀專賣麥豆及設姜肆牟利，並拒絕。

translations.literal: Unscrupulous merchants relied on the power of the privileged to seek monopolies on wheat, beans, and ginger shops for profit, and he refused them all.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants backed by powerful patrons tried to monopolize wheat and beans and set up ginger shops for profit. He refused them all.

sentences.zh: 上聞，皆韙之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of these matters he approved them all.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of these actions he approved them all.

sentences.zh: 會學政更替，命九卿舉所知。

translations.literal: When the education commissioner changed, the emperor ordered the Nine Ministers to recommend men they knew.
translations.idiomatic: When the education commissioner's post fell vacant, the emperor ordered the Nine Ministers to recommend men they knew.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕亦舉一人。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I too will recommend one man."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I too will recommend one man."

sentences.zh: 命以僉事督學廣西。

translations.literal: He ordered him appointed as administrative commissioner to supervise studies in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed him administrative commissioner to supervise education in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 逾年，調浙江，除弊務盡，教士先德行而後文藝。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to Zhejiang; he eliminated abuses to the full and taught scholars to value conduct before literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Zhejiang. He rooted out abuses thoroughly and taught scholars to value character before literary skill.

sentences.zh: 值南巡，召對，褒獎曰：「汝不負朕舉，朕將用汝為巡撫。」

translations.literal: During a southern tour he was summoned for audience; the emperor praised him, saying: "You have not failed my recommendation. I intend to appoint you governor."
translations.idiomatic: During a southern tour he was summoned to audience. The emperor praised him, saying, "You have justified my recommendation. I mean to appoint you governor."

sentences.zh: 讓以母老乞終養，賜御書「天庥堂」額以榮其母。

translations.literal: Rang begged to retire and care for his aged mother to the end; the emperor granted an imperial inscription reading "Hall of Heaven's Blessings" to honor his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Rang asked to retire and care for his aged mother. The emperor granted an imperial plaque reading "Hall of Heaven's Blessings" to honor her.

sentences.zh: 尋母喪，以毀卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward his mother died, and he died from grief-induced debility.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his mother died, and he died from grief.

sentences.zh: 崔華，字蓮生，直隸平山人。

translations.literal: Cui Hua, styled Liansheng, was a native of Pingshan in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hua, styled Liansheng, was from Pingshan in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the sixteenth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the sixteenth year of Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，授浙江開化知縣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Kaihua in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Kaihua in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 政務寬平，建塾校藝，士爭鄉學。

translations.literal: His administration was lenient and even-handed; he established schools to examine talent, and scholars competed to enter village learning.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was lenient and fair. He founded schools to cultivate talent, and scholars flocked to village learning.

sentences.zh: 縣舊有里總，主賦稅，橫派滋擾，除之。

translations.literal: The county had formerly had district heads in charge of tax collection whose arbitrary levies caused increasing harassment; he abolished them.
translations.idiomatic: The county had district tax heads whose arbitrary levies harassed the people. He abolished the office.

sentences.zh: 又以虛糧為累，請豁於上官，未竟其事。

translations.literal: He also petitioned his superiors for remission of phantom grain quotas that burdened the people, but did not live to finish the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned his superiors to remit phantom grain quotas that burdened the county, but did not live to finish the matter.

sentences.zh: 十三年，耿籓亂作，縣南墾戶多閩人，豎旗以應，城守千總吳正通賊，陷城，露刃相逼。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Prince of Jing's rebellion broke out; many of the reclaimed settlers south of the county were Fujianese who raised banners in response. The garrison thousand-commander Wu Zheng colluded with the rebels, the city fell, and blades were bared to force submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Prince of Jing rebelled. Many reclaimed settlers south of the county were Fujianese who raised rebel banners. Garrison commander Wu Zheng joined the rebels, the city fell, and blades were drawn against Hua.

sentences.zh: 華從間道出，檄召十六都義勇鄭大來、夏祚等，涕泣開諭，立聚萬人，躬冒矢石，閱五日，城遂復。

translations.literal: Hua escaped by a hidden route, issued proclamations summoning the volunteer militia of the sixteen districts—Zheng Dalai, Xia Zuo, and others—and with tears explained the situation; ten thousand men gathered at once. He personally braved arrows and stones, and after five days the city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Hua slipped out by a hidden route and summoned the militia of sixteen districts—Zheng Dalai, Xia Zuo, and others. Weeping, he rallied them, and ten thousand men gathered at once. He personally braved arrows and stones, and after five days the city was retaken.

sentences.zh: 總督李之芳上其事，詔嘉之。

translations.literal: Governor-General Li Zhifang reported the affair, and an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Li Zhifang reported the feat, and the court issued an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 時閩寇方熾，分三路犯浙。

translations.literal: At that time Fujian rebels were flourishing and invaded Zhejiang in three columns.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian rebels were then at their height and invaded Zhejiang in three columns.

sentences.zh: 衢州當中路之衝，縣城再陷，慘掠尤甚，民無叛志。

translations.literal: Quzhou lay in the path of the central column; the county seat fell twice and suffered especially savage plunder, yet the people showed no inclination to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Quzhou lay in the path of the central column. The county seat fell twice and suffered especially brutal looting, yet the people never wavered.

sentences.zh: 華率兵退保遂安，圖恢復，時出有所擒斬。

translations.literal: Hua led troops in retreat to hold Su'an and planned recovery, sallying forth from time to time to capture and execute enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Hua withdrew with his troops to Su'an and planned the recovery, sallying out from time to time to capture and kill enemy fighters.

sentences.zh: 大兵扼衢州，久與賊持。

translations.literal: Imperial forces held Quzhou and remained locked in stalemate with the rebels for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial forces held Quzhou and remained locked in stalemate with the rebels for a long time.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，始遣將由遂安復開化，至秋，大破賊軍。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year generals were first dispatched from Su'an to recover Kaihua; by autumn the rebel army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifteenth year imperial generals marched from Su'an to retake Kaihua. By autumn the rebel army was routed.

sentences.zh: 浙境漸清，流亡初集，積逋尤多。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang region gradually cleared; refugees were just beginning to return, and accumulated arrears were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang gradually quieted. Refugees were just returning, and tax arrears had piled up.

sentences.zh: 華圖上遺黎困苦狀，乞為請命，盡蠲十三年至十六年額賦。

translations.literal: Hua mapped and submitted the distressed condition of the surviving populace, begged to petition on their behalf, and obtained full remission of assessed taxes from the thirteenth through the sixteenth years.
translations.idiomatic: Hua documented the plight of the survivors and petitioned on their behalf for full remission of assessed taxes from the thirteenth through the sixteenth years.

sentences.zh: 贖民之流徙者，俾得完聚。

translations.literal: He ransomed people who had been displaced so they could reunite with their families.
translations.idiomatic: He ransomed displaced people so families could reunite.

sentences.zh: 疫癘盛行，廣施藥餌，全活無算。

translations.literal: Epidemic disease was widespread; he broadly dispensed medicines and saved countless lives.
translations.idiomatic: Epidemic disease was rampant. He distributed medicine widely and saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 先後論功，十九年，擢江南揚州知府。

translations.literal: Merit was assessed on several occasions; in the nineteenth year he was promoted to prefect of Yangzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: For his repeated service he was promoted in the nineteenth year to prefect of Yangzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 值湖、河並漲，屬縣被災者眾，華加意撫卹。

translations.literal: When lakes and rivers rose together, many subordinate counties suffered disaster, and Hua gave special care to relief and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: When lakes and rivers flooded together, many subordinate counties were stricken. Hua gave special attention to relief.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，命九卿舉中外清廉之吏，廷推七人，外吏居其三，華為首焉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the emperor ordered the Nine Ministers to recommend incorrupt officials within and without the capital; the court nominated seven men, three of them provincial officials, with Hua first among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the emperor ordered the Nine Ministers to recommend incorrupt officials throughout the empire. The court nominated seven men, three of them provincial officials, with Hua first.

sentences.zh: 擢署兩淮鹽運使，軍興商困，乃權宜變通，令先行鹽、後納課，務與休息，商力甦而賦亦無缺。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting salt transport commissioner of the Two Huai regions; with war arising merchants were distressed, so he made flexible expedients, ordering salt to be delivered first and tax paid afterward, striving to give them rest. Merchant strength revived and tax revenue was not lacking.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting salt transport commissioner of the Two Huai. War had strained the merchants, so he adopted a flexible policy: salt could be delivered first and tax paid later. The trade recovered and revenue did not fall short.

sentences.zh: 先是湖南諸府因兵蠲引三十九萬有奇，至是有請補行蠲引者。

translations.literal: Previously the prefectures of Hunan had been granted exemption of 390,000-odd salt certificates on account of war; at this time there was a request to make up and implement those exempted certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Hunan's prefectures had been granted exemption of more than 390,000 salt certificates because of the war. Now there was a proposal to make up those exempted certificates.

sentences.zh: 華以兩淮浮課重，又帶加斤，若補蠲引，必致額售者滯銷誤課，力言不便，事得寢。
