translations.literal: Hua argued that the Two Huai regions already bore heavy surcharges and additional weight levies; if exempted certificates were made up, quota sellers would surely suffer stagnant sales and missed tax payments. He strongly declared the plan inconvenient, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Hua argued that the Two Huai already faced heavy surcharges and extra weight levies. Making up the exempted certificates would force quota holders to oversell and miss tax targets. He protested forcefully, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，遷甘肅莊涼道，未行，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was transferred to the Zhuangliang circuit in Gansu; before he could depart he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was transferred to the Zhuangliang circuit in Gansu, but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 淮商祠祀之。

translations.literal: Huai merchants enshrined and sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai salt merchants built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 周中鋐，字子振，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhonghong, styled Zizhen, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhonghong, styled Zizhen, was from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙中為江南崇明縣丞。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign he served as assistant magistrate of Chongming in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he served as assistant magistrate of Chongming in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 崇明故重鎮，兵籍千人，欲預取軍食於官，不獲，彀刃譁噪。

translations.literal: Chongming was formerly an important garrison town with a thousand men on the military rolls; they wished to draw rations from the government in advance, were refused, and drew blades in an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Chongming was an important garrison with a thousand men on the rolls. They demanded rations in advance from the government, were refused, and drew blades in a riot.

sentences.zh: 官吏咸避匿，中鋐獨挺身前，宣布順逆利害，感切聳動，眾皆投械散。

translations.literal: Officials all avoided and hid; Zhonghong alone stepped forward in person, proclaiming the benefits and harms of loyalty and rebellion, moving them deeply and stirring them; the crowd all cast down weapons and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: While other officials fled and hid, Zhonghong alone stepped forward, explaining the consequences of loyalty and rebellion with such force that the soldiers were deeply moved and laid down their weapons.

sentences.zh: 擢華亭知縣，民有被誣殺人久繫獄，中鋐立出之，而坐其實殺人者。

translations.literal: Promoted to magistrate of Huating, there was a commoner falsely accused of murder long imprisoned; Zhonghong immediately released him and punished the one who had actually committed murder.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to magistrate of Huating, he immediately freed a man who had long been jailed on a false murder charge and punished the real killer.

sentences.zh: 提標兵庇盜，前令莫敢問，中鋐捕治置諸法，境內乂安。

translations.literal: Provincial garrison troops sheltered robbers; previous magistrates none dared investigate; Zhonghong captured and punished them according to law, and within the territory there was order and peace.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial troops had been shielding bandits, and previous magistrates dared not intervene. Zhonghong arrested and punished them by law, and the district was restored to order.

sentences.zh: 四十三年秋，大霪雨以風，海水驟溢，漂數縣。

translations.literal: In autumn of the forty-third year, great torrential rain with wind; seawater suddenly overflowed, sweeping away several counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the forty-third year (1704), violent wind and rain drove the sea over its banks and flooded several counties.

sentences.zh: 乃具衣糗棺槥救卹之，又為請賑蠲租，活民甚眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon he prepared clothing, dried grain, coffins, and coffin boards for rescue and relief; further he petitioned for famine relief and rent remission, saving very many people.
translations.idiomatic: He supplied clothing, food, coffins, and burial goods for the victims, petitioned for relief and tax remissions, and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，以催科不及格罷，縣民萬數遮言，上官聞於朝，得復職。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, because tax collection failed to meet quota he was dismissed; tens of thousands of county people blocked the road to speak; superiors reported to court, and he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongzheng (1726) he was dismissed for failing to meet tax collection quotas. Tens of thousands of residents blocked his departure to plead his case, and after superiors reported to the throne he was reinstated.

sentences.zh: 時左都御史硃軾被命修海塘，知中鋐賢，悉以事付之。

translations.literal: At the time Left Censor-in-Chief Zhu Shi was ordered to repair the sea dikes; knowing Zhonghong was worthy, he entrusted all matters entirely to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Left Censor-in-Chief Zhu Shi was ordered to repair the sea dikes, he recognized Zhonghong's ability and entrusted the entire project to him.

sentences.zh: 塘成，丁母憂，民復籥留，中鋐先已擢松江知府，至是予假治喪，還視府事。

translations.literal: When the dike was completed, he encountered his mother's mourning; the people again locked the gates to detain him; Zhonghong had already been promoted to prefect of Songjiang; at this time he was granted leave to manage the funeral and then returned to oversee prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the dike was finished he went into mourning for his mother. The people again barred the gates to keep him from leaving. Already promoted to prefect of Songjiang, he was granted leave to bury his mother and then resumed his prefectural duties.

sentences.zh: 五年，議濬淞、婁諸水，以中鋐署太倉知州，董其役。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, dredging of the Song, Lou, and other waterways was proposed; Zhonghong was appointed acting prefect of Taicang to supervise the labor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1727) plans were made to dredge the Song, Lou, and other rivers. Zhonghong was appointed acting prefect of Taicang to direct the work.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，築壩於陳家渡，一再潰，與千總陸某晝夜冒險指揮，倉卒覆其舟，既歿而築合。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year, building a dam at Chenjiadu, it collapsed repeatedly; with thousand-commander Lu he day and night braved danger in command; suddenly his boat capsized; after his death the construction joined together.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year (1728), while building a dam at Chenjiadu, the works collapsed twice. He and Thousand-Commander Lu directed operations day and night at personal risk until his boat suddenly capsized. He drowned, but the dam was completed.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太僕寺少卿。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned of his death, he was posthumously granted the rank of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 當中鋐令華亭時，奉賢猶隸境內，後析為縣，中鋐適為知府，至是民懷其澤，奉以為奉賢城隍之神，歲時祈報，著靈異，長洲王芑孫為廟碑紀其事。

translations.literal: When Zhonghong was magistrate of Huating, Fengxian was still subordinate within his jurisdiction; later it was separated as a county; Zhonghong happened to be prefect; at this time the people cherished his beneficence and honored him as the city-god of Fengxian, praying and offering thanks at seasons; miraculous signs appeared; Changzhou's Wang Qisun wrote a temple stele recording the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhonghong was magistrate of Huating, Fengxian was still part of his jurisdiction. Later it became a separate county while he was prefect. Grateful for his benevolence, the people enshrined him as Fengxian's city god, and miracles were reported at the shrine. Wang Qisun of Changzhou wrote a stele commemorating the affair.

sentences.zh: 道光七年，巡撫陶澍复濬吳淞江，疏請立廟江乾。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daoguang, Governor Tao Shu again dredged the Wusong River and memorialized requesting a temple be established on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daoguang (1827), Governor Tao Shu dredged the Wusong River again and petitioned to erect a shrine on its bank.

sentences.zh: 劉棨，字弢子，山東諸城人。

translations.literal: Liu Qi, courtesy name Taozi, was a native of Zhucheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi, styled Taozi, came from Zhucheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi he became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi (1685).

sentences.zh: 三十四年，授湖南長沙知縣，以廉明稱。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was appointed magistrate of Changsha in Hunan, known for integrity and clarity.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year (1695) he was appointed magistrate of Changsha in Hunan and became known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 時訛言裁兵，撫標千人環轅門大噪，棨為開陳大義，預給三月餉，示無裁意，眾乃定。

translations.literal: At the time false rumors spread of troop reductions; a thousand men of the provincial garrison surrounded the yamen gate clamoring loudly; Qi opened and explained the great principle, advance-issuing three months' pay, showing no intent to reduce troops; the crowd then settled.
translations.idiomatic: When rumors spread that troops would be cut, a thousand provincial soldiers surrounded the yamen gate in uproar. Qi explained the situation, paid three months' rations in advance to show there would be no reductions, and the men were calmed.

sentences.zh: 總督吳琠以循良薦之。

translations.literal: Governor-General Wu Kan recommended him as an upright official.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Wu Kan recommended him as a model local official.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，擢陝西寧羌知州。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was promoted to prefect of Ningqiang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year (1698) he was promoted to prefect of Ningqiang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 關中大饑，漢南尤甚。

translations.literal: Within the passes there was great famine; south of the Han it was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: A great famine struck Guanzhong, and the region south of the Han suffered most severely.

sentences.zh: 州無宿儲，介萬山中，艱於輓運。

translations.literal: The prefecture had no stored reserves, situated among myriad mountains, difficult for transport and hauling.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had no grain reserves and lay deep in the mountains, making transport extremely difficult.

sentences.zh: 棨請貸鄰邑倉粟，約民能負一斗至者予三升，不十日輓三千石。

translations.literal: Qi requested to borrow grain from neighboring counties' granaries, agreeing that commoners who could carry one dou there would receive three sheng; within ten days three thousand shi were hauled.
translations.idiomatic: Qi borrowed grain from neighboring counties' granaries and promised three sheng of grain to anyone who carried one dou over the mountains. Within ten days three thousand shi were delivered.

sentences.zh: 大吏下其法賑他邑，咸稱便。

translations.literal: High officials issued his method down to relieve other districts; all praised its convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Superior officials adopted his method for famine relief elsewhere, and it was widely praised as effective.

sentences.zh: 又奉檄賑洋縣，移粟沿漢而下。

translations.literal: Also by order he relieved Yang County, moving grain down along the Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to relieve Yang County, shipping grain down the Han River.

sentences.zh: 棨先遍歷審勘，剋期給發，數日而畢。

translations.literal: Qi first toured everywhere investigating and surveying, fixed a date for distribution, and within several days finished.
translations.idiomatic: Qi first surveyed the entire area, set a fixed date for distribution, and completed the relief within days.

sentences.zh: 謂洋令曰：「此粟貸之官，倘民不能償，吾兩人當代任。」

translations.literal: He said to the Yang County magistrate: "This grain is borrowed from the government; if the people cannot repay, the two of us shall bear responsibility in their place."
translations.idiomatic: He told the Yang County magistrate, "This grain is a loan from the government. If the people cannot repay it, you and I shall answer for it ourselves."

sentences.zh: 比秋大熟，洋縣民相勉還粟，不煩催督。

translations.literal: By autumn the harvest was greatly abundant; Yang County people encouraged one another to return grain, without need for urging and supervision.
translations.idiomatic: When autumn brought a bumper harvest, the people of Yang County repaid the grain willingly without any need for coercion.

sentences.zh: 始寧羌地苦凋瘵，棨為均田額，完逋賦，補棧道，修旅舍。

translations.literal: At first Ningqiang's territory suffered bitter desolation and exhaustion; Qi equalized land quotas, completed arrears in tax, repaired plank roads, and built travel lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Ningqiang had been deeply impoverished. Qi equalized land tax quotas, cleared tax arrears, repaired plank roads, and built roadside inns.

sentences.zh: 安輯招徠，期年而廬舍萃集。

translations.literal: Pacifying and gathering settlers, within a year dwellings gathered and assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Through resettlement and encouragement, within a year houses clustered together again.

sentences.zh: 山多槲葉，民未知蠶，遣人旋鄉里，齎蠶種，募善蠶者教之，人習其利，名所織曰「劉公綢」。

translations.literal: The mountains had many oak leaves; the people did not yet know sericulture; he sent men back to their home districts, carrying silkworm eggs, recruiting skilled sericulturists to teach them; people learned its profit; the cloth they wove was named "Prefect Liu's silk."
translations.idiomatic: The mountains abounded in oak leaves suitable for silkworms, but the people knew nothing of sericulture. He sent men home to fetch silkworm eggs and skilled teachers. Once they learned the trade, the cloth they wove was called "Prefect Liu's silk."

sentences.zh: 士苦無書，為召賈列肆，分購經籍，建義塾，親為講解。

translations.literal: Scholars suffered from lack of books; he summoned merchants to set up shops, separately purchasing classics and records, built charity schools, and personally lectured and explained.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars lacked books, so he invited merchants to open shops and buy classics for them. He founded charity schools and lectured there himself.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，擢甘肅寧夏中路同知，未赴，母憂去。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was promoted to sub-prefect of the Middle Circuit of Ningxia in Gansu; before departing, his mother's mourning took him away.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year (1702) he was promoted to sub-prefect of the Middle Circuit of Ningxia in Gansu, but went home in mourning for his mother before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 以代民完賦，負累不能行，囑弟代售遺產，不足，弟並以己產易金償負。

translations.literal: Because he had paid taxes on the people's behalf, burdened with debt he could not travel; he instructed his younger brother to sell inherited property on his behalf; it was insufficient, and his brother also exchanged his own property for gold to repay the debt.
translations.idiomatic: Having paid taxes on behalf of the people, he was so burdened with debt that he could not travel. He asked his brother to sell their inherited property; when that was not enough, his brother sold his own holdings as well to pay the debt.

sentences.zh: 民聞之，爭輸金為助，卻不受。

translations.literal: When the people heard, they competed to contribute gold to assist; he refused and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the people heard of this, they offered money to help, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補長沙府同知。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed sub-prefect of Changsha Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he returned to service as sub-prefect of Changsha Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入覲，奉溫旨，試文藝於乾清門，即日擢山西平陽知府。

translations.literal: Entering audience, he received a warm edict; his literary skill was tested at the Gate of Heavenly Purity; that same day he was promoted to prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience with the emperor he received a gracious edict, was tested on his literary skill at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and was promoted that same day to prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 裁汰陋例，蠲除煩苛，訟牘皆立剖決之。

translations.literal: He cut corrupt customary fees, remitted troublesome exactions, and all legal documents were immediately adjudicated.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished corrupt customary fees, removed burdensome exactions, and decided every case brought before him without delay.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，九卿應詔舉廉能吏，以知府被舉者，惟棨與陳鵬年二人。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, the Nine Ministers responding to an edict recommended incorruptible and capable officials; among prefects recommended, only Qi and Chen Pengnian were two.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year (1709), when the Nine Ministers were ordered to nominate incorrupt and capable officials, only Qi and Chen Pengnian were recommended among prefects.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，擢直隸天津道副使，迎駕淀津，詔許從官恭瞻親灑宸翰。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he was promoted to vice commissioner of Tianjin Circuit in Zhili; meeting the imperial progress at Dianjin, an edict permitted attending officials respectfully to view the Emperor's personally written brushwork.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year (1710) he was promoted to vice commissioner of Tianjin Circuit in Zhili. When he met the emperor at Dianjin, the court allowed attending officials to view the emperor's own calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 棨因奏兄果昔官河間知縣，奉「清廉愛民」之褒，乞賜御書「清愛堂」額，上允之。

translations.literal: Qi thereupon memorialized that his elder brother Guo had formerly served as magistrate of Hejian and received the praise "incorruptible and loving the people," begging to be granted an imperial inscription of "Hall of Pure Love"; the Emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Qi memorialized that his elder brother Guo, former magistrate of Hejian, had been praised as "incorruptible and loving the people," and asked for an imperial plaque reading "Hall of Pure Love." The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 歷江西按察使、四川布政使。

translations.literal: He served successively as judicial commissioner of Jiangxi and financial commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial commissioner of Jiangxi and then as financial commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，上詢九卿，本朝清介大臣數人，求可與倫比者。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year the Emperor inquired of the Nine Ministers about several incorruptible and upright great ministers of this dynasty, seeking those who could be compared with them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year (1716) the emperor asked the Nine Ministers which officials of the dynasty could be ranked with the most incorruptible ministers of the past.

sentences.zh: 九卿舉四人，棨與焉。

translations.literal: The Nine Ministers recommended four men; Qi was among them.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Ministers named four men, Qi among them.

sentences.zh: 駕幸湯泉，又以棨治狀語諸從臣，會廷推巡撫，共薦棨，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the imperial progress visited the hot springs, he again spoke of Qi's administrative record to attending ministers; meeting court nomination for governor, all jointly recommended Qi; the Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: At the hot springs the emperor spoke to his attendants of Qi's record of governance. When governors were being nominated at court, all recommended Qi, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 以四川用兵，未輕調。

translations.literal: Because Sichuan was under military campaigns, he was not lightly transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sichuan was at war, he was not transferred lightly.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year (1718) he died in office.

sentences.zh: 兄果，官山西太原府推官，有聲。

translations.literal: Elder brother Guo served as reviewing officer of Taiyuan Prefecture in Shanxi and had a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Guo served as reviewing officer of Taiyuan Prefecture in Shanxi and won a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 改河間知縣，康熙八年，駕幸河間，問民疾苦，父老陳果治狀，召見褒之。

translations.literal: Transferred to magistrate of Hejian; in the eighth year of Kangxi the imperial progress visited Hejian, inquiring of the people's hardships and sufferings; elders reported Guo's administrative record; summoned for audience he was praised.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to magistrate of Hejian, he was summoned when the Kangxi Emperor visited the county in the eighth year (1669). After elders reported on his governance, the emperor received and praised him.

sentences.zh: 卒，祀名宦。

translations.literal: Upon death he was enshrined among distinguished officials.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was enshrined in the hall of distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: 棨子統勳、孫墉、曾孫鐶之，並為時名臣，自有傳。

translations.literal: Qi's son Tongxun, grandson Yong, and great-grandson Huanzhi all were renowned ministers of the time and have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's son Tongxun, grandson Yong, and great-grandson Huanzhi all became eminent officials and have biographies of their own.

sentences.zh: 陶元淳，字子師，江蘇常熟人。

translations.literal: Tao Yuanchun, courtesy name Zishi, was a native of Changshu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Yuanchun, styled Zishi, came from Changshu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 康熙中舉博學鴻詞，以疾不與試。

translations.literal: During Kangxi he was nominated for the Boxue Hongci special examination; due to illness he did not participate in the test.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he was nominated for the special examination in erudite learning, but illness kept him from taking part.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，成進士，廷對，論西北賦輕而役重，東南役均而賦重，原減浮額之糧，罷無益之費。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he became a metropolitan graduate; at the palace examination he discussed how the northwest had light taxes but heavy corvée, the southeast had even corvée but heavy taxes; he wished to reduce inflated grain quotas and abolish useless expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1688) he passed the metropolitan examination. In the palace debate he argued that the northwest bore light taxes but heavy corvée, while the southeast had even corvée but heavy taxes, and urged reducing inflated grain quotas and abolishing wasteful spending.

sentences.zh: 閱者以其言戇，置二甲。

translations.literal: The examiners, because his words were blunt, placed him in the second class.
translations.idiomatic: The examiners judged his remarks too blunt and ranked him in the second class.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，授廣東昌化知縣，到官，首定賦役，均糧於米，均役於糧。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was appointed magistrate of Changhua in Guangdong; upon reaching office he first fixed tax and corvée, equalizing grain quotas in rice and equalizing corvée in grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year (1694) he was appointed magistrate of Changhua in Guangdong. On taking office he first reformed taxes and corvée, equalizing grain quotas in rice and corvée obligations in grain.

sentences.zh: 裁革雜徵，自坊裡供帳始，相率以力耕為業。

translations.literal: He cut and abolished miscellaneous levies, beginning with neighborhood supply accounts; one after another they took diligent farming as their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished miscellaneous levies, starting with neighborhood supply fees, and the people turned wholeheartedly to farming.

sentences.zh: 縣隸瓊州，與黎為界，舊設土舍，制其出入，吏得因緣為奸，元淳立撤去。

translations.literal: The county was subordinate to Qiongzhou and bordered the Li people; formerly native headmen posts were established to control their coming and going; officials could use the opportunity for corruption; Yuanchun immediately removed them.
translations.idiomatic: The county belonged to Qiongzhou and bordered Li territory. Former headmen had controlled Li movement at the border, giving officials opportunities for abuse. Yuanchun abolished the posts at once.

sentences.zh: 一權量，定法度，黎人便之。

translations.literal: He unified weights and measures and established regulations; the Li people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He standardized weights and measures and fixed regulations, to the great convenience of the Li people.

sentences.zh: 城中居人，舊不滿百家，至此戶口漸蕃。

translations.literal: Residents within the city formerly numbered fewer than a hundred households; by this time households gradually multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: The town had once held fewer than a hundred households; under his rule the population steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 元淳時步行閭里間，週諮疾苦，煦嫗如家人。

translations.literal: Yuanchun often walked on foot among the lanes and neighborhoods, everywhere inquiring into hardships, nurturing warmly like family members.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchun often walked the lanes on foot, asking everywhere about people's hardships and comforting them like family.

sentences.zh: 瓊郡處海外，軍將多驕橫，崖州尤甚。

translations.literal: Qiong Prefecture lay beyond the sea; military officers were mostly arrogant and overbearing; Yazhou was especially so.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong Prefecture lay overseas, and its garrison officers were notoriously arrogant—none more so than at Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 元淳嘗署州事，守備黃鎮中以非刑殺人，游擊餘虎縱不問；

translations.literal: Yuanchun once acted as prefectural administrator; garrison commander Huang Zhenzhong killed a man by illegal torture; battalion commander Yu Hu let it go uninvestigated;
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanchun once served as acting prefect, Garrison Commander Huang Zhenzhong tortured a man to death, and Battalion Commander Yu Hu let the matter pass;

sentences.zh: 且貪，索黎人獻納。

translations.literal: Moreover he was greedy, demanding tribute from the Li people.
translations.idiomatic: He was also corrupt and extorted tribute from the Li people.

sentences.zh: 元淳廉得其狀，列款以上，虎私以金賄之不得，造蜚語揭之。

translations.literal: Yuanchun thoroughly obtained the facts, listing charges and reporting upward; Hu privately tried to bribe him with gold but failed, and fabricated slanderous handbills against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchun investigated thoroughly and submitted a detailed indictment. When Yu Hu tried to bribe him and failed, Hu posted slanderous handbills against him.

sentences.zh: 總督石琳下瓊州總兵會訊，元淳申牘曰：「私揭不應發審，鎮臣不應侵官，必挫執法之氣，灰任事之心。

translations.literal: Governor-General Shi Lin sent the Qiongzhou regional commander to conduct joint inquiry; Yuanchun submitted a document stating: "Private handbills should not be sent for trial; the regional commander should not encroach on civil authority—this would necessarily frustrate the spirit of enforcing law and extinguish the will to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Shi Lin ordered the regional commander to join the inquiry. Yuanchun protested in writing: "Anonymous accusations should not trigger a trial, and a military commander should not encroach on civil authority. This would destroy the will to enforce the law.

sentences.zh: 元淳當棄官以全政體，不能蒲伏武臣，貽州縣羞也。」

translations.literal: Yuanchun ought to abandon office to preserve governmental integrity; he cannot prostrate himself before military officials and bring shame on prefectures and counties."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather resign than preserve official dignity by groveling before a military officer and shaming every magistrate in the land."

sentences.zh: 初鞫是獄，鎮中令甲士百人佩刀入署，元淳據案怒叱曰：「吾奉命治事，守備敢令甲士劫持，是藐國法也。」

translations.literal: At the first hearing of this case, Zhenzhong ordered a hundred armored soldiers with drawn blades to enter the yamen; Yuanchun leaned on the desk and angrily shouted: "I am ordered to conduct affairs—how dare the garrison commander send armed soldiers to coerce me? This is contempt for national law."
translations.idiomatic: At the first hearing Huang ordered a hundred armed soldiers into the yamen. Yuanchun slammed the desk and shouted, "I serve by imperial commission. How dare a garrison commander send armed men to intimidate me? This is contempt for the law of the realm."

sentences.zh: 鎮中氣懾，疾揮去，卒定讞，論罪如律。

translations.literal: Zhenzhong's spirit was cowed; he quickly waved them away; ultimately the verdict was fixed and punishment was according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was cowed and hurried the soldiers away. Yuanchun finally secured a verdict and punishment according to law.

sentences.zh: 崖人為語曰：「雖有餘虎，不敵陶公一怒。」

translations.literal: The people of Yazhou made a saying: "Though there is Yu Hu, he cannot match one burst of anger from Prefect Tao."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yazhou said, "For all Yu Hu's power, he was no match for one burst of Prefect Tao's anger."

sentences.zh: 而總督卒因元淳倔彊，坐不檢驗失實，會赦免。

translations.literal: Yet the governor-general ultimately because Yuanchun was stubborn and unyielding, charged him with failure to verify and loss of truth; he was pardoned when an amnesty occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the governor-general, resenting Yuanchun's stubbornness, convicted him of failing to verify the facts properly. He was spared when an amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 复欲於計典黜之，巡撫蕭永藻初授事，曰：「吾初下車，便劾廉吏，何以率屬？」

translations.literal: Again wishing at the merit evaluation to demote him, Governor Xiao Yongzao, newly assuming office, said: "I have just taken up my post—if I immediately impeach an incorruptible official, how can I lead subordinates?"
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general then tried to demote him at the merit review. The newly appointed Governor Xiao Yongzao objected: "If I impeach an upright official the moment I take office, how can I lead my subordinates?"

sentences.zh: 為言於總督，乃已。

translations.literal: He spoke on his behalf to the governor-general, and the matter then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke to the governor-general on Yuanchun's behalf, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 元淳自奉儉約，在官惟日供韭一束。

translations.literal: Yuanchun maintained himself frugally; in office he had only one bundle of chives supplied daily.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchun lived frugally; in office his daily fare was a single bundle of chives.

sentences.zh: 喜接諸生，講論至夜分不倦。

translations.literal: He delighted in receiving scholars, lecturing and discussing until midnight without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed receiving scholars and would lecture with them until midnight without tiring.

sentences.zh: 屢乞病未果，竟以勞卒於官。

translations.literal: Repeatedly begging leave for illness without success, he ultimately died in office from overwork.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated requests for sick leave were denied, and he eventually died in office from overwork.

sentences.zh: 昌化額田四百餘頃，半淪於海，賦不及二千，浮糧居三之一，民重困。

translations.literal: Changhua's registered fields numbered more than four hundred qing; half had been lost to the sea; tax revenue did not reach two thousand; phantom grain quotas accounted for one-third; the people were heavily distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Changhua had more than four hundred qing of registered fields, half lost to the sea. Tax revenue fell below two thousand, with phantom grain quotas making up a third of the burden. The people were sorely afflicted.

sentences.zh: 元淳為浮糧考，屢請於上官，乞豁除，無應者。

translations.literal: Yuanchun compiled a study of phantom grain quotas, repeatedly petitioning superiors begging for exemption; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchun compiled a study of phantom grain quotas and repeatedly petitioned for their remission, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，元淳子正靖官御史，疏以入告，竟獲俞旨免焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong, Yuanchun's son Zhengjing served as censor; he memorialized reporting it upward; ultimately he obtained an approving edict and exemption was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianlong (1738), Yuanchun's son Zhengjing, then a censor, memorialized the throne, and the phantom quotas were at last remitted by imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 廖冀亨，字瀛海，福建永定人。

translations.literal: Liao Jiheng, courtesy name Yinghai, was a native of Yongding in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Jiheng, styled Yinghai, came from Yongding in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十九年舉人，四十七年，授江蘇吳縣知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi he became a provincial graduate; in the forty-seventh year he was appointed magistrate of Wu County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi (1690) and was appointed magistrate of Wu County in Jiangsu in the forty-seventh year (1708).

sentences.zh: 值歲旱，留漕賑饑，不足，自貸金易米以濟。

translations.literal: Encountering drought that year, he retained grain transport for famine relief; it was insufficient, and he personally borrowed gold to exchange for rice to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought he diverted transport grain for famine relief. When that proved insufficient, he borrowed money himself to buy rice for the hungry.

sentences.zh: 士人感其誠，相率捐助，賑以無乏。

translations.literal: Scholars were moved by his sincerity and one after another contributed donations; relief thus lacked nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his sincerity, local scholars donated in turn, and relief supplies never ran short.

sentences.zh: 吳中賦額甲天下，縣尤重，冀亨減火耗，用滾單，民皆稱便。

translations.literal: Tax quotas in Wu were foremost under Heaven; the county was especially heavy; Jiheng reduced melt-and-cast surcharges and used rolling registers; the people all praised the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Tax quotas in the Wu region were the heaviest in the empire, and Wu County bore an especially large share. Jiheng reduced melt-loss surcharges and introduced rolling tax registers, which the people found greatly convenient.

sentences.zh: 知收漕弊多，拘不法者重治之，凡留難、勒索、蹋斛、淋尖、高颺、重篩諸害，埽除一清。

translations.literal: Knowing that collecting transport grain had many abuses, he detained lawbreakers and punished them severely; all harms such as detention, extortion, treading the measure, heaping above the rim, high winnowing, and repeated sifting were swept away completely.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the many abuses in grain collection, he severely punished offenders and swept away every malpractice—from detention and extortion to treading measures, heaping grain above the rim, fraudulent winnowing, and repeated sifting.

sentences.zh: 太湖中有蘆洲，或墾成田，或種蓮養魚，官吏輒假清丈增糧名以自利。

translations.literal: In Lake Tai there were reed islets; some were reclaimed as fields, some used for lotus planting and fish raising; officials often used the pretext of land survey and increased grain quotas for personal profit.
translations.idiomatic: Reed islets in Lake Tai were sometimes reclaimed as fields or used for lotus and fish farming. Officials habitually used land surveys as a pretext to increase grain quotas for their own profit.

sentences.zh: 冀亨曰：「湖蕩偶爾成田，未可久持，今增其賦，朝廷所得幾何，而民累無盡期。」

translations.literal: Jiheng said: "Lake marshes occasionally become fields but cannot long be maintained; now increasing their tax—how much does the court obtain, while the people's burden has no end?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiheng said, "Marshland that happens to become fields cannot be maintained forever. Increasing its tax yields the court little, while the people's burden knows no end."

sentences.zh: 一無所問。

translations.literal: He made no inquiry into any of it.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored the matter entirely.

sentences.zh: 初，冀亨蒞任時，有吳人語之曰：「吳俗健訟，然其人兩粥一飯，肢體薄弱，凡訟宜少準、速決，更加二字曰'從寬'。」

translations.literal: At first, when Jiheng took office, a Wu native told him: "Wu custom is keen on litigation, yet its people eat two gruels and one meal; their bodies are frail; all lawsuits should have fewer standards, swift decisions, with two additional words: 'with leniency.'"
translations.idiomatic: When Jiheng first took office, a local man told him, "Suzhou people love to sue, but they eat sparingly and are physically frail. Hear cases sparingly, decide them quickly, and add two words: 'with leniency.'"

sentences.zh: 冀亨悚然受之。

translations.literal: Jiheng received it with awe.
translations.idiomatic: Jiheng took the advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 收詞不立定期，民隱悉達。

translations.literal: He accepted petitions without fixed schedules; the people's hidden grievances all reached him.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted petitions without fixed office hours, so every hidden grievance reached him.

sentences.zh: 嘗自謂訟貴聽，聽之明，乃能速決而無冤抑。

translations.literal: He once said to himself that litigation values listening; listening clearly enables swift decisions without wrongful suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He often said that the key to litigation was listening carefully—only clear hearing could bring swift and just decisions.

sentences.zh: 在吳三年，非奸盜巨猾，行杖無過二十，蓋守此六字箴也。

translations.literal: During three years in Wu, except for treacherous robbers and great rascals, beatings never exceeded twenty strokes—he guarded this six-character maxim.
translations.idiomatic: In three years at Wu County he never ordered more than twenty strokes of the bastinado except for major criminals—a rule he kept by that six-word maxim.

sentences.zh: 有庠生授徒鹽商家，自刎死，勘得實。

translations.literal: There was a licentiate teaching pupils in a salt merchant's household who cut his own throat and died; investigation established the facts.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate who taught in a salt merchant's household cut his own throat. Investigation confirmed suicide.

sentences.zh: 或有謗其受賄者，冀亨無所避，卒釋鹽商勿罪。

translations.literal: Some slandered him as having taken bribes; Jiheng did not avoid it; ultimately he released the salt merchant without punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Some accused him of taking bribes, but Jiheng did not shrink from the case and ultimately released the merchant without charge.

sentences.zh: 東山巡檢報鄉人弒父屠嫂，未遂，自盡。

translations.literal: The Dongshan sub-prefect reported that a village man had murdered his father and slaughtered his sister-in-law, failed in the attempt, and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Dongshan sub-prefect reported that a villager had tried to murder his father and sister-in-law, failed, and then killed himself.

sentences.zh: 冀亨方秉二燭閱其詞，燭無風齊滅，知有冤。

translations.literal: Jiheng was just holding two candles reading the petition when the candles without wind all extinguished together; he knew there was injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Jiheng was reading the report by candlelight when both candles went out simultaneously though there was no wind. He knew an injustice was involved.

sentences.zh: 克日渡湖往驗，大風，舟幾覆，從者色變。

translations.literal: On the appointed day he crossed the lake to inspect on site; great wind, the boat nearly capsized; attendants' faces changed color.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day he crossed the lake to investigate in person. A gale nearly capsized the boat, and his attendants turned pale.

sentences.zh: 冀亨曰：「縣官伸冤理枉而來，神必佑之，何懼！」

translations.literal: Jiheng said: "The county magistrate comes to redress wrongs and rectify injustice—the spirits will surely protect him; what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiheng said, "I come as magistrate to right a wrong—the spirits will protect me. Why fear?"

sentences.zh: 須臾抵岸。

translations.literal: In a moment they reached shore.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later they reached the shore.

sentences.zh: 訊得父故殺狀，巡檢得賄誣報，俱論如律。

translations.literal: Interrogation established that the father had died by suicide; the sub-prefect had taken bribes and falsely reported; all were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Questioning established that the father had killed himself and that the sub-prefect had taken bribes to frame the case. All were punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 冀亨既有聲於吳，他縣疑獄，往往令推治。

translations.literal: Jiheng already had a reputation in Wu; doubtful cases in other counties were often assigned to him for investigation and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Already renowned in Wu, Jiheng was often assigned to investigate doubtful cases in other counties.

sentences.zh: 會有宜興知縣誣揭典史故勘平民為盜，刑夾致死，冀亨奉檄按驗。

translations.literal: It happened that the Yixing magistrate falsely accused the clerk of deliberately torturing a commoner as a robber until he died under the leg-press; Jiheng received orders to investigate on site.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yixing magistrate falsely accused a clerk of torturing an innocent man to death on a robbery charge, Jiheng was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 知縣者總督噶禮之私人也，或告宜少假借，冀亨不為動。

translations.literal: The magistrate was a personal follower of Governor-General Gali; some advised that he should show a little leniency; Jiheng was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate was a protégé of Governor-General Gali, and some advised Jiheng to show leniency, but he would not be swayed.

sentences.zh: 檢踝骨無傷，原揭皆誣。

translations.literal: Examining the ankle bones found no injury; the original accusation was all false.
translations.idiomatic: Examination of the ankle bones showed no injury, proving the original accusation entirely false.

sentences.zh: 獄上，噶禮屢駁詰。

translations.literal: When the case was submitted upward, Gali repeatedly rejected and questioned it.
translations.idiomatic: When the case went up, Gali repeatedly rejected and challenged the findings.

sentences.zh: 再三審，卒如冀亨議，以是忤總督。

translations.literal: After repeated review, the outcome finally accorded with Jiheng's opinion; thereby he offended the governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated review the verdict finally matched Jiheng's findings, and he thereby offended the governor-general.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫張伯行以清廉著，深契冀亨，布政使陳鵬年尤重之；

translations.literal: At the time Governor Zhang Boxing was known for integrity and was deeply in accord with Jiheng; Financial Commissioner Chen Pengnian especially valued him;
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Boxing, renowned for integrity, was deeply allied with Jiheng, and Financial Commissioner Chen Pengnian especially valued him;

sentences.zh: 而噶禮不懌於伯行，尤惡鵬年。

translations.literal: Yet Gali was displeased with Boxing and especially hated Pengnian.
translations.idiomatic: but Gali disliked Zhang Boxing and especially hated Chen Pengnian.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，鵬年被劾，並及冀亨，以虧帑奪職。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year Pengnian was impeached, and Jiheng was implicated as well; for treasury deficit he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year Chen Pengnian was impeached, and Jiheng was implicated and dismissed on charges of treasury deficit.

sentences.zh: 逾年，噶禮敗，冀亨始復原官，以病不赴選。

translations.literal: After a year Gali fell from power; Jiheng was then restored to his original office, but due to illness he did not attend selection.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, after Gali's downfall, Jiheng was restored to office but did not return to service because of illness.

sentences.zh: 及卒，吳人祀之百花書院。

translations.literal: Upon his death, the people of Wu enshrined him at the Baihua Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the people of Wu enshrined him at the Baihua Academy.

sentences.zh: 冀亨歿後​​，家留於吳，入籍嘉定。

translations.literal: After Jiheng's death his family remained in Wu and registered domicile in Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiheng's death his family remained in Wu and took household registration in Jiading.

sentences.zh: 曾孫文錦，嘉慶十六年進士，由翰林出為河南衛輝知府，有惠政，祀名宦。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Wenjin, metropolitan graduate in the sixteenth year of Jiaqing, from the Hanlin Academy became prefect of Weihui in Henan, had benevolent policies, and was enshrined among distinguished officials.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Wenjin passed the metropolitan examination in the sixteenth year of Jiaqing, served as prefect of Weihui in Henan after leaving the Hanlin Academy, governed benevolently, and was enshrined among distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: 文錦子惟勳，道光十三年進士，亦由翰林為貴州鎮遠知府，撫苗有法，終貴陽府。

translations.literal: Wenjin's son Weixun, metropolitan graduate in the thirteenth year of Daoguang, also from the Hanlin Academy became prefect of Zhenyuan in Guizhou, pacified the Miao with proper methods, and ended as prefect of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin's son Weixun passed the metropolitan examination in the thirteenth year of Daoguang, served as prefect of Zhenyuan in Guizhou after leaving the Hanlin Academy, governed the Miao effectively, and later served as prefect of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 佟國瓏，字信侯，奉天人，隸漢軍籍。

translations.literal: Tong Guolong, courtesy name Xinhou, was a native of Fengtian, registered in the Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guolong, styled Xinhou, came from Fengtian and was registered in a Han Banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十年，由筆帖式授山東文登知縣。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Kangxi, from clerk-translator he was appointed magistrate of Wendeng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Kangxi he rose from clerk-translator to magistrate of Wendeng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 縣俗愚悍，有勸治宜嚴峻者。

translations.literal: County custom was ignorant and fierce; some advised that governance should be stern and severe.
translations.idiomatic: The county people were rough and stubborn, and some advised that he govern with severity.

sentences.zh: 國瓏曰：「為政在誠心愛民，興利除害，化導之而已，嚴峻非民之福也。」

translations.literal: Guolong said: "Governing lies in sincerely loving the people, promoting benefit and removing harm, transforming and guiding them—that is all; severity is not the people's blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Guolong replied, "To govern is to love the people sincerely, promote their welfare, remove harm, and guide them by moral example. Severity is no blessing to the people."

sentences.zh: 副將某以暱妓蝕餉，軍大噪，夜半斬關出屯東郊。

translations.literal: A deputy general, because he favored a prostitute and embezzled rations, caused the army to clamor loudly; at midnight they cut through the gate and encamped in the eastern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: A deputy general had embezzled rations to favor a prostitute, and the troops mutinied, breaking out at midnight to encamp in the eastern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 國瓏聞變，單騎往諭曰：「吾與軍民同疾苦，有冤當訴我，何妄動為？」

translations.literal: Guolong heard of the disturbance, went alone on horseback to instruct them, saying: "I share hardships with soldiers and civilians alike; if there is injustice you should appeal to me—why act rashly?"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the mutiny, Guolong rode out alone and said, "I share your hardships. If you have grievances, bring them to me. Why rebel?"

sentences.zh: 眾猶洶洶，國瓏當砲立，曰：「吾不忍見爾曹族誅，請先試若砲。」

translations.literal: The crowd was still turbulent; Guolong stood before the cannon and said: "I cannot bear to see you all exterminated to the last clan—please try your cannon on me first."
translations.idiomatic: The men were still unruly. Guolong stood before their cannon and said, "I cannot bear to see you all executed. Try your cannon on me first."

sentences.zh: 眾動色，曰：「公廉明，軍何敢犯，然事已至此，奈何？」

translations.literal: The crowd changed expression and said: "Your Honor is incorruptible and clear-sighted—how would the army dare offend? Yet matters have come to this—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Their faces changed. They said, "Your Honor is upright and just—we would never harm you. But things have gone this far. What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 國瓏力任保全。

translations.literal: Guolong forcefully undertook to guarantee their safety.
translations.idiomatic: Guolong pledged personally to protect them.

sentences.zh: 究其故，得實。

translations.literal: Investigating the cause, the facts were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: An investigation confirmed the facts.

sentences.zh: 縛妓扌失之，眾泣拜而散，副將尋被劾去。

translations.literal: He bound the prostitute and flogged her; the crowd wept, bowed, and dispersed; the deputy general was soon impeached and removed.
translations.idiomatic: He bound and flogged the prostitute. The soldiers wept, bowed, and dispersed, and the deputy general was soon impeached and removed.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，奸民騷動，國瓏歷村墟，給賑撫諭，捕治兇渠，民賴以安。

translations.literal: In a famine year wicked commoners stirred unrest; Guolong toured villages and ruins, distributing relief and offering consolation, capturing and punishing ringleaders; the people relied on this for peace.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year unruly elements stirred trouble. Guolong toured the villages distributing relief, capturing ringleaders, and restoring order.

sentences.zh: 邑豪宋某以鄰婦貸錢不償息殺之。

translations.literal: A local bully surnamed Song killed a neighboring woman because she could not repay a loan with interest.
translations.idiomatic: A local bully named Song killed a neighbor because she could not repay a loan with interest.

sentences.zh: 吏役得賂，皆為豪掩，又以千金賄國瓏。

translations.literal: Clerks and runners took bribes and all covered for the bully; they also offered a thousand taels to bribe Guolong.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks took bribes to cover for the bully and offered Guolong a thousand taels in bribes.

sentences.zh: 國瓏怒，覆驗婦有重傷，鞫得其情，置豪於法。

translations.literal: Guolong was angry; re-examination showed the woman had severe injuries; interrogation obtained the facts; he punished the bully according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Guolong was enraged. Re-examination revealed severe injuries on the woman's body, investigation proved the truth, and he punished the bully by law.

sentences.zh: 邑故瀕海，副將林某縛商舶之泊島嶼者數千人，指為寇，國瓏訊釋之，別捕誅真盜四十餘人。

translations.literal: The county bordered the sea; Deputy General Lin bound several thousand merchant vessels anchored at islands and called them pirates; Guolong interrogated and released them, separately capturing and executing more than forty real robbers.
translations.idiomatic: The county bordered the sea. Deputy General Lin had bound thousands of merchants anchored off the islands as pirates. Guolong released them after investigation and separately captured and executed more than forty actual robbers.

sentences.zh: 五十年，擢山西澤州知州。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he was promoted to prefect of Zezhou in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year of Kangxi he was promoted to prefect of Zezhou in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 歲祲，發常平倉以貸民，剋期輸還無爽。

translations.literal: In a bad harvest year he opened the Ever-Normal Granary to lend the people grain; repayment on the fixed date was never missed.
translations.idiomatic: In a bad harvest year he lent grain from the Ever-Normal Granary, and the people repaid on schedule without fail.

sentences.zh: 又減耗羨，革陋規，省徭役，平物價，民情大悅。

translations.literal: Further he reduced melt-loss surcharges, abolished corrupt customs, economized corvée labor, stabilized commodity prices, and the people's sentiment was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced melt-loss surcharges, abolished corrupt practices, eased corvée burdens, stabilized prices, and won the people's deep approval.

sentences.zh: 國瓏嘗以論事忤太原知府某，某嗾人誣揭之，坐罷任。

translations.literal: Guolong once offended a certain Taiyuan prefect in discussing affairs; the prefect instigated someone to falsely accuse him, and he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Guolong once offended the Taiyuan prefect in a policy dispute. The prefect instigated a false accusation and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 州民鳴鐘鼓罷市，欲詣闕。

translations.literal: Prefectural people rang bells and drums and closed the markets, wishing to go to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: The people rang bells and drums, closed the markets, and prepared to petition the throne.

sentences.zh: 既而得白，留原任。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the truth was cleared and he was retained in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon cleared and restored to his post.

sentences.zh: 時平陽民變，巡撫檄國瓏以兵往，國瓏曰：「是速之亂也。」

translations.literal: At the time the people of Pingyang mutinied; the governor ordered Guolong to go with troops; Guolong said: "That would hasten the disorder."
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Pingyang rose in unrest, the governor ordered Guolong to go with troops. Guolong said, "That would only make the disorder worse."

sentences.zh: 單騎馳赴，民皆額手曰：「佟公至，吾屬無慮矣！」

translations.literal: Alone on horseback he galloped there; the people all placed hands on foreheads and said: "Prefect Tong has come—we need have no worry!"
translations.idiomatic: He rode out alone. The people clasped their hands and said, "Prefect Tong is here—we need fear nothing!"

sentences.zh: 乃安堵受撫。

translations.literal: Thereupon they settled peacefully and accepted pacification.
translations.idiomatic: They then settled peacefully and accepted his reassurance.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，以疾乞免。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he begged to be relieved due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year he requested retirement due to illness.

sentences.zh: 後以所屬高平令虧帑被逮，責償萬金，民感其惠，捐金投州庫代償其半云。

translations.literal: Later because the Gaoping magistrate under his jurisdiction had a treasury deficit and was arrested, he was ordered to repay ten thousand taels of gold; the people, moved by his benevolence, donated gold to the prefectural treasury to repay half on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Gaoping magistrate under his jurisdiction was arrested for a treasury deficit, Guolong was ordered to repay ten thousand taels. Grateful for his benevolence, the people donated half the sum to the prefectural treasury on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 陸師，字麟度，浙江歸安人。

translations.literal: Lu Shi, courtesy name Lindu, was a native of Gui'an in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shi, styled Lindu, came from Gui'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少負文名。

translations.literal: In youth he bore a literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He won a literary reputation in youth.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十年進士，授河南新安知縣。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the fortieth year of Kangxi, he was appointed magistrate of Xin'an in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fortieth year of Kangxi and was appointed magistrate of Xin'an in Henan.

sentences.zh: 修學校，集諸生治經，童子能應試者免其徭，民興於學。

translations.literal: He repaired schools, gathered scholars to study the classics, exempted boys able to take examinations from corvée, and the people were inspired toward learning.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired schools, gathered scholars to study the classics, exempted boys who could sit examinations from corvée, and the people turned enthusiastically to learning.

sentences.zh: 響馬賊季國玉為患久，捕誅之。

translations.literal: The mounted bandit Ji Guoyu had long been a scourge; he captured and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He captured and executed the mounted bandit Ji Guoyu, who had long terrorized the region.

sentences.zh: 巡鹽使者下縣，取鹽犯四十人。

translations.literal: The salt-inspection commissioner came down to the county and took forty salt offenders.
translations.idiomatic: The salt-inspection commissioner came to the county and demanded forty salt offenders.

sentences.zh: 師曰：「律以人鹽並獲始為犯，今勘犯止二人，何濫為？」

translations.literal: Shi said: "The law requires both offender and salt to be seized together before it counts as a violation—now investigation finds only two offenders; why expand it arbitrarily?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "The law requires both offender and contraband salt to be seized together. Investigation finds only two offenders. Why expand the case arbitrarily?"

sentences.zh: 父憂歸，在途，有六七騎挾弓矢，驅牛車，載婦女三十餘人，言歸德饑民，某將軍買以歸者也。

translations.literal: Returning home for his father's mourning, on the road there were six or seven horsemen with bows and arrows driving an ox cart carrying more than thirty women, saying they were famine refugees from Guide whom a certain general had bought to take home.
translations.idiomatic: On his way home for his father's mourning he encountered six or seven horsemen with bows driving an ox cart loaded with more than thirty women, said to be famine refugees from Guide whom a general had bought.

sentences.zh: 師叱止之，令官還婦女於其家，白將軍收其騎卒。

translations.literal: Shi shouted to stop them, ordered officials to return the women to their homes, and reported to the general to take custody of his mounted followers.
translations.idiomatic: Shi ordered them halted, had the women returned to their families, and reported to the general to take custody of his men.

sentences.zh: 或謂已去官胡忤將軍，師曰：「知縣一日未出境，忍以饑民婦女媚將軍耶？」

translations.literal: Some said he had already left office—why offend the general? Shi said: "A magistrate who has not left the border for one day—how can he bear to fawn on a general with famine refugees' women?"
translations.idiomatic: Some asked why he offended a general after leaving office. Shi replied, "Until a magistrate has crossed the border, how can he endure handing famine refugees' women to a general as a gift?"

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark.
translations.idiomatic: End of quoted passage.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補江蘇儀徵。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed to Yizheng in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was assigned to Yizheng in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 有盜引良民為黨，師親馳往捕，見壞器滿地，言有暴客食此不償值，因而鬥毀。

translations.literal: Robbers had implicated upright commoners as accomplices; Shi personally galloped to capture them, saw broken vessels all over the ground, and was told that violent guests had eaten without paying and therefore fought and destroyed things.
translations.idiomatic: When robbers implicated innocent men as accomplices, Shi rode out personally to investigate. He found broken vessels everywhere and learned that unruly guests had eaten without paying and started a brawl.

sentences.zh: 詰其人，狀與盜肖，事得白。

translations.literal: Questioning those persons, their account matched the robbers'; the matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Questioning the accused, their account matched the robbers' story, and the innocent were cleared.

sentences.zh: 春徵，勸富戶先輸，秋則減其耗，令自封投櫃。

translations.literal: For spring collection he urged wealthy households to pay first; in autumn he reduced their melt-loss surcharge and ordered them to seal and deposit payments themselves.
translations.idiomatic: For spring tax collection he urged wealthy households to pay first, then reduced their melt-loss surcharge in autumn and let them seal and deposit payments themselves.

sentences.zh: 故事，驛夫臨時取給鋪戶，倉猝滋擾。

translations.literal: By precedent relay runners took supplies on the spot from shop households, causing sudden disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: By custom relay runners requisitioned supplies on the spot from shopkeepers, causing sudden harassment.

sentences.zh: 一切禁革，但令戶日賦一錢歸驛，商賈以安。

translations.literal: He abolished all of this, only ordering each household to pay one cash daily to the relay station; merchants and traders thereby had peace.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the practice entirely and required only a daily cash payment per household to the relay station, to the great relief of merchants.

sentences.zh: 揚州五縣飢，大吏令縣各以五千金糴穀備賑，具舟車往，則虛而歸。

translations.literal: Five counties around Yangzhou suffered famine; high officials ordered each county to use five thousand taels of gold to buy grain for relief preparation; they prepared boats and carts to go, but returned empty-handed.
translations.idiomatic: When five counties around Yangzhou faced famine, superior officials ordered each county to spend five thousand taels buying relief grain. Counties sent boats and carts but returned empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 師察知府意欲縣官借補所虧也，力爭，於是五縣皆得穀以賑。

translations.literal: Shi perceived the prefect intended county officials to borrow funds to cover deficits; he forcefully contested it, and thus all five counties obtained grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Shi saw that the prefect intended county officials to cover shortfalls from their own funds and fought the order. All five counties then obtained grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 卻鹽商例餽，固請，乃籍其入以修學宮，具祭器樂舞，浚泮池，植桃李其上。

translations.literal: He refused the salt merchants' customary gifts; when they pressed him he registered the income to repair the Confucian temple, provided sacrificial vessels and musical instruments, dredged the ceremonial pool, and planted peach and plum trees upon it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the salt merchants' customary gifts, but when they insisted he recorded the money for repairing the Confucian temple, furnishing sacrificial vessels and musical instruments, dredging the ceremonial pool, and planting peach and plum trees around it.

sentences.zh: 修宋文天祥祠，又以其餘建倉廒，潔治囹圄。

translations.literal: He repaired the Song dynasty Wen Tianxiang shrine, and with the remainder built granaries and cleaned and maintained the prison.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the shrine to Song loyalist Wen Tianxiang, and used the remainder to build granaries and improve the jail.

sentences.zh: 質庫書票，故有月無日，勿論久近，皆取一月息。

translations.literal: Pawnshop receipts formerly had month but no day; regardless of how long or recent, all took one month's interest.
translations.idiomatic: Pawnshop receipts recorded the month but not the day, so one month's interest was charged regardless of how long the loan had run.

sentences.zh: 師辭其歲餽，令視他縣月讓五日。

translations.literal: Shi refused their annual gifts and ordered that compared with other counties one month should grant five days' leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Shi refused their annual gifts and ordered pawnshops in his county to grant five extra days of grace each month compared with other counties.

sentences.zh: 舊有豬稅，下令蠲除之。

translations.literal: There was formerly a pig tax; he ordered it remitted and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the old pig tax.

sentences.zh: 課最，行取擢吏部主事，升員外郎。

translations.literal: Rated highest in evaluation, selected by special promotion to secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, and elevated to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Rated highest in evaluation, he was selected for promotion to secretary in the Ministry of Personnel and then vice director.

sentences.zh: 掌選，有要人求官，力持不可。

translations.literal: Managing appointments, when an influential man sought an office he forcefully held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: While managing appointments he firmly refused when an influential man sought an office.

sentences.zh: 督山東礦務，條上開採無益，罷其役。

translations.literal: Supervising Shandong mining affairs, he submitted in sequence that mining was without benefit and abolished the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Shandong mining, he memorialized that mining brought no benefit and had the work stopped.

sentences.zh: 還，擢御史，巡河、讞獄皆稱職。

translations.literal: Returning, he was promoted to censor; inspecting rivers and reviewing cases he was all competent.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to censor and distinguished himself inspecting rivers and reviewing cases.

sentences.zh: 康熙六十一年，河督陳鵬年疏請以師為山東兗沂曹道，未到官，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year of Kangxi, River Commissioner Chen Pengnian memorialized requesting Shi as commissioner of the Yan-Yi-Cao Circuit in Shandong; before reaching office he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year of Kangxi River Commissioner Chen Pengnian recommended Shi for commissioner of the Yan-Yi-Cao Circuit in Shandong, but Shi died before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: He was enshrined in the hall of distinguished officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was honored with enshrinement in the hall of distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: 龔鑑，字明水，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Gong Jian, courtesy name Mingshui, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Jian, styled Mingshui, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 早與同郡杭世駿齊名。

translations.literal: Early on he was equally famous in his commandery with Hang Shijun.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he was as renowned in his prefecture as Hang Shijun.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，以拔貢就選籍，授江蘇甘泉知縣。

translations.literal: In the early Yongzheng period, as a selected tribute student entering selection he was appointed magistrate of Ganquan in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yongzheng reign, as a selected tribute graduate he was appointed magistrate of Ganquan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 縣新以江都析置，故脂膏之地，鑑恥為俗吏，一以子惠黎元、振興文教為己任。

translations.literal: The county was newly separated from Jiangdu, thus a rich and fertile place; Jian was ashamed to be a vulgar official and took solely nourishing the common people and reviving culture and education as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: The county had just been carved out of Jiangdu and was a wealthy district. Jian scorned being a conventional official and devoted himself to caring for the people and reviving culture and education.

sentences.zh: 故某侍郎子與有舊，入謁，有所囑，拒之。

translations.literal: A former vice minister's son had old ties with him and came to call, making requests; he refused him.
translations.idiomatic: The son of a former vice minister, an old acquaintance, came to call with requests, but Jian turned him away.

sentences.zh: 有同城官為大吏所暱，令伺察屬吏者，有挾而請，又拒之；

translations.literal: There was a fellow official favored by a high official, assigned to spy on subordinate officials; he came with leverage to request favors, and Jian again refused;
translations.idiomatic: A fellow official favored by a high official, assigned to spy on subordinates, came with leverage seeking favors, and Jian refused again;

sentences.zh: 巨室延飲，又拒之。

translations.literal: Great households invited him to drink; he again refused.
translations.idiomatic: great families invited him to banquets, and he refused again.

sentences.zh: 於是大江南北盛傳甘泉令不近人情，鑑益自刻苦，無一長物。

translations.literal: Thereupon north and south of the Yangzi widely spread the saying that the Ganquan magistrate was unapproachable; Jian became even more self-denying, without a single superfluous possession.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread across the Yangzi region that the magistrate of Ganquan was unapproachable. Jian lived even more frugally, without a single luxury.

sentences.zh: 縣境邵伯埭受高、寶諸湖之水，地卑下。

translations.literal: Within the county the Shaobo Dam received water from the Gaoyou and Baoying lakes; the land was low-lying.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaobo Dam in his county received water from the Gaoyou and Baoying lakes, and the land there was low-lying.

sentences.zh: 鑑謂當於農隙運土築高埂沿堤為防，以徐議溝洫。

translations.literal: Jian said that during agricultural slack seasons earth should be transported to build high embankments along the dike as protection, gradually discussing ditches and canals.
translations.idiomatic: Jian proposed building high embankments along the dikes with earth moved during the agricultural off-season, as a first step toward drainage works.

sentences.zh: 堤上即植桑，興蠶事。

translations.literal: Upon the dikes mulberry would immediately be planted to promote sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberry trees would be planted on the dikes to promote sericulture.

sentences.zh: 其西境地高，浹旬不雨即龜坼，宜每一里為水塘以蓄之。

translations.literal: Its western territory was high; if ten days passed without rain the ground cracked like tortoise shell; it was suitable to make a water pond every li to store it.
translations.idiomatic: The western part of the county was higher; ten days without rain cracked the ground. He proposed a storage pond every li.

sentences.zh: 如是則高下之田俱無患。

translations.literal: Thus high and low fields would both be without trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In this way both low-lying and upland fields would be protected.

sentences.zh: 大吏韙之，然不能行。

translations.literal: High officials approved it, yet it could not be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Superior officials approved the plan, but it was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 邵伯埭下有芒稻河，設閘洩水尤要。

translations.literal: Below the Shaobo Dam was the Mangdao River; setting sluice gates to release water was especially important.
translations.idiomatic: Below the Shaobo Dam lay the Mangdao River, where sluice gates for releasing water were especially critical.

sentences.zh: 值大水氾溢，鑑冒雨至，呼閘官洩之。

translations.literal: Encountering great flood overflow, Jian came through rain and called on the sluice official to release water.
translations.idiomatic: When floods overflowed, Jian came through the rain and ordered the sluice official to release water.

sentences.zh: 閘官以鹽漕為言，不可。

translations.literal: The sluice official spoke of salt transport and grain tribute and said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The sluice official refused, citing salt and tribute transport.

sentences.zh: 會總河嵇曾筠視河至，鑑直陳，厲聲訶閘官，曾筠即令啟閘。

translations.literal: It happened that Grand Canal Director Ji Zengyun came to inspect the river; Jian stated directly, loudly rebuking the sluice official; Zengyun immediately ordered the sluice opened.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Canal Director Ji Zengyun arrived on inspection. Jian stated the case directly and sharply rebuked the sluice official. Zengyun immediately ordered the sluice opened.

sentences.zh: 又用鑑言，定鹽漕船過湖需水不過六尺，過即啟閘，無得藉口蓄水，為民田患。

translations.literal: Also adopting Jian's words, he fixed that salt and tribute boats crossing the lake needed no more than six chi of water; once exceeded the sluice must be opened, not using stored water as a pretext to harm civilian fields.
translations.idiomatic: He also adopted Jian's proposal that salt and tribute boats needed no more than six chi of water to cross the lake, and that the sluice must be opened once that depth was exceeded, so water could not be hoarded to the harm of farmland.

sentences.zh: 每歲晏，江都之鰥寡孤獨多入甘泉部中。

translations.literal: Every year at year's end, Jiangdu's widowers, widows, orphans, and solitaries mostly entered Ganquan's jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Every year at year's end many widows, orphans, and elderly without support from Jiangdu fell under Ganquan's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 西湖聖因寺僧明慧者，恃前在內廷法會恩寵，幹求遍於江、浙。

translations.literal: The monk Minghui of Sheng'in Temple at West Lake, relying on former favor from imperial Buddhist assemblies in the inner court, sought favors everywhere in Jiangsu and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Minghui of West Lake's Sheng'in Temple, relying on favor won at imperial Buddhist assemblies in the inner court, solicited favors across Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 一日以書幣關白，鑑杖其使而遣之。

translations.literal: One day he sent letters and gifts to request favors; Jian beat his messenger with rods and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: One day he sent letters and gifts seeking favors. Jian had his messenger beaten with rods and sent away.

sentences.zh: 事流傳，上聞。

translations.literal: The matter spread and reached the Emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread, and the emperor heard of it.

sentences.zh: 世宗召明慧還京，錮不許出。

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor summoned Minghui back to the capital and confined him, not permitting him to leave.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor summoned Minghui back to the capital and confined him, forbidding him to leave.

sentences.zh: 當是時，甘泉令聲聞天下。

translations.literal: At that time the Ganquan magistrate's reputation resounded throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the magistrate of Ganquan was famed throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 在任六年，以父憂去官，貧，至無以葬。

translations.literal: During six years in office he left office for his father's mourning; he was poor, to the point of having no means for burial.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in office he left for his father's mourning so poor that he could not afford a funeral.

sentences.zh: 河南巡撫尹會一故為揚州守，雅與鑑善，招之，欲使主大樑書院，以修脯助葬。

translations.literal: Henan Governor Yin Huiyi had formerly been prefect of Yangzhou and was on good terms with Jian; he invited him, wishing to have him direct the Daliang Academy, using salary to assist burial.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Governor Yin Huiyi, formerly prefect of Yangzhou and an old friend of Jian, invited him to head the Daliang Academy so that his salary could help pay for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 遂卒於河南。

translations.literal: Thereupon he died in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Henan.

sentences.zh: 鑑湛深經術，能摘先儒之誤，顧書多未成。

translations.literal: Jian was deeply versed in classical learning and could point out errors of earlier Confucians, yet many of his books were not completed.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was deeply learned in the classics and could identify errors in earlier Confucian scholarship, though many of his writings remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 所成者毛詩疏說，闡明李光地之說為多。

translations.literal: What was completed was expository commentary on the Mao version of the Book of Songs, mostly elucidating the doctrines of Li Guangdi.
translations.idiomatic: What he did finish was a commentary on the Mao recension of the Book of Songs, largely developing the views of Li Guangdi.
